papers.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.

papers.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
papers.abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Velázquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.

papers.title: Some variants of function domination
papers.abstract: We investigate whether classical recursion-theoretic notions defined by function domination remain unchanged when success is required only on sets of prescribed asymptotic density. We establish robustness for many such notions and uncover unexpected connections between familiar degree properties by comparing upper and lower density. In contrast, pdomination, as defined by Chong, Hoi, Stephan and Turetsky, is not robust under density weakenings. We also answer a question of Kjos-Hanssen and Nies by characterizing superhighness as domination with a threshold boundedly limit recursive in the oracle. As an application, we introduce supermaximal sets, a strengthening of maximality whose degrees are exactly the superhigh r.e. degrees.

papers.title: Effective Hausdorff dimension one is cofinal in the K-degrees
papers.abstract: Every K-degree has an upper bound of effective Hausdorff dimension one and Kurtz random sequences are cofinal in the K-degrees.

papers.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
papers.abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

papers.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
papers.abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.

papers.title: Gamification Box: Automated Personalized Rewards for Improved Task Experience
papers.abstract: We introduce a gamified rewarding system, called "Gamification Box", and conduct a user study to examine its effects on task experience and performance. Gamification Box provides an interface for automated rewards that are intrinsically enjoyable activities, such as watching short video clips. In a controlled user experiment, 118 participants completed a short-term memory task involving meaningless syllables under either a gamified reward condition or a non-rewarded control condition. Participants in the gamified condition reported significantly greater perceived task enjoyment than those in the control group. Importantly, this increase in perceived enjoyment did not come at the cost of performance: no significant differences were observed in free recall or recognition accuracy between conditions. These findings suggest that while gamified rewards may not directly enhance immediate performance, they function as a motivational regulator, thereby improving task enjoyment. The primary benefit of such systems may therefore lie in supporting sustained effort over time, where cumulative performance gains are more likely to emerge.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Joint Generative Modeling of Fault Event Sequences and Sensor Time Series in Solar PV Plants
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multimodal generative model designed to simulate a solar energy plant system for predictive maintenance and fault prediction. We propose a novel approach to enhance system generation through conditional generation by leveraging both event sequences and time-series data and improve next event prediction. The framework employs a Transformer Hawkes Process (THP) to encode event data and an iTransformer to encode time-series data, integrated via a co-attention mechanism that effectively captures cross-modal dependencies between discrete events and continuous signals. From these integrated representations, we employ two specialized decoders for simulation: a Conditional Latent Diffusion Model (CLDM) for modeling future sensor trajectories and the Score Matching-based UnceRtainty quantiFication for Transformer Hawkes Process (SMURF-THP) for high-fidelity event prediction. This dual-decoder strategy supports uncertainty-aware, history-conditioned simulation by rolling the model forward for a specified number of generation iterations, producing finite stochastic scenarios rather than deterministic extrapolations over the full observational record. Evaluated on a comprehensive dataset from the Red Rock Solar Site in Arizona, our approach improves aggregate event-prediction F1 relative to baselines and supports applications in predictive maintenance, fault detection, and energy optimization for solar power systems.

papers.title: FlyWheel: Attention Kernels Built for the TPU
papers.abstract: Attention kernels on Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) often underutilize their matrix units (MXUs) because of repeated matrix operand loads, vector-intensive computation, and dependencies that leave MXUs idle. We present FlyWheel, a set of fast TPU kernels for both softmax and linear attention. FlyWheel reformulates softmax and triangular inversion to reduce vector work, while coordinating data layouts to improve matrix operand reuse. It then overlaps independent computation to hide execution latency. We apply these techniques to both softmax attention and Gated DeltaNet on TPU v6e and v7x. FlyWheel speeds up softmax attention by up to $4.14\times$ over the state-of-the-art RPA kernel and $1.80\times$ over Splash Attention, reaching 81% of peak BF16 throughput on v6e. It also speeds up Gated DeltaNet prefill by up to $3.61\times$. Integrated into vLLM serving Qwen3.8-27B, FlyWheel improves prefill throughput by up to $1.56\times$ while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.title: Towards Fine-grained and Robust Detection of Human-AI Co-authorship
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping how textual content is produced, complicating text provenance, and raising concerns for misinformation, plagiarism, and intellectual property. While prior work on AI-generated text detection has progressed, one-dimensional human-AI co-authorship scores lack signals directly relevant to ``AI involvement''. It remains unclear how adversarial paraphrasing distorts detection signals. In this work, we formulate a discrete-class text provenance detection framework. This framework allows an abstraction of realistic co-authorship scenarios into distinct degrees of AI involvement, differentiating the AI polishing on the surface level from the AI updating the discourse structures. This framework reveals the mechanisms of how adversarial paraphrasing blurs the decision boundaries for co-authorship detectors. To improve robustness of the detectors, we augment training data with adversarial paraphrases generated by the state-of-the-art paraphrasing attack model, exposing detectors to challenging meaning-preserving rewrites. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and generation models demonstrate that adversarial paraphrasing substantially degrades detectors trained only on benign data, while adversarial data augmentation leads to consistent robustness gains and good cross-generator transferability. Overall, our findings highlight the value of discrete-class formulation and principled data augmentation for building reliable detectors of human-AI co-authorship.

papers.title: Whittaker modules for the principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ via free field realizations
papers.abstract: We study Whittaker and generalized Whittaker modules for the universal principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, using two free field realizations: one in the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank two and the other in the tensor product of the universal Virasoro vertex algebra with the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank one. Under explicit conditions on the parameters, we construct universal Whittaker modules, establish their ordered bases, and obtain explicit irreducibility criteria. Under an explicit nondegeneracy condition, we also show that the submodules of these tensor products correspond to the submodules of the Virasoro factor. We prove irreducibility of the universal Whittaker modules constructed in this paper.

papers.title: When Should an Agent Refresh? Adaptive Index Reuse for Efficient Long-Horizon Reasoning
papers.abstract: Language agents read code, tool output, and dialogue in contexts that grow at every step. Dynamic sparse attention lets a small indexer choose the earlier tokens each query attends to, but the indexer still scores the whole prefix at every layer. Cross-layer reuse methods such as IndexCache rerun the indexer at only some layers, with one fixed pattern for every input. In an agent, the relevant evidence can change abruptly when a traceback or test result arrives, so fresh selections matter more at some steps than at others. We propose Adaptive Index Reuse (AIR), which keeps IndexCache's execution and learns, for each segment of an agent episode, how many layers refresh their selection. A small controller reads signals from completed computation and the latest tool event, chooses a pattern from a nested library, and learns from terminal task reward under an expected compute budget. On Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with a 128K context, AIR improves success over the strongest static schedule at matched cost on SWE-bench Verified (27.0% to 32.4%), Terminal-Bench 2.0, and three $τ^2$-bench domains, and it lowers time per successful task on all five. Across 50 backbone, context, and benchmark settings, it matches or exceeds that schedule in 44.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Minimax Prediction for Stationary Renewal Processes
papers.abstract: The minimax next-symbol Kullback-Leibler risk for stationary binary renewal processes is known to have order n^(-1/2). We give a polynomial-time predictor attaining this order for an arbitrary unknown finite-mean interarrival law. The construction uses a classical type-uniform renewal code. Its contribution is an exact dynamic program for censored prefix marginals, avoiding enumeration of gap histograms or binary completions. Combined with an established prediction reduction, it gives risk at most [log M_(n+1)+log(n+2)]/n, where M_N counts renewal types. Shared suffix updates reduce the total computation to O(n^3) arithmetic work and polynomial bit complexity, without tail, mixing, known-mean, or bounded-support assumptions. The statistical rate and its lower bound are prior results; the proposed advance concerns computation.

papers.title: Longest-Queue Policies in Dynamic Matching with Abandonments
papers.abstract: We study a dynamic two-way matching market in which agents of heterogeneous types arrive over time, wait to be matched according to a compatibility network, and abandon the system if their random patience expires. The decision maker collects match rewards and pays holding and abandonment costs, and seeks to maximize the expected net value over a finite horizon. We evaluate policies by their approximation ratio against a fluid benchmark, the optimal value of a linear-programming relaxation that upper bounds the expected net value of every policy. Under a general position gap (GPG) condition, which requires the unique optimal dual solution of this linear program to remain optimal under small perturbations of the arrival rates, we propose a longest-queue policy. The policy first uses this dual solution to identify a set of good match types and a set of critical agent types. Upon each arrival, it considers only good matches and matches the arrival to the critical partner with the longest queue subject to availabilities. In the high-volume regime, in which arrival rates are scaled by s, we prove that the policy attains an approximation ratio of at least 1-O(1/s) at every scale s >= 1 and every horizon T >= 1, so the ratio tends to 1 as s goes to infinity.

papers.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
papers.abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

papers.title: $L^1$ amplification near a self-similar vortex collapse in 2D Navier-Stokes
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative $L^1$ instability for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse as viscosity tends to zero. For every $0<γ<\frac12$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, we construct solutions that are $O(ν^{1-γ})$-close in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ at $t_0$ but exhibit order-one $L^1$ separation in a shrinking neighborhood of the collapse point at times approaching collapse as $ν\to0$. By time translation, we also obtain pairs of solutions with initial $L^1$ distance $O(ν^{1-γ})$ that develop order-one separation at a fixed positive time. In both constructions, the solutions have the same viscosity and total circulation and are uniformly bounded in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The proof exploits the amplification of small time delays, the fast speed of the vortex centers near collapse, together with sharp inviscid approximation estimates for the Navier--Stokes equations established in~\cite{Ga11,NguyenCollapse}.

papers.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
papers.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.

papers.title: World average charged-current inclusive neutrino cross section from 6 to 200 GeV
papers.abstract: The methods of the Particle Data Group are applied to produce a world average inclusive, charged-current, muon neutrino cross section energy-dependence slope $σ/E_ν$ . For the energy range $30 < E_ν< 200$, values obtained are (0.677 $\pm$ 0.013) and (0.335 $\pm$ 0.007) $\times 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV for neutrino and anti-neutrino, respectively. These values are practically identical to those in common use. This paper expands the experiments whose data are used and describes the evolution of measurements leading to the result. Next, the value for $σ/E_ν$ is obtained for the low energy extensions by experiments that used the low-$ν$ method to anchor to the high energy result. In the range $6 < E_ν< 30$ GeV, values of (0.698 $\pm$ 0.018) and (0.316 $\pm$ 0.012) $\times 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV are obtained. These are higher than the high energy average for neutrino and lower for anti-neutrino, but consistent at the edge of the uncertainty estimates. An interpretation of the evolution of the inclusive cross section, nuclear effects, and isoscalar corrections is provided in the context of the Bodek Yang 2000 model and two configurations of the GENIE neutrino event generators. These cross sections underpin foundational neutrino quantities such as structure functions, electroweak parameter measurements, and oscillation parameter determinations.

papers.title: Transport for Conditional Sampling: Foundations and Applications
papers.abstract: Conditional sampling is central to Bayesian inference, generative modeling, and causal inference: given a joint law for random variables $X$ and $Y$ and an observation $Y=y$, one seeks to sample from the conditional law of $X\mid Y=y$. Even when the joint distribution is accurately represented, this task can be computationally difficult as it may require evaluating intractable normalizing constants or solving a new inference problem for each observation. Measure transport provides an approach to this problem by identifying a map with triangular structure that directly pushes forward a reference to the conditional of a joint distribution for any observation. This article reviews the theoretical, methodological, and algorithmic foundations of triangular transports, with the Knothe-Rosenblatt rearrangement as a canonical construction. We discuss methods for estimating triangular maps from finite samples, as well as their use in simulation-based inference and causal inference. While our primary aim is to review existing formulations, we also present new ideas and open questions for conditional sampling using transport.

papers.title: Adaptive Surface Cleaning under Uncertain Cleaning Response
papers.abstract: Surface cleaning requires robots to adapt both where they clean and how they interact with contamination whose response to cleaning may vary spatially and remain unobservable prior to interaction. We formulate adaptive surface cleaning as a partially observable Markov decision process and propose a belief-aware planning framework that uses observed cleaning outcomes to update a latent local cleaning-response model and adapt subsequent cleaning motions, forces, and passes. Preliminary grid-world simulations demonstrate the resulting closed-loop planner adapting its spatial decomposition and cleaning actions as the surface evolves.

papers.title: FOCUS: Closed-Loop Attention Feedback for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding
papers.abstract: Processing every video frame through Vision-Language Models (VLMs) adds significant inference cost and limits their ability to comprehend real-time video. Existing approaches either sub-sample frames uniformly, ignoring content and missing important events, or prune visual tokens inside the VLM to cut per-call cost while still invoking the model on every sampled frame. We introduce FOCUS, a training-free three-layer framework that reduces the number of invocations and steers each one towards what matters. Temporal gating measures inter-frame dissimilarity in the patch-embedding space of a smaller VLM from the same family, triggering burst captures only when the scene changes in a semantically meaningful way. Patch-level dissimilarity is then accumulated across the burst and fused with a top-down attention prior into a spatial focus map that encodes where motion and semantic relevance coincide. That map calibrates the VLM's value cache during generation, progressively amplifying vision tokens in task-relevant regions and attenuating off-target ones, without removing any token from the context. The loop closes after each response: text-to-vision cross-attention is extracted from the decoder and fed back as the prior for the next burst, letting the system converge on semantically important regions over successive observations. We evaluate FOCUS on the 500-video EgoSchema subset in streaming mode, with a single Qwen3-VL-8B backbone shared by every method. It reaches 74.8% accuracy using 25.4 VLM calls per clip, against 74.6% with 55 calls for uniform sampling and 74.2% with 55 calls for BOLT. On egocentric video captioning across four domains, it matches the best baseline's quality while issuing 57% fewer VLM invocations than uniform sampling.

papers.title: Parameters and lim CM sequences: the Q-sequence conjecture and Lech's formula
papers.abstract: We prove that if a local ring has a weakly lim Cohen-Macaulay sequence of modules, then it satisfies the conjecture that every system of parameters is a Q-sequence. We also give a generalization of Lech's formula for the multiplicity of a local ring $(R,m)$ with respect to a system of parameters that allows a very large class of sequences of $m$-primary ideals generated by monomials in the parameters to be used in the calculation. The cases where the sequence of ideals consists of the powers of the ideal generated by parameters, or where the ideals in the sequence are generated by varying powers of the individual parameters all of which tend to infinity, which is Lech's original formula, are included.

papers.title: Precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with Weibull-type and lognormal-type random step sizes
papers.abstract: We prove precise large deviations for the symmetric elephant random walk with random step sizes. When the distribution of $|Z_1-1|$ is subexponential, we first show that, for each fixed$p\in[0,1]$, there exists a positive number sequence $b_n\to\infty$ such that \[ \mathbb P(S_n>x)\sim \mathbb P(S_n<-x)\sim \frac n2\overline F(x) \] uniformly for $x\ge b_n$, where $\overline F(x)=\mathbb P(|Z_1-1|>x)$. This existence result requires no moment assumptions and does not specify the growth rate of $b_n$. For $p\in[0,3/4]$, we further give explicit sufficient conditions on $b_n$ under Weibull-type and lognormal-type tail conditions with a regularly varying factor $x^γL(x)$, where $γ\in\mathbf R$ and $L$ is a positive measurable slowly varying function. Analogous results hold with $\mathbb P(|Z_1|>x)$ and non-strict tails.

papers.title: Renormalized Cellular Intelligence: When Does Model Reduction Preserve Collective Capability?
papers.abstract: As multi-agent systems grow in size and complexity, understanding which features of their interactions support collective capability becomes increasingly difficult. Can a simpler description preserve both task performance and the measured contribution of interactions between agents? Preserving collective dynamics alone is insufficient: reduction can alter decision-relevant information or give a non-communicating baseline access to pooled observations, distorting the measured advantage of interaction. We introduce Renormalized Cellular Intelligence (RCI), a framework for specifying and auditing capability preservation across scales. RCI treats the task, interacting dynamics, matched baseline, decision interfaces, and resource budget as a joint object of reduction. It specifies dynamical closure, decision compatibility, and preservation of the intended baseline comparison, and bounds the resulting error in relative capability gain. An exact analytical construction demonstrates task-score preservation, while a counterexample shows how closed reduced dynamics can erase the measured interaction gain. Using cellular systems as models of locally interacting agents, we evaluate three reduction candidates on five frozen learned models without retraining. The final candidate reduces the evolving state from eight to five dimensions per cell (37.5%). Within-run uncertainty bounds support relative gain above a prespecified threshold for the fixed model collection, yet the candidate fails the closure and decision-preservation requirements for a complete RCI certificate. RCI provides explicit criteria for distinguishing positive interaction gains from

papers.title: Dual Path Following for an Aerial Manipulator Under State and Input Constraints via Transverse Feedback Linearization
papers.abstract: This paper studies dual path following for a quadrotor carrying a three-degree-of-freedom arm. The center of mass of the combined system must follow a vehicle path and the end effector must follow a second path, while the arm respects its joint limits and avoids its singular postures. The vehicle and the arm are mechanically coupled, so one controller must handle both paths. With the center of mass and the end-effector path coordinates as outputs, and a dynamic extension of the thrust, the system admits a normal form without internal dynamics. We characterize the states where this normal form fails. We formulate the transverse feedback linearizing controller as a quadratic program that relaxes only the speed of the end effector along its path and imposes safety and actuator limits as inequality constraints. The program reduces to a scalar problem with a closed-form solution. If it remains strictly feasible for all time, the feedback is locally Lipschitz, both paths are invariant and attractive, and every constraint holds. In the physics engine Drake, the controller resolves a conflict between the two speed references by slowing the end effector while both paths remain invariant. By contrast, a cascade with a safety filter leaves both paths. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/am_dual_pf-/

papers.title: $p$-Wasserstein distance and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$. We also determine the covariance bias under the uncorrected normalization and establish the corresponding Wasserstein bounds, lower bounds and moderate deviation estimates. The dimension and the model parameters are fixed.

papers.title: Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers
papers.abstract: Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $π_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $p_k:\tilde{R}_n\rightarrow R_n$ be the standard $k$-sheeted regular cyclic cover of $R_n$ induced by a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action on $\tilde{R}_n$ (which is homotopy equivalent to $R_{n_k}$, where $n_k=k(n-1)+1$) generated by a free rotation through $2π/k$ of $\tilde{R}_n$. Let $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ be the liftable outer automorphism group associated with a standard $k$-sheeted normal cover $p_k$. For $n\geq3$, we show that $\{\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)\}_{k\geq2}$ forms an infinite family of self-normalizing subgroups of $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$. For $n\geq2$, these groups are maximal if and only if $k$ is prime. Furthermore, we derive explicit finite generating sets for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_{n_k}}(F_n)$ for $k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle τ\rangle$, where $τ$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. As a final application, we obtain a finite generating set for $\mathrm{Out}_{F_\infty}(F_n)$ when $n\geq 3$.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials
papers.abstract: For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{τ,δτ,τδ,δτδ\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $δ$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langleδ\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.

papers.title: I-PTC: Interactive Programmatic Tool Calling for Stateful Tool-Augmented Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly capable of writing and executing code, suggesting a natural paradigm for tool-augmented agents: expressing tool use as programs rather than isolated calls. Programmatic tool calling (PTC) captures this idea through loops, batching, abstraction, and structured computation, but existing PTC approaches are largely stateless, limiting their ability to reuse intermediate results and adapt over time. This is problematic for real-world tasks, where tool environments and problem-solving processes are inherently stateful. We therefore present I-PTC, an interactive framework that executes stateful PTC: models issue code snippets that call tools, maintain reusable state, and evolve the tool interface through API corrections. To evaluate the effectiveness of I-PTC and the general PTC setting, we introduce PTC-Bench, a benchmark of long-tail, production-style user requests whose difficulty comes from large initial environments, many dependent API interactions, extended planning, and recovery across follow-ups and transient failures. Experiments on PTC-Bench show that I-PTC improves performance on complex multi-step tasks with large tool sets while substantially reducing token consumption over conventional tool-calling baselines and the original PTC baseline, highlighting stateful programmatic tool calling as a promising direction for scalable tool-augmented agents.

papers.title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
papers.abstract: Uncertainty estimates from fuzzy regression are informative only when the implementation is correct and the comparison protocol makes the sources of variation visible. We revisit a first-order Takagi--Sugeno--Kang (TSK) regression implementation and rebuild its dense, conjugate Bayesian, BIC-based, and rule-level spike-and-slab estimators using corrected code. The corrected pipeline freezes the Gaussian membership partition at training time, uses a scaled conjugate prior, evaluates firing strengths in the log domain, and reports direct posterior-predictive quantiles for Bayesian methods. Across 30 outer 80/20 splits on three targets from two UCI regression datasets, corrected TSK-LS obtains $R^2=0.957$, $0.923$, and $0.786$ on Energy-Heating, Energy-Cooling, and Concrete, respectively; rule-level Gibbs sampling with Bayesian model averaging obtains $0.957$, $0.922$, and $0.784$. We then evaluate the same workflow on a bounded chronological sample of the Building Data Genome 2 meter data that covers 158 buildings across 17 sites. In a common-unit evaluation, every method is scored on the same 47,400 test rows and every trained model uses 94,800 train--validation rows. Persistence has RMSE $27.710$, compared with $29.083$ for both TSK-LS and Bayesian TSK; the pre-specified building-level mean RMSE difference between Bayesian TSK and persistence is $+0.0447$ with a 95% site-cluster bootstrap interval of $[-1.5536,1.5665]$. The Bayesian TSK 90% intervals have PICP $0.980$ and MPIW $116.469$. Taken together, the evidence supports a narrower conclusion: spike-and-slab model averaging is a reproducible implementation option, but it does not provide a demonstrated accuracy or calibration advantage across the tested tabular and building-meter settings.

papers.title: Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction
papers.abstract: A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain Ωin \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (Δt=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);

papers.title: CONFIRM: Governing Scientific Reporting for Trustworthy Agentic Neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can autonomously run neuroimaging analyses from research questions to reported findings. Existing agentic systems use tools to check that code runs and reported values match its output, but rely on LLM judgment to decide which results warrant scientific reporting. We show that LLM judges endorse site-confounded findings even when the confound is presented as evidence. We present \textbf{CONFIRM}, a framework that separates running an analysis from deciding which findings to report. CONFIRM encodes each hypothesis as a machine-readable, pre-specified analysis plan that fixes the claim and its pass criteria before computing results. It then filters results through five deterministic gates (search history and multiplicity, confounds, power, analytic stability, and replication) under three configurable reporting standards, from least to most demanding: \textit{Screen}, \textit{Replicate}, and \textit{Full}. Failed claims receive diagnoses that guide follow-up analyses. To evaluate reporting decisions at the claim level, we introduce \textbf{NeuroClaimBench}, comprising 489 executable neuroimaging claims with frozen data, including literature-supported findings and 150 controls designed to violate individual methodological requirements. On NeuroClaimBench, CONFIRM falsely supports at most 3\% of controls, compared with 23--38\% for the baselines, while recovering up to 61\% of literature-supported claims. When auditing an existing agent, CONFIRM reduces false support on controls from 23\% to 0\% while retaining the agent's literature-supported claims. Its diagnostic feedback also produces more supported revisions than Self-Refine with fewer LLM calls. Together, CONFIRM and NeuroClaimBench show that basing reporting decisions on pre-specified analysis plans and deterministic gates is essential for trustworthy autonomous scientific discovery.

papers.title: CipherFlow: Compiling AI Programs for Efficient Cryptographically Secure Inference
papers.abstract: Cryptographically secure inference faces two practical challenges: making secure programming accessible to AI developers and data scientists, and achieving efficient execution across deployment environments. Developers must compose cryptographic primitives correctly, while performance depends on hardware, networks, and evolving ciphertext states. We present CipherFlow, a compiler framework that takes a high-level AI computation graph, available cryptographic primitives, and a target hardware and network configuration to generate an executable, latency-optimized secure inference program. CipherFlow automates cryptographic execution decisions through three techniques: MicroBench profiles deployment-specific primitive costs; state-expanded planning jointly optimizes homomorphic encryption (HE) and secure multi-party computation (MPC) placement, conversions, and ciphertext maintenance under cryptographic-state constraints; and BlockFold summarizes branched regions to scale planning to Transformer graphs. Evaluation using measured HE/MPC backend costs across CPU/GPU and network settings shows up to 16.5$\times$ speedup on BERT-base and over 22$\times$ on ViT compared with static hybrid placement baselines. CipherFlow separates model programming from cryptographic execution decisions, enabling developers to express AI computations while the compiler constructs efficient secure programs.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $Q$ with conductors coprime to $3$, with a main term of order $Q$ and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order $Q^{\frac{5}{6}}$, with error $O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)$.

papers.title: Improved first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We study the smoothed first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions for which every nontrivial power of the character remains primitive. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet and finite order Hecke $L$-functions occurring in the proof, we obtain asymptotic formulas with errors $O(Q^{\frac{49}{58}+\eps})$ and $O(Q^{\frac{23}{26}+\eps})$, respectively. We follow the double Dirichlet series approach of Gao and Zhao. The main ingredient is a joint estimate for the two sums arising from the removal of rational prime divisors, with the Möbius coefficients retained. This gives a quotient of Dirichlet $L$-functions. Under GRH, we bound both the Dirichlet $L$-functions and their reciprocals. Combining the joint estimate with estimates for the generating series of Gauss sums gives larger regions of meromorphic continuation. These regions do not separate the possible secondary terms.

papers.title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
papers.abstract: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circΦ^{-1}$. For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $Λ_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+Φ(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$. We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern. An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.

papers.title: PROBE: Learned Proxy-Based Execution for Highly Selective Multimodal Semantic Queries
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enable semantic queries over unstructured data, but invoking an LLM on every row is prohibitively expensive. Proxy-based execution can reduce this ple with the LLM and training a lightweight proxyto label the remaining rows. Nevertheless, in practical scenarios where semantic queries are highly selective, it remainschallenging to identify representative samples foLM budget and to achieve accurate predictions overthe remaining data using the proxy. We present PROBE, a learned proxy-based execution framework for highly selective multimodal semantic queries. PROBE uses selectivity-adaptive sampling to discover rare polightweight proxy on the acquired labels. It thenrefines proxy predictions through residual correction and homogeneity smoothing over a similarity graph. To address sampling bias, PROBE jointly calibrates refined scores usiarate calibration sample, then selectively routescandidates to the LLM by optimizing the tradeoff between estimated F1 and evaluation cost. On queries from SemBench and LRO-Bench with positive rates as low as 2.17x10^-5 budget yields a geometric-mean F1 of 0.762,compared with 0.797 for exhaustive LLM evaluation, at a geometric-mean speedup of 4.87x and a maximum speedup of 9.3x.

papers.title: Local Limit Theorem for Branching Processes in Varying Environments
papers.abstract: Let $Z_{i,n}$ be the population at time $n$ descended from one particle at time $i$ in a branching process in a varying environment. Under two-sided bounds on products of offspring means, an integrable uniform second-moment tail condition, and nondegeneracy and unit positive-support gcd of all weak limits, we prove $\mathbb{P}(Z_{i,n}=k)\le C(n-i+1)^{-2}$ uniformly in $0\le i<n$ and $k\ge1$, and obtain a local limit theorem as $n-i,k\to\infty$ with $k\le L_0(n-i)$, without third-moment assumptions. These results extend the classical local probability estimates for critical Galton--Watson processes to varying environments.

papers.title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
papers.abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.

papers.title: ContactCut: A Partition-Aware Contact Selection Framework for False-Merge Correction in Connectomics
papers.abstract: Localized false-merge correction in connectomics requires converting an identified error into an executable native 3D partition. Still, neither intermediate correction predictions nor seeded graph solvers alone determine which native source-sink constraints should define that partition. We formulate this problem as a 3D-native partition-aware contact selection problem: selecting candidate contacts based on the complete partitions they induce. Our solution comprises two components: ContactCut (CC)-Auto, which uses learned single-contact selection, and ContactCut (CC)-Search, which enables bounded paired-contact search, generates compact alternatives, and applies learned panel ranking. On historical two-way false-merge corrections from MICrONS and FlyWire, CC-Auto improves failure-aware 3D partition (FA-3D Part.) mIoU by 5.9 and 3.4 points over the strongest graph-based controls and by 12.5 and 10.0 points over the best learned baselines. A MICrONS-trained ranker transfers to FlyWire with negligible degradation. CC-Search expands oracle reachability and prioritizes near-oracle alternatives. The code is available at https://github.com/bentake/ContactCut.

papers.title: Convergence of many-body truncations in the in-medium similarity renormalization group
papers.abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) is a leading \textit{ab initio} method for describing atomic nuclei. Most applications truncate the flowing operators at the normal-ordered two-body level, neglecting induced higher-body terms. Convergence with increasing operator rank remains poorly understood, particularly in strongly correlated systems. We systematically assess the many-body truncation hierarchy in the single-reference and multi-reference IMSRG, retaining normal-ordered operators through the four-body and three-body levels, respectively. Using an exactly solvable pairing-plus-particle-hole model, we quantify successive higher-body corrections over a broad range of interaction strengths, spanning weakly to strongly correlated regimes. The multi-reference formulation exhibits faster and more robust convergence than its single-reference counterpart, with the advantage becoming most pronounced at strong coupling. In this regime, higher-rank irreducible density matrices play an essential role in achieving convergence of the many-body expansion.

papers.title: Vehicle and UAV Detection and Tracking with LTE Downlink Reference Signals: A Ray-Traced Evaluation on a Mapped Suburban Site with Licensed Base-Station Records
papers.abstract: Passive sensing on the cellular downlink places the receiver at the user equipment and changes nothing in the network. We report simulation results for an LTE band-3 cell-specific reference signal arm on a ray-traced channel. On a synthetic street canyon the arm is compared with an uplink sounding reference signal arm on the same band, target and scorer: missed-detection probabilities of 0.667 and 0.772. On a surveyed site built from OpenStreetMap footprints and the licensed site record, nine receiver positions along the street track the vehicle at coverage between 29.9 % and 61.7 %; a 283 m lap separates target height from trajectory at 1.6 to 30 m; a 137 m lap on the built-up street tracks a vehicle and a 15 m airborne target on every cell, and 8 receivers at 135 m spacing carry one illuminator's coverage over 1140 m of the street. Potential future work includes extending the analysis to multiple illuminators and varying receiver configurations, and confirmation through over-the-air measurements.

papers.title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
papers.abstract: Humans continuously acquire knowledge from carefully crafted materials such as books and tutorial videos, carrying that understanding into future tasks. Millions of such instructional videos are uploaded online every day, yet LLM agents remain unable to exploit this ever-expanding wealth of human teaching. Their capabilities are frozen after training, while parameter updates at scale remain prohibitively expensive. This raises the central question: can LLM agents learn from this vast instructional resource without parameter updates? We introduce Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured tutorialbook memory through a two-stage adversarial process that harvests hard, video-grounded questions and uses them to refine the memory. At inference time, TAL retrieves through a Table-of-Contents (TOC) tree, tying retrieval directly to the model's reasoning rather than to embedding similarity. To study this setting, we introduce VidLearn, a multimodal QA benchmark built from 72 chess tutorial videos spanning 12 openings. On VidLearn, TAL outperforms all evaluated baselines and improves monotonically as more videos are consumed, achieving up to 113% and 91% relative gains over the corresponding vanilla MLLMs on the training and test splits, respectively. In actual gameplay, TAL reaches a stronger opening-phase position than its vanilla counterpart in 69% of head-to-head games. Evaluation in a second domain further demonstrates the generality of TAL. Together, these results highlight instructional videos as a scalable resource for parameter-update-free agent continual learning.

papers.title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
papers.abstract: Assigning GWAS variants to causal genes requires evidence from multiple resources. We present V2G, an agentic pipeline that records evidence retrieval and returns ranked genes alongside the retrieved evidence. We evaluate whether language-model reranking improves gene prioritisation and whether its gains depend on the retrieved evidence or recall of known associations. On 135 held-out loci where candidate retrieval succeeded and Open Targets L2G predicts, reranking by a language model improves Precision@1 over the evidence ordering it receives, 0.793 against 0.711 (+0.081, 95% CI +0.038 to +0.129), and over nearest-gene assignment (+0.178); no difference from Open Targets L2G or from training-membership baselines was detected. Given only the trait and the candidate gene symbols, in shuffled order, the same model scores 0.864 on these loci (three seeds, 0.859 - 0.867) and names the reference gene at 0.594 of the loci where the pipeline never retrieved it; with each gene's symbol moved to another gene's evidence row it follows the top-scored row and scores 0.284. The gain over the evidence ordering is recall of known genes, and the evidence as presented anchors the model to the ordering rather than informing it. Across the 296 held-out loci (five seeds each) the model keeps the given top candidate at 86% of decisions; at naturally retrieved loci its departures select a reference gene in 85% of departure decisions (31 of 37 loci), and none displaced one. Its calls carry trait-matched mouse mutant or Mendelian phenotype annotations more often than other candidates at the same locus. Train-test overlap is reported throughout. The study includes a frozen benchmark, cached predictions and reproduction code.

papers.title: Optimizing synthetic jet placement for control stability in increasing Reynolds number flows based on deep reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: This study utilizes reinforcement learning algorithms to develop advanced control strategies for manipulating synthetic jets positioned on a cylinder, aiming to achieve effective flow control. It addresses critical challenges in achieving robust performance across moderate to high Reynolds numbers (Re) and varying jet placement configurations. The results demonstrate that placing synthetic jets near flow separation regions yields optimal control performance. At Re = 500, the multi-objective flow control strategy achieves up to 37.4% drag reduction and 99% suppression of lift oscillations, while completely suppressing vortex shedding. At Re = 1,000, drag reduction improves to 49.1%, with equally effective lift suppression and complete vortex shedding suppression. At Re = 2,000, the strategy achieves a maximum drag reduction of 58.8% and suppresses 90% of lift oscillations, although some residual wake instabilities persist. Additionally, synthetic jets effectively disrupted detached vortices and stabilized the wake, resulting in streamlined flow and suppressed vortex shedding. These findings underscore the pivotal influence of jet placement in optimizing flow control efficacy, while affirming the advanced capability of control strategies to tackle intricate challenges.

papers.title: DIMWIT: Directly Invoking Models Without Intensive Tuning
papers.abstract: Resource managers typically encode what to do in a task-specific policy---a heuristic, an optimization procedure, or a model trained for the task---that must be developed before use and may need revision as the workload or system changes. We propose bypassing policy development and instead asking pretrained models to make resource-management decisions directly, given the current system state, desired outcome, and available choices. We evaluate this approach on microservice autoscaling, DRAM sizing, and video encoding, using a frontier LLM and two small decision models. On two microservice applications, a small decision model meets latency targets while using within 10% of the replicas allocated by policy-based autoscalers and within 13% of the frontier LLM. In DRAM sizing, a small decision model reduces DRAM usage by up to 27.5% relative to static provisioning while maintaining at least 95% of baseline performance. In video encoding, it completes encodes up to 4.3$\times$ faster than the frontier LLM, with an imperceptible 1.1-point decrease in Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), a metric of perceptual video quality. Making individual resource-management decisions may be considerably simpler than developing a general strategy for making them.

papers.title: Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $φ_T=T+g_1τ+\cdots+g_rτ^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. Ordering the coefficient tuples $\vec{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ by their maximum degree, we prove that, for a density-one set of tuples, the $λ$-adic Galois representation is surjective for every prime $λ$ of $A$, and the adelic Galois image contains $\mathrm{SL}_r(\widehat A)$. Moreover, for every tuple in this set, the index of the adelic image equals the index of the corresponding rank-one determinant representation and hence divides $q-1$. These results extend Zywina's theorem in rank $2$ to arbitrary ranks $r\geq 3$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

papers.title: Extremal permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with many good slopes and applications to quantum Latin squares
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We prove the sharp upper bound $\varphi(n)$ on the number of good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. We classify and count the equality cases for prime powers and products of two distinct odd primes. Non-affine equality cases exist for every composite $n\ge6$. We also prove the sharp bound $p_0-1$ for the size of a set of good slopes with invertible differences between distinct elements, where $p_0$ is the least prime divisor of $n$. Finally, we establish gap results below $\varphi(n)$ and apply our bounds to a construction of quantum Latin squares due to Ball and Simoens.

papers.title: Resolve, Clear, or Defer: Training-Free Active Prototype Triage for Ecological Detection Pipelines
papers.abstract: Ecological monitoring increasingly relies on camera traps and aerial surveys that generate large image collections. High-recall animal detectors can localize candidate animals at scale. However, they also produce many detections that still require expert review, including false positives, ambiguous cases, and animals difficult to identify at the species level. Since exhaustive review requires substantial effort, we propose training-free active prototype triage, where reviewed detections become reusable evidence to (1) Resolve supported foreground classes, (2) Clear likely background false positives, or (3) Defer insufficiently supported cases for expert review. Across camera-trap and aerial datasets, foreground recognition and false-positive rejection benefit from different pretrained representations: BioCLIP2 provides foreground evidence while DINOv3 provides background evidence, reducing erroneous foreground clearing while improving automatic foreground recovery. Deferring unsupported cases avoids the higher error rates caused by forced decisions. Compared with confidence-thresholded multiclass k-NN and uncertainty-sampling logistic regression, prototype triage improves foreground recovery while maintaining competitive or lower review burden. Acquisition goes beyond class discovery: even after classes are represented, prototype choice determines how reliably evidence propagates through the remaining detections. Our results suggest that once animal localization reaches high recall, the challenge shifts from finding animals to deciding which examples to review, how to reuse them, and when evidence does not support an automatic decision.

papers.title: See, Think, Use: Diagnosing Perception and Reasoning Failures in VLMs
papers.abstract: We present See, Think, Use, a protocol that traces each answer of a vision-language model to perception, reasoning or the use of perception. The diagnosis shows a developer which stage to improve and directs test-time compute to the stage that fails. Benchmarks score the final answer, and an answer that rests on the image earns the same credit as a guess or a memorized prior. The protocol asks the model two extra questions per item and needs no access to its weights. A localization probe asks for a box around every instance and measures seeing, and a text-replacement probe answers from a description and measures thinking. Use is the rate at which the answer follows the model's own perception across counterfactual image pairs. The rate needs no answer labels, because the question and its prior are the same on both images. On two model families and six datasets the protocol shows that the knob that helps follows the task family. Answers follow the model's perception except on images that contradict a common prior, and asking the model to localize first repairs this failure when its boxes are right. Allocating compute by the measured stages comes close to the best uniform policy at lower cost and beats a random allocation of the same compute wherever a knob raises the short stage. We will release the code, the prompts and the per-question outputs.

papers.title: The Stability of Data Exchange in Competitive Markets
papers.abstract: We study the stability of data exchange among competing firms. Unlike tangible goods, data is non-rival: sharing it does not deprive the giver of its use. On one hand, competing firms-- often operating as machine-learning-driven predictors that collect observations from a shared environment to solve similar tasks-- can improve their predictive accuracies from pooling data. On the other hand, they compete for market share, which may depend on their relative predictive performance. This raises the central question of this paper: can there be a stable data exchange in such competitive environments? We formalize this via a model of $n$ firms exchanging fractions of their datasets, with predictive performance feeding into market competition. We adopt core stability as our solution concept, accounting for externalities via worst-case responses by non-participating firms. Our main results reveal a sharp contrast driven by demand structure: (i) in fully rational markets, where customers flock entirely to the top-performing firm, a core-stable exchange always exists for any monotone continuous prediction functions; (ii) in partially rational markets with logit-style demand, core-stable exchanges may fail to exist-and even approximate cores can be empty. Our impossibility results suggest that internal profit-sharing within coalitions can restore stability in partially rational markets. We formalize this intuition by showing that when co-operating coalitions equally redistribute market-share revenues among members, a core-stable data exchange exists. Finally, we propose a natural exchange dynamic and demonstrate empirically that it converges to a core-stable data exchange in fully rational markets on simulated instances derived from real datasets.

papers.title: Dynamically defined bulges reveal that early-type galaxies with compact bulges host more massive black holes
papers.abstract: We revisit the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation for early-type galaxies by introducing a uniform bulge defined by dynamical decomposition. From the set of nearby galaxies with accurately measured black hole masses, we select 30 early-type galaxies that have been observed with wide-field integral-field unit instruments (MUSE, ATLAS3D, or PPAK). For each galaxy, we construct an orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model and obtain its stellar orbit distribution. In this framework, we define the bulge uniformly as comprising stellar orbits with circularity $λ_z < 0.7$ (or, in an alternative definition, $λ_z < 0.2$) and lying within $r < 3$ kpc. From these orbits, we reconstruct the spatial density distribution of the bulge and measure its mass ($M_{bulge}$), size ($R_{bulge}$) and surface density slope ($γ_{bulge}$). We find that the dynamical bulge defined by $λ_z < 0.7$ yields masses that are systematically consistent with the photometric bulge masses. Comparing to the bulge from photometric decomposition, using this dynamical bulge definition slightly decreases the scatter around the best-fitting from 0.56 to 0.47. More interestingly, we identify a clear trend: at a given bulge mass, galaxies hosting more compact bulges (i.e. smaller bulge sizes or steeper bulge density slopes) systematically contain more massive black holes; eight outliers show overmassive BHs together with ultra-compact bulges. We interpret this as direct observational evidence that the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation evolves over a galaxy's merger history, with that history imprinted in bulge compactness. Incorporating compactness via an $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}-R_{e, bulge}$ (or $γ_{bulge}$) relation brings the outliers into agreement and reduces the overall scatter of the sample to $\sim 0.3$.

papers.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Multi-User OFDM ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a key enabling technology for 6G networks. Efficient resource sharing between communication and sensing is a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ISAC systems, particularly in multi-user scenarios, where channel diversity can be exploited to improve resource utilization. This paper investigates joint subcarrier assignment and power allocation for a downlink multi-user OFDM ISAC system, with the objective of minimizing the delay Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) subject to constraints on the normalized integrated sidelobe level (ISL) over the region of interest (RoI), per-user data rates, and total transmit power. We first derive a convex formulation for sensing power allocation given fixed subcarrier assignments, and then develop an equivalent mixed-integer conic formulation of the joint optimization problem. To obtain computationally tractable solutions, we propose a conic relaxation-guided fix-and-optimize (CRG-FO) algorithm that integrates continuous relaxation, power re-optimization under fixed subcarrier assignments, and restricted neighborhood search. Simulation results demonstrate that joint subcarrier and power allocation reduces the distance CRLB relative to uniform subcarrier and power allocation across the tested ISL thresholds, rate loads, and user configurations. Power optimization on uniform sensing supports captures most of this gain, while adaptive subcarrier assignment provides only modest additional improvement.

papers.title: Almost global solutions of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains without the second null condition
papers.abstract: For 3-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and small initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$, the authors of two papers [M. Keel, H. Smith, C.D. Sogge, Amer. J. Math. 122 (2000), no. 4, 805-842; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004), no. 1, 109-153] have shown that the lifespan ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions satisfies ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ or ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon}$, depending on whether the null condition holds or not, respectively. However, for the corresponding 2-D problem in exterior domains, it remains a difficult and unsolved problem to determine the precise lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions. In our previous papers, we have established that $T_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ holds when both the first and second null conditions are satisfied; and that $T_{\varepsilon}\ge\frac{C}{\varepsilon^2}$ holds when the first null condition is violated. In this paper, we will prove $T_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon^2}$ when the first null condition holds but the second null condition is violated. Combining these results, we have systematically established sharp estimates for the lifespan $T_{\varepsilon}$ of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moreover, our series of results for quasilinear wave equations in 2-D exterior domains are consistent with the corresponding results for the classical Cauchy problem.

papers.title: Causal Optimal-Transport Attention: Positional Priors and Length Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Causal masking obstructs the column balancing used by optimal-transport (OT) attention. We study a prefix-consistent unbalanced operator and characterize the positional prior it induces. Under bounded scores, for any fixed balancing strength $ρ<1$, its fixed point dilutes attention: every fixed window receives a vanishing share as the context grows. For constant scores, we derive an exact scale-invariant prior. We then classify positional encodings by whether their distant attention mass remains bounded away from one. Discrete window-mass bounds quantify the finite-length dilution of summable log-distance priors near exponent one. Preregistered experiments with 25M- and 100M-parameter language models establish improved loss extrapolation over softmax; exploratory comparisons favor an explicit distance bias at a fraction of the cost. CABLE outperforms RoPE with evaluation-time YaRN on every seed at three training lengths. Changing only the bias beyond the training length moves long-context loss in the predicted direction on all 30 tested checkpoints. Even with exponents constrained above one, many heads approach the summability boundary during training. A margin selected by prior-only calculations for a specified window, length range and growth tolerance controls distant-mass growth in the tested setting. These results connect loss extrapolation to positional decay over the lengths actually evaluated.

papers.title: A Surrogate Model for Variation-Aware Clock-Mesh Analysis and Design-Space Exploration using Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Clock meshes are widely used in high-performance VLSI systems to minimize skew and tolerate On-Chip Variation (OCV) in nanometer technologies. However, analyzing meshes is difficult because reconvergent paths and multi-source drivers prevent static timing analysis (STA) tools from handling mesh loops, making SPICE the industrial standard. SPICE simulations are accurate but slow, so clock-mesh synthesis relies on approximate models that overlook critical effects such as non-linear buffer driving caused by input slew and input skew. We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture that predicts power while also improving the delay and slew predictions at the sinks and capturing the skew histogram under OCV. Trained on SPICE data and tested on unseen real designs, our model achieves average errors of $3.40$~ps in delay, $4.14$~ps in slew and $4.46$~ps in skew, compared with $6.28$~ps, $12.35$~ps, and $11.62$~ps for our prior model, and $74.37$~ps delay and $27.51$~ps skew for the approximate method used in current state-of-the-art works. Our model predicts power within $3.4\%$ of SPICE on average, while delivering $18\times$-$1706\times$ speed-ups over the approximate method under OCV modeling, enabling faster and more accurate clock-mesh design-space exploration. A case study on a real design further shows that our surrogate model finds buffering candidates that, at a balanced tradeoff, improves $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile skew by $49.1\%$, reduces power by $25.7\%$, and reduces area by $37.3\%$ at the cost of a $6.8\%$ increase in $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile maximum slew as compared to the state-of-the-art work.

papers.title: Accounting for Irregular State Transitions through Belief Estimation in Online Medical Consultation
papers.abstract: While online medical consultation broadens access, unprompted patient disclosures and topic shifts frequently disrupt clinician inquiry, leaving clinical states progressively revealed. We characterize these dynamics using both existing evaluation metrics and task-specific interaction metrics designed in this work. Through an empirical study across 16 medical dialogue datasets, we show that authentic online interactions exhibit substantially lower contextual continuity and higher unpredictability than offline and simulated benchmarks. We propose PRISM (Policy Reasoning with Inferred States for Medicine), a framework inspired by partially observable Markov decision processes that decouples latent state estimation from action selection to address drifting dialogue trajectories. Specifically, PRISM factorizes clinical triage into belief estimation, policy optimization, and response realization. By maintaining an evolving posterior belief over consultation states and conditioning action selection on the maximum a posteriori state, PRISM advances clinical goals while accommodating patient-initiated shifts. Extensive evaluations show that PRISM substantially outperforms frontier LLMs and clinical agents, achieving a 22.40 percentage point gain in clinical decision accuracy alongside decisive improvements in response generation, surpassing the strongest baseline by 5.51 points in BERTScore_F1. Furthermore, ablation studies show that providing oracle consultation states consistently boosts response quality across all evaluated baselines by guiding their action reasoning, yielding average gains of 5.58 points in BERTScore_F1.

papers.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: KPZ universality
papers.abstract: We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.

papers.title: Low-Latency Joint Source-Channel Coding with Multiple Constant Curvature Curves
papers.abstract: We propose constant-curvature curve multicode (C3M), a multi-branch extension of constant-curvature curve tube (C3T) analog joint source-channel coding for one-shot transmission over fixed isotropic AWGN channels. Instead of mapping a scalar source to a single curve on the power sphere, C3M partitions the source interval across a union of constant-speed branch curves in even-dimensional Euclidean space. This construction increases the available geometric degrees of freedom while preserving a low block length analog encoding structure. We derive the induced mixture output distribution, posterior representation, MAP and MMSE estimators, and mutual-information decomposition into branch-identification and along-curve components. We then introduce geometry- and classification-aware branch allocation rules based on tube density, curve length, and branch-classification reliability. The resulting design procedure fixes the optimal C3T curve as a starting branch and sequentially selects additional branches, thereby reducing the combinatorial cost of exhaustive multi-curve search. We use NORM-inspired branch-conditioned spectral decoders based on Fourier-feature lifting of the received ambient vector. Numerical experiments in four and six dimensions show that adding candidate branch curves improves the finite-dimensional end-to-end signal-to-distortion ratio, with selected two- and three-candidate C3M systems outperforming the one-curve baseline at +10 dB SNR. The results show that multi-curve analog mappings provide a practical finite-dimensional design route for low block length joint source-channel coding.

papers.title: Spectral gaps near one quarter for Weil--Petersson random surfaces with growing cusp number
papers.abstract: We prove that the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ with $n=n(g)\ge1$ labelled cusps converges in probability to $1/4$ as $g\to\infty$, for every sequence $n=o(\sqrt g)$. More precisely, for each fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, there are constants $C_\varepsilon\ge2$ and $g_\varepsilon\ge3$, independent of $n$, such that the expected number of nonzero $L^2$ eigenvalues in $(0,1/4-\varepsilon]$, counted with multiplicity and including residual eigenvalues, is at most $C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2/g$ whenever $g\ge g_\varepsilon$ and $g\ge C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2$. This proves a conjecture of Shen and Wu. A matching lower bound shows that the count estimate is optimal up to constants for each fixed $\varepsilon$, and that $n=o(\sqrt g)$ is necessary for convergence of the gap to $1/4$. The proof combines volume estimates uniform in the cusp count with polynomial approximation and a positive trace on truncated surfaces.

papers.title: Robust Appointment Scheduling with Heterogeneous Costs
papers.abstract: Designing simple appointment systems that under uncertainty in service times, try to achieve both high utilization of expensive medical equipment and personnel as well as short waiting time for patients, has long been an interesting and challenging problem in health care. We consider a robust version of the appointment scheduling problem, introduced by Mittal et al.\ (2014), with the goal of finding simple and easy-to-use algorithms. Previous work focused on the special case where per-unit costs due to under-utilization of equipment/personnel are homogeneous i.e., costs are linear and identical. We consider the heterogeneous case and devise an LP that has a simple closed-form solution. This solution yields the first constant-factor approximation for the problem. We also find special cases beyond homogeneous costs where the LP leads to closed form optimal schedules. Our approach and results extend more generally to convex piece-wise linear costs. For the case where the order of patients is changeable, we focus on linear costs and show that the problem is strongly NP-hard when the under-utilization costs are heterogeneous. For changeable order with homogeneous under-utilization costs, it was previously shown that an EPTAS exists. We instead find an extremely simple, ratio-based ordering that is 1.0604 approximate.

papers.title: Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
papers.abstract: We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $λ$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-λt$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.

papers.title: A solution to the Erdős-Sárközy product-density problem
