We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. Numerical experiments show that, under a fixed total photon budget, task-driven metrology changes little over 12-64 views, while reconstruction-driven metrology is strongly view-dependent with much larger errors. The direct estimator also follows the expected photon-limited scaling. These results demonstrate a computational sensing strategy in which XCT acquisition, physical modeling, and inference are evaluated according to the quantitative information required by the task rather than for general-purpose volumetric image fidelity.

papers.title: Strong convergence of a slowly damped primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling, Tikhonov regularization and implicit Hessian damping
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel mixed-order inertial primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling and Tikhonov regularization coefficients, together with implicit Hessian damping, for solving convex optimization problems with linear equality constraints in Hilbert spaces. The proposed dynamical system incorporates slowly vanishing viscous damping and is developed based on a time-dependent Tikhonov-regularized Lagrangian. Under suitable assumptions, we establish fast convergence rates for the objective residual, the feasibility violation, and the primal-dual gap using a Lyapunov analysis. Moreover, we prove that the generated primal-dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm primal-dual solution. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and indicate improved convergence performance relative to the comparison dynamical systems.

papers.title: The Structure of Disagreement in Emotion Annotation
papers.abstract: Calculating inter-annotator agreement is an established practice in NLP, and disagreement-aware work increasingly retains the distribution of human judgments rather than reducing annotations to a single gold label. Keeping the distribution, however, does not explain why annotators disagree. This paper examines the types of disagreement that occur in emotion annotation, starting from multilabel annotations of 1,677 sentence-level units from Ernest Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea and testing the patterns they reveal against individual-level annotations from BRIGHTER and GoEmotions. Across the three datasets, we find three main recurring disagreement structures. Emotion categories overlap systematically; annotators differ both in how broadly they apply labels and in how they treat particular category boundaries, while sparse participation and explicit abstention can look like disagreement. Where intensity is rated, disagreement over whether an emotion is present can be separated from disagreement over its intensity once recognized. Similar aggregate disagreement can therefore arise from qualitatively different annotation processes. Hard aggregation removes most of this structure, while annotator vote-share representations keep marginal label frequencies but not the co-occurrence, annotator-specific, or procedural patterns that produced them. We argue that disagreement should be understood in terms of its underlying patterns before it is summarized, aggregated, or used as a modeling target, and propose a vocabulary for disagreement structure.

papers.title: Social Networks and the Propagation of Household Shocks to Asset Prices
papers.abstract: When can local household disturbances move credit prices? I develop a financially weighted propagation operator on the social network. In a conditional household-intermediary equilibrium, its projection determines the household-demand component of the excess bond premium. Because responses decay at different rates across network patterns and channels, a location's relative financial importance generically changes with the horizon, so no single centrality measure summarizes exposure across horizons. Household measurements recover this projection exactly when they span independently measured demand sensitivities. Empirically, social exposure to storm-damaged counties is negatively associated with spending weeks later in counties outside the recorded footprints. In simulations on the observed network under the model's diffusion law, the operator predicts the propagated credit-premium component of held-out storms with about 30 percent less error than direct social exposure.

papers.title: MoPort: A View-Aware 2D Interface for Motion Language Models
papers.abstract: Motion language models (MoLMs) encode 3D human motion as discrete tokens for language-based understanding. Deploying them on monocular video raises two problems. Pose detection yields 2D joint sequences, leaving a dimensional gap from the 3D motion used in training. Moreover, the 2D observation changes with the camera viewpoint, while the depth lost in projection makes the 2D pose ambiguous across viewpoints. We propose MoPort, a view-aware 2D interface that enables MoLMs to take 2D observations as input. We introduce Paired View Alignment (PVA), which gives two views of the same motion a shared 3D teacher target and directly constrains the consistency of their latents, so that 2D observations from different viewpoints are mapped to a consistent semantic representation. Camera-Modulated Encoding (CME) estimates the camera extrinsics from the 2D sequence and uses them to modulate encoding, providing the 2D latents with geometric information about the viewpoint. MoPort achieves R@1 of 0.5674 on HumanML3D and 0.3286 on KIT-ML, outperforming all evaluated baselines. On HumanML3D, its R@1 decreases only from 0.5763 on in-distribution viewpoints to 0.5585 on out-of-distribution viewpoints. We validate portability on three downstream MoLMs. Furthermore, on the real-world RGB video dataset Fit3D, MoPort achieves 80.36\% accuracy. Code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Rank-Optimal Sample Complexity of Riemannian Gauss-Newton for Low-Rank Matrix Recovery
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the recovery of an unknown rank-$r$ matrix $\boldsymbol{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2}$ from Gaussian linear measurements using the Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) algorithm. Each iteration of RGN solves the RGN equation followed by a fixed-rank retraction. We prove that, with high probability, RGN with spectral initialization converges quadratically to $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$ using $\mathcal{O} ( r(n_1+n_2)κ^2 )$ measurements, where $κ$ is the condition number of $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$. This is the first result to simultaneously achieve rank-optimal sample complexity and quadratic convergence for Gaussian low-rank matrix sensing. The key to the proof is a sharp spectral-norm analysis of the iterates, which requires controlling the inverse operator arising from the RGN equation. Our analysis develops an exact finite Neumann expansion of this inverse operator and combines it with a virtual-sequence decoupling argument and the restricted isometry property. Extensive numerical experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantages of RGN.

papers.title: GSExplorer: Interactive World Generation with a Persistent 3D Gaussian World State
papers.abstract: Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbf{GSExplorer}, a generation--reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.

papers.title: Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.

papers.title: Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.

papers.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<ρ<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloorρn\rfloor,n-\lfloorρn\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.

papers.title: Wilker property, function spaces and hyperspaces
papers.abstract: The Wilker property requires that a compact set covered by two open sets admit compact covering pieces inside those open sets. We study this property through products, compact-open function spaces and hyperspaces. We construct countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ hereditarily Wilker spaces with non-Wilker products and squares. For spaces whose compact subsets are closed, Wilker-ness is equivalent to every compact subspace being Hausdorff; this yields a positive product theorem when one Wilker factor has closed compact subsets. For an irreducible subset system $H$, we characterize preservation of $H$-sobriety by compact-open function spaces in terms of $H$-supercompactness of compact subsets of the domain, and show that Wilker spaces satisfy this criterion. The Hoare hyperspace of a space is Wilker exactly when binary union on the Scott space of its open-set lattice is jointly continuous for the ordinary product topology. Consequently, the Hoare construction preserves and reflects Wilker-ness on consonant bases, although preservation fails in general. We also identify core-compactness of the base with local compactness of its Hoare hyperspace and prove that the Smyth construction reflects Wilker-ness.

papers.title: Band2Net: Frequency-to-Network Transport Distillation for fMRI-Privileged, EEG-Only Session-Condition Decoding
papers.abstract: Functional MRI resolves large-scale brain networks but is expensive and stationary, whereas EEG is portable but poorly localised. We treat fMRI as privileged information, available during training and absent at deployment, with EEG and fMRI acquired from the same participants under matched conditions but not simultaneously. Band2Net encodes EEG into five frequency-specific connectivity graphs and fMRI into seven canonical network tokens from a frozen teacher, and solves a balanced entropic transport problem between the two token sets that gives each EEG band its own fMRI target. In subject-grouped cross-validation on the PsiConnect psilocybin data set, Band2Net reaches 0.801 ROC-AUC for EEG-only session-condition decoding, 5.0 AUC points (95% CI 1.8-8.2) above an EEG-only student. Although its margins over a single shared plan, a KL-relaxed plan and label-free network descriptors remain unresolved, secondary comparisons favour band-specific transported targets over logit, global-feature, contrastive and pooled-target distillation, though not after Holm correction.

papers.title: Revisiting LLM Homogeneity Through a Multidimensional Lens
papers.abstract: Concerns about LLM homogeneity are typically quantified with embedding similarity, which reduces two texts to a single score. We revisit homogeneity with 25 interpretable metrics spanning five dimensions: semantic, lexical, syntactic, structural, and stylistic & presentational. A human study shows that perceived similarity depends on both content (what responses say) and form (how they say it), yet embedding similarity correlates less with human meaning judgments than sentence-level matching ($ρ=0.417$ vs. $0.606$) and not significantly with form judgments ($ρ=0.140$). Across 18 contemporary LLMs, models say similar things in different words: they share global semantics and broad linguistic profiles but remain distinct in lexical characteristics, structural patterns, and interactional conventions. Across releases from 2024 to 2026, models become more like themselves but not more like one another: among significantly changing metrics, intra-model distances decrease for 17 of 22, and inter-model distances increase for 14 of 21. Across two post-training pipelines, model-specific conventions emerge during SFT and are selectively reshaped by preference optimization. These results suggest that homogeneity is multidimensional and evolving, and that embedding similarity alone can overstate cross-model homogeneity while concealing diverging intra- and inter-model trends.

papers.title: Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication
papers.abstract: Advances in monocular depth estimation (MDE) now let an attacker generate depth from publicly available RGB images and submit forged RGB-D queries. Such attacks break a core assumption of RGB-D place authentication: that depth comes from a sensor. We study a presentation attack detection (PAD) classifier that uses geometric consistency between the enrollment and query views, as a software-layer defense. A three-stage evaluation shows how far this classifier detects software-injected depth, depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. In the first stage, the attacker has only an estimate of the intrinsics, and the PAD classifier separates forgeries generated by all three MDE models with a validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997-0.999. In the second stage, the attacker obtains the exact intrinsics, and the original PAD classifier falls to near chance (AUC 0.54-0.61); a retrained PAD classifier, however, still has the registration residual between enrollment and query as a cue. In the third stage, an oracle evaluation, in which the evaluator fits warps using the ground-truth 3D geometry, shows that detection falls to near chance only in its strongest case, where every valid query keypoint is given its ground-truth 3D coordinate. Of the detection cues, the reprojection error captures the attacker's misestimate of the intrinsics, whereas the registration residual remains even when the attacker knows the exact intrinsics.

papers.title: TopoDPO: Dense Preference Alignment for Structure-Sensitive Aerial Referring Segmentation
papers.abstract: Preference optimization for multimodal segmentation faces a granularity mismatch: dense masks contain spatially heterogeneous preference signals, whereas image-level objectives assign one shared nonlinear weight to all spatial margins. We introduce TopoDPO, a topology-aware dense preference alignment framework for structure-sensitive aerial referring segmentation. Topo-Prior mines informative preference pairs using connected-component discrepancy and macro-corner recall, while the dense objective applies the preference penalty to each local margin before spatial aggregation against a frozen supervised reference. On Topo-RS-Hard, a 4590-instance structural stress set, TopoDPO improves intersection over union (IoU) from 50.91% to 51.24% over image-level direct preference optimization (DPO) and reduces Betti-0 error from 1.34 to 0.90; paired image-cluster bootstrap intervals against image-level DPO exclude zero for all five reported metrics. Matched supervised controls and a complete factorial analysis separate the effects of topology-aware pair mining, localized correction, and dense reference-relative preference weighting. An unfiltered stratification over all 39,244 validation records further shows the clearest structural gains on samples with moderate or severe pre-alignment component-count errors. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/phy709/TopoDPO.

papers.title: Can Large Language Models Extend Their Agentic Capabilities to Goal Pursuit in Open-Ended Multi-Turn Interaction?
papers.abstract: Goal pursuit in open-ended dialogue requires agents to adapt their actions to interaction feedback across successive exchanges. We investigate whether agentic capabilities developed for multi-step tool use carry over to dialogue organized through the model's native tool interface, and how this changes interaction behavior. We define Tool-Mediated Interaction (TMI) as a training-free protocol that represents dialogue actions as tool calls and counterpart responses as tool results, maintaining a continuous reasoning-action-observation loop with retained reasoning and interaction history. We evaluate TMI across social interaction, emotional support, persuasion, and price negotiation using two models and 15,678 main-experiment episodes. Across both models, TMI improves social goal attainment, emotional-support preference, donation amounts, and buyer negotiation margins over conversational baselines with and without thinking. A Qwen ablation further shows that TMI outperforms ordinary conversation with retained reasoning on all four primary outcomes. Behavioral analyses associate the improvements with task-specific patterns in initial proposals and responses to interaction feedback. Alongside these gains, TMI reduces mean reasoning tokens per decision by 42.0-81.5% relative to the thinking baseline and lowers mean cross-turn phrase reuse across all eight model-environment pairs. These findings show that interaction organization shapes both goal attainment and reasoning across dialogue turns.

papers.title: A Deterministic O(log m)-Competitive Algorithm for Online Minimum Cost Bipartite Matching with Delays
papers.abstract: In the online Minimum cost Bipartite Perfect Matching with Delays (MBPMD) problem, $m$ requests and $m$ servers arrive over time in a metric space. An online algorithm has to match each request to a server and can postpone a matching decision by paying the delay cost. The objective is to minimize the total distance and delay cost. Azar, Chiplunkar, and Kaplan gave a randomized $O(\log n)$-competitive algorithm for metric spaces with $n$ points that are known in advance. For deterministic algorithms, however, the best known competitive ratio in general metric spaces was $O(m^{0.59})$, due to Azar and Jacob-Fanani. On the line, Kuo proposed the Virtual Robust Matching (VRM) algorithm and showed that it is $O(\sqrt{m}\log^2 m)$-competitive. We prove that VRM is $O(\log m)$-competitive for the MBPMD problem in any metric space. VRM is deterministic and does not need to know the metric space or $m$ in advance. It is the first deterministic polylogarithmic-competitive algorithm for the MBPMD problem in general metric spaces. Unlike the previous analysis of VRM, our analysis does not rely on a geometric decomposition of the metric space. Instead, it charges the waiting time of requests over time to the edges of a fixed optimal matching. We also extend VRM to the non-bipartite version and prove that the resulting deterministic algorithm is $O(\log m)$-competitive. This improves the $O(\log^5 m)$ bound of Dufay and Wattenhofer and matches a concurrent result of Ahmadian, Chawla, Kumar, Purohit, and Zhang. The proof that VRM is $O(\log m)$-competitive and its non-bipartite extension were found by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) with almost no human input. We used Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) to simplify and present the results. See the AI Usage and Methodology section for details. We take full responsibility for this paper.

papers.title: Short Paper No. 1: Relation between integer sequence A319433 and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs
papers.abstract: This short paper presents the interesting relation between integer sequence A319433 in https://oeis.org and the maximum degrees of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$ where $n = 1,2,3,\dots$. The result first appeared as a conjecture. Subsequently, a proof through AI-assisted mathematical reasoning came to the fore. Appropriate clarity remarks follow in the main text. It appears that $\textit{Golden ratio}$-like floor function plays an important role in the analysis of the graph structural properties of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs.

papers.title: A resident-traveller model for global aspects of vaccination
papers.abstract: A model for the spread of a vaccine-preventable infectious disease is set in a resident-traveller metapopulation context to investigate global aspects of vaccination. Of particular interest here is the effect of varying vaccine coverage in some patches on the spread of disease in the whole system. Analytically and numerically, the resident-traveller framework is compared with a classic metapopulation model where individuals become residents of the patch they move to. A numerical example inspired by the 2003--2004 poliomyelitis resurgence in western and central Africa is then considered, illustrating how heterogeneous vaccine coverage can sustain widespread regional transmission that classic metapopulation models predict to be much smaller.

papers.title: Counting Nilpotent Galois extensions with prescribed genus number
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a nontrivial finite nilpotent group. In this paper, we study the distribution of genus numbers of Galois extensions of $\Q$ with Galois group isomorphic to $G$, ordered by absolute discriminant. We show that the proportion of fields with any prescribed genus number tends to zero, and obtain a quantitative bound for this proportion. Moreover, if every element of order $\ell$ in $G$ is central, where $\ell$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, we determine the orders of magnitude of the average genus number and its higher moments.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
papers.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.

papers.title: Text-Assisted Event Stream Visual Place Recognition via Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Benefiting from the high dynamic range, high temporal resolution, and low energy consumption of event cameras, low-altitude economic research leveraging event cameras has become a popular topic. Several existing attempts introduce natural-language descriptions into visual place recognition (VPR) to mitigate the sparsity of structural spatial information inherent to event cameras. Nevertheless, these methods still fail to fully address two core challenges: effectively encoding event streams and semantically aligning event streams with text. In this paper, we propose a multi-scale spatial-temporal optimal transport approach, MSTOT-EPR, to address these challenges. Specifically, given event streams and scene text information, we first adopt a visual encoder and a text encoder to extract respective feature representations. We then apply optimal-transport constraints to achieve cross-modal alignment. We then design a cross-modal bottleneck fusion module to further fuse bimodal features. Furthermore, we develop multi-scale spatial optimal transport and inter-frame temporal optimal transport modules to mine high-quality spatial-temporal event features for scene recognition. Extensive experiments on the NYC-Event-VPR and EPRBench datasets fully validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework for event-based VPR. The source code of this paper will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title: Generative Modeling with Continuous Flows: Sample Complexity of Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion-based generative modeling, offering a continuous-time ordinary differential equation formulation with fast sampling and a simple regression-based training objective. Despite its empirical success, some theoretical analyses idealize the learning procedure by assuming that the velocity field is obtained by exact empirical risk minimization. This assumption does not reflect the practical finite-dataset setting, where the empirical flow-matching loss is only approximately minimized by a finite number of stochastic-gradient updates. We develop an empirical-risk-minimizer-free analysis for flow matching that explicitly accounts for both finite-sample statistical error and finite-time empirical optimization error. Our analysis considers a finite dataset of \(N\) flow-matching samples and a learned parameter \(θ_T\) obtained after \(T\) stochastic gradient updates on the empirical objective. Under regularity assumptions on the interpolation path, sub-exponential source and target distributions, approximation by a bounded-parameter smooth neural velocity class, empirical-loss optimization, and uniform flow stability, we prove a guarantee that holds with high probability over the finite training dataset and in expectation over the stochastic-gradient randomness. The resulting bound separates approximation error, statistical error from the finite dataset, tail error from unbounded source and target distributions, and empirical optimization error from approximate minimization of the finite-sample objective.

papers.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
papers.abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

papers.title: A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization
papers.abstract: In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros. The criterion contains the full positive Krawtchouk range and the dual $q$-Krawtchouk arrays, and through a quadratic decomposition of symmetric finite systems it covers Szwarc's quadratic system $Q_n$ in its sharp range $0<p_0\leq1/2$. As a limit to any such criterion, property (P) fails at coefficient distance $O((1-r^2)^N)$ from the Krawtchouk array of size $N$ with fixed ratio $c_i/d_i=r<1$. All theorems, corollaries and propositions are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Finite-Time Online Sample Complexity for Conditional Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: We study the finite-time training and sampling error of conditional diffusion models trained by online stochastic-gradient denoising score matching. Rather than assuming access to an exact empirical or population risk minimizer, we analyze the score network produced after a finite number of stochastic-gradient updates under an explicit localized Polyak--Łojasiewicz (PL) condition, stochastic-gradient regularity, and a trajectory-containment assumption. Our analysis separates the network approximation complexity from the online training-sample budget and propagates both errors through the reverse diffusion process. Under anisotropic smoothness, a joint intrinsic-dimensional structure for the data and conditioning variables, sub-exponential tails, and explicit approximation-class compatibility, we obtain a conditional score approximation error of order \[ \widetilde{\mathcal O}\!\left(M^{-η_{\mathrm{app}}}\right), \qquad η_{\mathrm{app}} = \frac{2α_x} {2α_x+d_x'+(α_x/α_y)d_y'}, \] where \(M\) denotes the approximation complexity, \(d_x'\) and \(d_y'\) are the intrinsic response and conditioning dimensions, and \(α_x,α_y\) are their corresponding smoothness exponents. For \(N=RB\) online denoising samples used by SGD, the finite-time optimization error is controlled explicitly in terms of the PL, smoothness, gradient-noise, and initialization constants. Combining these ingredients with reverse-process stability yields a total-variation bound that decomposes into terminal-initialization, time-discretization, approximation/localization, and finite-time optimization errors.

papers.title: \textsc{ChatDify}: Automating End-to-End Dify Workflow Synthesis from Natural Language via Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract: The proliferation of Large Language Models has catalyzed powerful application development platforms like Dify, which enable users to build sophisticated LLM-powered workflows through modular node orchestration. However, manually configuring these workflows requires deep platform expertise and remains time-consuming and error-prone, creating a significant barrier for non-expert users. To address this challenge, we propose \textsc{ChatDify}, a novel multi-agent framework that automates end-to-end Dify workflow synthesis from natural language descriptions. \textsc{ChatDify} employs an Actor-Critic architecture comprising three specialized agents: the \textit{Planner Agent} that decomposes user requests into structured execution plans, the \textit{Executor Agent} that performs context-aware parameter synthesis and schema-augmented DSL compilation, and the \textit{Reviewer Agent} that ensures reliability through hybrid verification with closed-loop refinement. We evaluate \textsc{ChatDify} on a curated benchmark of 100 production-inspired tasks across three state-of-the-art LLM backends, achieving 0.96, 0.91, and 0.75 success rates with Qwen-3.7, GLM-5.1, and DeepSeek-v4, respectively. These results demonstrate its robustness and practical applicability for lowering the technical barrier to creating sophisticated LLM applications.

papers.title: Meta-memorization and memorization scaling laws in transformers
papers.abstract: Larger transformers can memorize more data, with a capacity (in bits) that scales roughly linearly with the number of parameters. Counterintuitively, larger models also memorize faster, requiring fewer repetitions of a sequence during training before it is memorized. We reproduce both memorization scaling laws in transformers trained on random binary sequences, showing that rapid memorization can arise even when data contain no semantic or compositional structure. Rapid memorization is due to a meta-memorization effect, where models trained to memorize a large set of random sequences learn to memorize novel sequences more quickly. The rate $r(t)$ at which models memorize grows with training time $t$ as a power-law $r(t) \sim t^β$ with a fixed exponent $β$ but an increasing upper cutoff across model scales. Meta-memorization enables even one-layer transformers to few-shot memorize a 100-bit sequence. This effect is partly explained by the formation of structured attention heads that convey position-invariant sequence information to MLPs where memorized sequences are stored. Meta-memorization is recapitulated in a simplified model of a dense associative memory where retrieval is constrained by an attentional bottleneck. Our results suggest transformers, through pre-training, acquire reusable mechanisms that enable highly efficient storage and retrieval of memories.

papers.title: Beyond Validation Loss: Coverage and Reliability Dynamics in Robot Policy Pretraining
papers.abstract: In modern robot learning, generative robot policies are first pretrained through supervised learning from demonstrations, then refined through reinforcement learning, supervised finetuning, or other forms of posttraining. Yet conventional pretraining metrics, such as validation loss and average task success, provide an incomplete account of which policies support both effective direct deployment and subsequent posttraining. In this work, we study closed-loop pass@k, which evaluates the probability that k rollouts from the same initial condition attain at least one success. Thus, pass@1 measures mean task success; large-k pass@k measures whether success remains reachable under repeated sampling. Across a wide range of posttraining recipes, we show that large-k pass@k reveals posttraining differences not captured by pass@1. In particular, checkpoints with similar pass@1 but different large-k pass@k have different posttraining performance. Moreover, we show pass@k peaks at different checkpoints during supervised pretraining, revealing a coverage-reliability tradeoff over the course of training. Based on these observations, we propose two practical interventions: (1) a purely offline checkpoint-selection criterion that balances coverage and reliability without closed-loop evaluation, and (2) a generative data augmentation procedure that expands supervision beyond the finite demonstration set, preserving large-k pass@k while maintaining or improving pass@1 and raising the observed coverage-reliability Pareto frontier. Together, our results motivate evaluation, checkpoint selection, and training procedures that explicitly account for posttraining. Blog post, visualizations, and code are available at https://zhanyisun.github.io/robot-policy-learning-dynamics/.

papers.title: Principled Human-AI Collaboration in Agentic Workflows
papers.abstract: Organizations adopting AI face the challenge of deciding which outputs can be released without human review while meeting the quality standards of human experts. We develop a statistical framework for delegating tasks between experts and black-box generate-verify workflows, in which AI-generated answers are verified and revised over multiple rounds. Before deployment, human experts evaluate selected outputs, and their judgments are used to calibrate the verifier threshold and number of attempts. Our method selects the policy with the highest estimated automation rate among statistically approved candidates, without modifying the generator or verifier. We establish finite-sample control of the error rate among released outputs, characterize the expert evaluations sufficient to attain a target automation rate, and derive a minimax lower bound establishing rate optimality in the quality margin and required confidence. In a MultiHiertt financial question-answering case study, average held-out automation increases from 2.50% to 24.17% as expert evaluations accumulate, while released-output error rates remain around 1.20%. In contrast, heuristics that release answers after consistently high verifier scores either violate the 5% error tolerance or automate at most 1.30% of tasks. Synthetic experiments further examine these theoretical predictions under controlled settings.

papers.title: A sphere-product counterexample to the additivity of homology nilpotency
papers.abstract: Homology nilpotency need not increase under a product with a sphere. We construct a simply connected, closed smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $53$, rationally elliptic with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(π_*(M)\otimes\mathbb Q\bigr)=7$, such that $cat_0(M)=10$ and $Hnil(M\times S^2)=Hnil(M)=11$. The inequality $Hnil(X\times Y)\leq Hnil(X)+Hnil(Y)$ can therefore be strict even for a product of a closed manifold with $S^2$ as the second factor.

papers.title: Search-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sibling Alignment for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation retrieves items by autoregressively generating semantic IDs, typically via beam search. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enhances training supervision by transferring privileged self-teacher knowledge at student-generated states. However, beam-search retention depends on competition among prefixes: visited states differ in importance, and initially reliable decisions may approach the pruning boundary as training evolves. Moreover, conventional distribution matching couples target-token confidence with preferences among competing continuations, potentially weakening relational supervision when the self-teacher strongly favors the target. To address these challenges, we propose Search-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation (SA-OPSD), a framework that transfers privileged self-teacher knowledge to the states visited during the student's own beam search. Specifically, we introduce Evolving-Boundary Sampling, which prioritizes search-critical states by considering both current pruning-boundary proximity and initial-reference retention-margin decline under a controlled distillation budget. Furthermore, we develop Confidence-Decoupled Branch Distillation, which separates target-probability calibration from informative sibling relations to better preserve the teacher's preferences among competing branches. Experiments on Industrial, Office, and Instruments demonstrate strong performance for SA-OPSD.

papers.title: A logarithm-free subexponential algorithm for minimum quartet inconsistency
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for complete, unweighted minimum quartet inconsistency (MQI) with time and space $2^{O(k^{1/4})}+n^{O(1)}$, where $n$ is the number of taxa and~$k$ is the allowed number of quartet disagreements. This removes the logarithmic factor from the exponent of the MQI bound announced in 2009. The algorithm combines low-error anchoring, chromatic coding, and dynamic programming that accounts for disagreements with all input quartets, with a refined count of colorings and merging states. We also record a generic ETH-based lower bound. The optimality of the fourth-root exponent remains open.

papers.title: Fredholm approximations to the Bethe-Salpeter equation with spherical-Bessel kernels for Wannier-Mott excitons
papers.abstract: We develop a deterministic radial approximation to the static Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE), designed for rapid preliminary screening of Wannier-Mott exciton binding across direct-gap bulk materials. The approximation replaces the electron-hole transition problem by small radial eigenvalue problems that require no stochastic sampling. Starting from the four-point BSE and its matrix representation in a Bloch electron-hole basis, we retain one valence and one conduction band in the effective-mass limit within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation. We introduce a central projection of the screened direct interaction and omit bare electron-hole exchange. The resulting model applies to spatially extended excitons whose envelopes vary slowly on the scale of the unit cell, provided that the effective-mass description and central screened interaction adequately represent the exciton of interest. A partial-wave decomposition separates the angular-momentum channels and expresses their interaction kernels as spherical-Bessel transforms of the real-space screened Coulomb interaction. Nyström discretization produces real symmetric radial matrices suitable for standard eigensolvers. Their dimension is set by the radial grid independently of the Brillouin-zone sampling used to calculate screening. We implement the formulation in the all-electron, full-potential code $\texttt{exciting}$. For bulk GaAs, the compact radial problem reproduces the corresponding conventional matrix-BSE binding energy within $(1~\mathrm{meV})$ at matched sampling. Further refinement achieves finite-mesh stability within the same tolerance on denser screening meshes without increasing the radial matrix size.

papers.title: $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ Proves the Collapse of the Intersection Principles Hierarchy
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the pairwise intersection principle ($2\mathrm{IP}$) implies, over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, the existence of a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to every given set. Together with the known implications, this yields the equivalence over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ of the finite intersection principle (FIP), $2\mathrm{IP}$, and $1$-GEN. In fact, FIP is equivalent to $n\mathrm{IP}$ for every fixed $n\geq 2$. These results give affirmative answers to Questions~1 and~2 of Cholak, Downey, and Igusa, and to Question~9.10.26 of Dzhafarov and Mummert. The proof uses cumulative, nested supports satisfying a finite Helly property and a decoding argument based on a least selected label. Neither $Σ^0_2$ induction nor $Σ^0_2$ bounding is required.

papers.title: Impossible Code, Barely Changed Score: A Replay Study of Judge-Based Evaluation
papers.abstract: Language models are often used to judge generated code without running it. A useful evaluation should reveal substantial changes in the answers it scores. We examine this requirement by repeating an earlier evaluation on 421 coding problems, comparing Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct with two versions trained using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). One receives rewards from execution tests (CE-trained), and the other from a strong language-model judge (SLJ-trained). The base model's syntax-failure rate remains stable, but the trained checkpoints produce invalid Python on 63%-67% of attempts. Despite this change, the strong judge's Pass@32 scores fall by only about 3 percentage points, from 96.67% to 93.95% for SLJ-trained. Within the later run, allowing more attempts makes the base and trained checkpoints look increasingly similar under the judge. With 128 attempts per question, the judge accepts at least one SLJ-trained answer on 96.44% of problems, compared with 28.27% under execution tests. We recommend reporting the share of answers that pass Python's syntax check alongside every judge-based score. This check requires no tests or code execution and flags invalid answers that the judge accepts, although it cannot establish functional correctness. Our findings show how a high judge-based score can hide substantial output damage and motivate checking an evaluation's sensitivity to change. Project page and code: https://curiousorbitnotes.github.io/evorobust-replay-audit/

papers.title: Spend the Bits Where the Tiny Objects Are: Rate-Utility Region Coding for Aerial Detection
papers.abstract: Bandwidth-limited aerial cameras must compress their images before a remote detector can find the many tiny objects in them. Threshold-based region-of-interest (ROI) coding sends only confidently detected regions, and because tiny objects provide limited visual evidence and often score low, it can discard the regions that contain them. We propose rate-utility region coding (RUO), which sends a region when its expected detection utility justifies its measured byte cost, choosing to drop it or to send it at low or high quality with one multiplier shared across images. RUO trains no model, uses a standard image codec and decodes in a few milliseconds. On all 1,610 VisDrone-DET test-dev images, RUO uses 42.4% fewer bits than a tuned threshold-based ROI coder, averaged over their shared tiny-object average precision (AP) range. RUO also needs fewer bits for tiny objects than the AV1 Image File Format (AVIF), High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) and three published learned codecs, and its advantage over threshold-based ROI coding persists when the sender and receiver use different detectors. For AP over all object sizes RUO needs 25.4% more bits than the tuned ROI coder, because its allocation drops large regions first at low rates, so it suits tasks that target tiny objects. We plan to release the code.

papers.title: Exact solution of the dynamic pseudogap model: Fock-space formalism for Gaussian fluctuations
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution of the dynamic finite-$Q$ pseudogap model, in which electrons scatter between two nested Fermi-surface patches off a classical Gaussian order-parameter field with characteristic frequency $ω_0$ and damping $γ$. The disorder-averaged Green's function is shown to be a single matrix element of the resolvent of a sparse non-Hermitian matrix acting on a Fock space of two (commensurate fluctuations) or four (incommensurate fluctuations) bosonic modes with complex energies. The non-commutativity of the pseudospin vertices at different times, which prevented an exact treatment so far, is retained in full. We derive the representation, its symmetries, and the exact limits it contains: the static continued fractions, the closed-form commensurate solution at the Fermi surface, and the second-order self-energy. A numerically exact implementation gives spectral functions and densities of states for all values of the fluctuation frequency, damping and electron energy. We find that the sideband comb of the spectral function stays close to multiples of $ω_0$ and that quasiparticle damping is governed by an energy-dependent decoherence rate. At resonance of a quasiparticle energy with $ω_0/2$, we obtain the static fuctuating-gap in a rotating frame, which leads to resonant splitting of the quasiparticle peak.

papers.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -Δu+u=λu\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<λ<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.

papers.title: 1-Genericity Is Not Weihrauch Reducible to the Finite Intersection Principle
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the problem of producing a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to a given oracle is not Weihrauch reducible to the finite intersection principle (FIP). More strongly, no nontrivial computable FIP instance admits a single Turing functional that produces an absolute $1$-generic real from every enumeration of every maximal centered set of indices. The argument combines a $1$-generic real that computes no perfect tree all of whose paths are $1$-generic with local constancy and a parametrization of maximal centered sets. This answers Question~9.10.25 of Dzhafarov and Mummert.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Edge Mappings of Graphs
papers.abstract: The study of extremal problems for set mappings was initiated by Erdős and Hajnal in 1958. Alon and Caro, and later Caro, Patkós, Tuza and Vizer, studied related problems for edge mappings of graphs. For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $g_0(G)$ be the minimum integer $N$ such that every mapping $f:E(K_N)\to E(K_N)$ satisfying $f(e)\cap e=\varnothing$ for every $e\in E(K_N)$ admits a copy $G^*$ of $G$ in $K_N$ with $f(e)\notin E(G^*)$ for every $e\in E(G^*)$. Gishboliner, Jin and Sudakov conjectured that $g_0(G)=O(n+m/\sqrt n)$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by constructing a family of graphs. We then prove that $g_0(G)=O(n+m^{3/4})$. Furthermore, for every $n\ge2$ and $m$ satisfying $\lceil n/2 \rceil\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}$, there exists a graph $G_*$ with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and no isolated vertices satisfying $g_0(G_*)=Ω(n+m^{3/4})$. Thus the upper bound is best possible in terms of $n$ and $m$.

papers.title: Recoverability-Aware Evaluation of Diffusion Video Inpainting and Object Removal
papers.abstract: Video inpainting for object removal is scored over the whole hole, although the background behind the object is visible in other frames of the shot for some hole pixels and in no frame for others. A whole-hole score therefore mixes copying with generation and cannot show which of the two a remover does well. To separate the two, we propose recoverability-stratified evaluation, in which a point tracker run on the clean video labels each hole pixel by whether and how far away it is observed, so that fidelity and temporal stability can be reported per stratum against a copy reference. To reuse the observed content, we also propose evidence-guided sampling (EGS), which blends tracked colors into the clean-latent prediction of a video diffusion remover without training. On DAVIS, the perceptual advantage of three diffusion removers over flow propagation shrinks where the content is visible a few frames away (LPIPS difference-in-differences +0.046 to +0.056 against E2FGVI-HQ), and real paired captures show the same pattern for two of them. Their DAVIS hole warping error is two to four times that of ProPainter, and copying along clean-video tracks lowers their recoverable LPIPS by a quarter to two fifths. EGS closes 43% and 56% of the gap to this copy reference on held-out DAVIS when its colors come from clean-video tracks. With colors tracked on the masked input, a pre-registered confirmation finds no gain on MiniMax-Remover and a loss on ROSE. Diffusion removers thus leave observed content unused on DAVIS, and training-free reuse does not yet hold with tracked evidence.

papers.title: Spontaneous Geometric Structures in 2D MHD Flows
papers.abstract: Under suitable spatial decay assumptions on the initial data, we establish precise asymptotic expansions of the velocity and magnetic fields for two-dimensional incompressible MHD flows at each positive time. We identify in the far-field profile the hexagonal pattern previously discovered for the 2D Navier-Stokes equations by L. Brandolese \cite{Bra22}, characterized by six equally spaced directions of faster decay for each component of $u(x,t)-u_0(x)$. Surprisingly, the corresponding contribution to the magnetic field vanishes identically, owing to an exact cancellation associated with the antisymmetric structure of the magnetic nonlinearity. Thus, at order $|x|^{-3}$, the hexagonal structure appears only in the velocity field.

papers.title: foraois: Fast, Flexible Extended Press-Schechter Merger Trees with a General First-Crossing Solver
papers.abstract: We present foraois (Gaelic for Forest; FAW-reesh), an open-source Python framework for generating Monte Carlo dark matter halo merger tree histories. foraois separates the description of the linear density field, the physics of halo collapse, and the algorithmic construction of halo merger histories, allowing different cosmologies, collapse prescriptions, and tree building approaches to be combined within a common framework. The package implements two approaches to the same merger-tree problem of sampling progenitor masses in the excursion-set picture: the semi-empirical algorithm of Parkinson, Cole, & Helly (2008), which applies a fitted correction to the EPS progenitor distribution, and the numerical solution of the Markovian first-crossing equation developed by Zhang & Hui (2006), which for the default real-space top-hat window is an approximation to the correlated-walk problem. Linear matter power spectra for Cold, Warm, and Fuzzy Dark Matter (CDM, WDM, and FDM) can be supplied, while the modular collapse treatment provides an extension point for alternative barrier models. The framework also supports constrained merger histories based on the Brownian-bridge construction of Nadler et al. (2023). We run extensive validation and scaling tests, and also show an illustrative example of coupling foraois to a light-weight semi-analytical model of galaxy formation.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Exoskeleton Assistance Policies through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback
papers.abstract: To reduce reliance on manual design and extensive parameter tuning, a framework for the autonomous evolution of exoskeleton assistance policies through human feedback is proposed. Assistance policies are autonomously generated as executable control code by an intelligent agent and evaluated in experiments with human participants. Subjective user feedback, movement performance, and muscle activation measurements are incorporated into policy assessment. Based on these assessments, policy deficiencies are autonomously identified and the control code is revised by the agent for subsequent trials. A closed loop of policy generation, human feedback, evaluation, and autonomous refinement is thereby established. The framework is evaluated using GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, and Kimi, and initial assistance performance and refinement outcomes are compared across models. Despite differences in initial performance, effective assistance is achieved with all four models after a single autonomous refinement iteration under the tested conditions. Across three tasks, biceps and triceps muscle activation levels are reduced by 29.4% and 35.2%, respectively, compared with those measured without an exoskeleton. However, limited adaptability to unexpected situations is observed, indicating that further improvements in robustness and safety are required.

papers.title: Measuring User Success in Randomized Search Experiments: Interpreting Good Abandonment in Generative AI Search
papers.abstract: Randomized search experiments increasingly evaluate experiences in which large language models answer information needs directly on the results page. Click status alone cannot identify success: a click may lead to an unsatisfactory result, while no click may indicate successful answer consumption, or "good abandonment." Prior research has shown that good abandonment is difficult to detect because dwell, scrolling, and reformulation are meaningful only in context. We present Session Success Rate (SSR), a human-grounded, interpretable outcome metric designed for online controlled experiments. Trained judges label complete session experiences using privacy-protected interaction evidence and video recordings; these offline labels train models scored online from query events, viewport behavior, result-page interactions, and semantic reformulations. Out-of-sample evaluation on 6,904 labeled queries yields 0.75 balanced accuracy overall and 0.68 within abandoned queries; session-level balanced accuracy is 0.68. The sample shows why interaction status is not an adequate outcome: 53.2% of abandonments were successful and 6.5% of clicked queries were unsuccessful. In a validation portfolio of seven ranking and five non-ranking experiments, SSR agreed with Sessions per User in seven cases, was inconclusive in four, and disagreed in one under a common p < 0.05 rule. Separately, across approximately 4,000 production experiments, SSR produced about 2.5 times the binary sensitivity of Sessions per User; in the studied workflow, this supported lower traffic allocations and greater experiment throughput under a fixed traffic budget.

papers.title: Second-Order Asymptotics for the Scalar Gaussian Broadcast Channel
papers.abstract: This paper characterizes the second-order coding region of the scalar Gaussian broadcast channel along the curved boundary of its capacity region. The characterization holds under both average and maximal error criteria and allows correlation between the receiver noises. At each interior point of this boundary, the second-order region is a halfspace, as in the work of Scarlett and the author on Gaussian multiple-access channels with degraded message sets. Achievability follows from spherical superposition coding with a blocklength-dependent power allocation. The main innovation lies in the converse. Using Ornstein--Uhlenbeck entropy dissipation and Gaussian functional inequalities, we construct an auxiliary observation through an additive Gaussian noise channel and establish quantitative relative entropy bounds for the channel output distributions conditioned on this observation. The strong functional representation lemma of Li and El Gamal then allows us to select a realization of its independent random seed to obtain a deterministic partition of the retained receiver-1 message set. The component label plays a role analogous to the auxiliary random variable in the capacity characterization, while providing the distributional control needed at the second-order scale. These properties guide the construction of auxiliary output measures whose likelihood ratios admit the cancellations and normal approximation needed to evaluate an information spectrum converse.

papers.title: Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem
papers.abstract: Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $σ$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $σ/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.

papers.title: StateGate: A Behavioral-Fidelity Prompt Optimization Method for Long-Chain LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Currently, long-chain LLM agents commonly suffer from behavioral degradation in complex tasks, where prompts are written in full but steps are not executed in full. To address this issue, existing approaches face three major challenges. First, constraints are strongly bound to their textual carriers; once natural-language constraint sentences are removed, their binding force vanishes. Second, the execution process lacks independent verification, as the evidence for judgment is often supplied by the executing party itself, leading to the failure of self-referential validation. Third, existing remediation schemes are difficult to generalize, and hard-coded mechanisms cannot be transferred across tasks. In this paper, we propose StateGate, a novel prompt-optimization scheme that transforms semantic constraints into symbolic gates enforced by an external deterministic runtime. By decoupling the content of a constraint from its carrier of efficacy, StateGate achieves behavioral fidelity in long-chain tasks without losing the binding force of the prompt. Specifically, we first propose four independent compression strategies (deduplication, generalization, externalization, and text-to-gating) together with their corresponding decision chains, enabling principled prompt symbolization. Second, we design a three-component architecture consisting of a state file, a validator, and an orchestrator, which thoroughly separates judgment authority from execution authority. Third, we formally prove that the compliance of symbolic constraints is independent of context size. Finally, we validate the framework on a vulnerability-discovery task in the security domain; the results show that StateGate achieves 100% execution closure and accurate vulnerability detection.

papers.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
papers.abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

papers.title: Attack Patterns in Cross-chain Bridges: A Trust-based Empirical Analysis
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of multiple blockchain ecosystems has made cross-chain bridges essential for transferring assets and information across independent blockchains. Their multi-component architectures, cross-chain trust assumptions, and concentration of valuable assets expose them to diverse security threats. This paper presents an empirical study of cross-chain bridge attacks based on 48 evidence-supported real-world incidents from January 2022 to August 2026. We propose a behaviour-based attack pattern architecture comprising six trust-violation attack patterns, each defined by the primary trust assumption violated by the attacker: Proof Forgery,Logic Exploitation, Event Injection, Economic-State Manipulation, Credential Seizure, and Infrastructure Hijacking. The architecture further maps these patterns to five functional domains of cross-chain bridges: Deposit, Relay, Verification, Execution, and Governance and Operations, separating how a trust assumption is violated from where the compromised trust boundary lies. The 48 incidents correspond to $2.676 billion in gross bridge-specific losses, with the ten largest incidents accounting for 92.4% of total losses. Measured on the primary loss basis, Proof Forgery and Credential Seizure make up 86.2% of all losses, and the Verification and Governance and Operations domains hold 93.9%. A handful of very large incidents drives this concentration, yet it still holds when we switch to other loss bases or reclassify the boundary cases. By tying what attackers do to the bridge functions and security assumptions they target, the architecture gives threat modelling for cross-chain bridges an empirical footing.

papers.title: Contractable 2-connected subgraphs in minimally 3-connected graphs
papers.abstract: We study the 2-connected subgraphs of minimally 3-connected graphs whose contraction preserves 3-connectedness. We show that every minimally 3-connected graph that is not a wheel or a complete bipartite graph $K_{3,n}$ contains a contractable 2-connected induced subgraph that is a cycle, a fan, a $K_{2,n}$ or a $K_{3,n}$. In addition, these subgraphs satisfy certain degree restrictions. We show that none of these four families can be discarded since for each one of the four families, there exists a minimally 3-connected graph containing a contractable induced 2-connected subgraph in that family and none in the other three families. Reversing the contraction process gives a new construction for 3-connected graphs using edge addition, expansions into prescribed 2-connected subgraphs and $Y$-sum.

papers.title: Topping's diameter conjecture for immersed surfaces
papers.abstract: We resolve Topping's diameter conjecture for closed immersed surfaces in Euclidean three-space, building on his recent result for embedded surfaces. More generally, we establish sharp diameter and mean-width estimates for compact connected immersed surfaces, possibly with boundary. As a consequence, we confirm the codimension-one case of the sharp length--diameter conjecture for immersed minimal surfaces.

papers.title: 6G Uplink Waveform and Rank Selection under Distributed Reception
papers.abstract: The development of 6G uplink is expanding waveform and spatial transmission options, while distributed reception makes their relative merits depend on the spatial and frequency structure of the aggregate channel. We study the joint selection of cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing and discrete Fourier transform spread OFDM at rank 1 and noncoherent rank 2 under common user equipment power constraints and centralized linear minimum mean-square error reception. We derive waveform switching thresholds at both ranks and a rank selection margin, establishing conditions for selecting among the four modes based on available transmit power, DFT despreading loss, and spatial multiplexing gain. We then characterize how port gains and correlations at individual access points (APs) form aggregate spatial separation and influence mode selection. At fixed port gains and available transmit powers, improving spatial separation without reducing it on any subcarrier increases the rank selection margin, while its effect on the preferred waveform within rank 2 depends on the frequency distribution of the improvement. Numerical results show that different AP deployments can favor different waveforms and ranks, even with the same receive antenna budget and comparable aggregate channel gains, including waveform switches at a fixed preferred rank.

papers.title: Feynman--Kac Representation for Parabolic Equations with Memory: A New Class of BSDEs
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the connection between parabolic equations with memory (MPEs, for short) and backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short). To provide a probabilistic representation of MPEs, we introduce a new class of BSDEs, called BSDEs with memory (MBSDEs, for short). The main feature of MBSDEs is that, at the current time $s$, the generator depends not only on the current value $Y^{t,x}(s)\equiv Y^{s,X^{t,x}(s)}(s)$ but also on the future path $r\mapsto Y^{r,X^{t,x}(s)}(r)$, $r\in[s,T]$. This structure reveals a fundamental difference from classical BSDEs: in the classical setting, the time and space variables are coupled and inseparable, whereas in MBSDEs they are completely independent. We prove the well-posedness of these MBSDEs and show that their adapted solutions provide a probabilistic representation for the solutions of MPEs. Furthermore, under a monotonicity condition, we establish a comparison principle for one-dimensional MBSDEs, which enables us to develop a viscosity solution theory for MPEs. This generalizes the celebrated nonlinear Feynman--Kac formula of Peng [25] and Pardoux--Peng [22] to the case with memory, in both the classical and viscosity solution senses.

papers.title: Access Resources and Stability of Error-Correction Capabilities in Continuous Strategic Codes
papers.abstract: Continuous quantum error correction depends on which parts of a measurement record remain available to the controller at recovery. We study this temporal access using continuous strategic codes, formulated as open continuous process tensors contracted with causal instruments and conditional recovery. For monitored stabilizer codes, a common-optimal-correction criterion identifies when records can be merged without loss and yields a factorization for separated CSS inference. Terminal decision labels and causal persistent memory carry different costs: five persistent classical states reach the complete-record optimum in a finite-strength counting model, whereas its two-window diffusive counterpart has nine terminal decision labels and requires unbounded memory for exact causal recovery. Uniform lower and constructive upper bounds establish an optimal fidelity deficit of order $m^{-2}$ for $m$ persistent states in the diffusive model. Counting and diffusive stability bounds translate open-process approximation into guarantees for deployed-controller performance and retained access advantages, quantified by explicit quantizers and model-mismatch curves. The same process--instrument framework connects storage with persistent environments and irreversible noise to spacetime interrogation and record-selected paths for a logical $T$ gate. These results specify which record distinctions recovery needs, the memory cost of approximating them, and the logical protection retained under model error.

papers.title: Energy-Dissipative, High-Order BDF Schemes for Simulating Geometric Flows via Energy Increments
papers.abstract: We propose energy-dissipative backward differentiation formula (BDF) methods for geometric flows in the Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element framework. Starting from a Lagrange-multiplier formulation, we replace the multistep approximation of the energy derivative by an energy-increment equation while retaining the BDF geometric equations. The Simpson quadrature and two interleaved time grids provide third- and fourth-order constructions. The positive quadrature weights ensure stepwise decay of the original discrete geometric energy for every nondegenerate solution of the nonlinear system. We establish an explicit conditional consistency bound for the scalar energy equation and a regularity criterion for the Newton system of curve-shortening flows. Then, the proposed schemes extend to simulating curve diffusion, mean curvature flow, and surface diffusion. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate geometric accuracy, energy decay, good mesh distribution, and high performance of the proposed schemes.

papers.title: Autoencoder Based Deep Clustering of Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Motivated by a problem in Generative Specification-Producing AIs (SPAIs), we focus on a problem of deep clustering of three-dimensional shapes specified by point clouds. After reviewing clustering and deep clustering, we study the fully unsupervised pipeline in which a FoldingNet autoencoder is first trained for reconstruction and then K-means++ is then applied to the resulting codewords. We report clustering accuracy (ACC), normalized mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI) on ModelNet10 and ModelNet40 datasets, as a function of the number of clusters K. We also provide t-SNE visualizations of the codewords, and discuss the choice of K.

papers.title: Physically Motivated Stellar Populations for Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn with a Temperature-Dependent IMF
papers.abstract: The first few years of James Webb Space Telescope observations have identified previously undetected galaxies at $z>12$ and provided new constraints on galaxies at $z>8$. Many of these objects have stellar masses that are difficult to reconcile with $Λ$CDM, inferred from models not calibrated for the high-redshift Universe. This necessitates new, more astrophysically plausible stellar population models for estimating stellar masses of galaxies at cosmic dawn. We introduce a simple stellar population (SSP) library, Simple Stellar Populations with Temperature (SSPT), computed using a temperature-dependent stellar initial mass function and its implementation in the public code CIGALE. When used in a configuration designed for high-redshift galaxies that requires young stellar population ages, the new models predict stellar masses that are ~0.3-0.5 dex lower than estimates from similar CIGALE analyses using models calibrated to the local Universe, and nearly 2 dex lower than estimates from analyses using other codes and softer constraints on stellar ages. Application of these physically motivated stellar populations suggests that stellar masses of early star-forming galaxies are not in tension with $Λ$CDM, and that galaxy formation from virialized halos remains a reasonable hypothesis at the highest redshifts. The SSPT SSPs and their CIGALE implementation are released publicly.

papers.title: Orbital stability for the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For equivariance index $m\ge2$ and a potential $V\in C^{3,1}([0,2])$ satisfying $V(0)=V'(0)=0$, we first establish local well-posedness for the Cauchy problem at the $H^2$ level, with the sphere constraint written in the natural affine space $u-\vec n\in H^2$. For nonnegative $V$ we then consider an $m$--equivariant ground state of $H_ω=E+ωM$, $ω>0$. Under a constrained nondegeneracy condition for the polar Hessian, the conserved energy and mass give orbital stability in $H^1$. A Gustafson--Shatah type continuation argument, in which the Chern--Simons feedback is treated as a tame nonlocal zeroth-order perturbation, upgrades this conditional stability to global $H^2$ existence for all $H^2$ initial data sufficiently close to the ground state orbit in $H^1$. For the quadratic potential we also verify the nondegeneracy condition in a nonempty interior near-BPS regime approaching the self-dual point $(κ,ω)=(1,0)$. This yields a concrete family of globally defined orbitally stable ground states.

papers.title: Cutoff and a Gaussian-shift profile for the Rudvalis shuffle
papers.abstract: The Rudvalis shuffle removes the top card and reinserts it uniformly at random in one of the bottom two positions. Hildebrand proved the classical upper bound $O(n^3\log n)$, and Wilson later proved the sharp lower coefficient $1/(8π^2)$, establishing the correct order but leaving the leading upper constant, cutoff, and the cutoff profile open. We prove that the full labelled shuffle has total-variation cutoff at \[ \frac{n^3\log n}{8π^2} \] with a window of order $n^3$. The upper bound is obtained by writing one deterministic rotation of the shuffle as a nonnormal sweep of adjacent averaging projections, comparing that sweep to a weighted interchange generator, and controlling the entire regular-representation heat trace. The key sharp-window ingredients are heat-kernel smoothing through the Octopus Inequality, zero extension of deletion-harmonic ordered-tuple functions, a representation-theoretic multiplicity payment, and a sectorwise entrance estimate that disposes of all large Young-diagram deficits. For the profile, an exact complex one-card eigenfunction yields a deck statistic whose surviving first Fourier mode converges to a Gaussian shift. A matching full-deck $L^2$ bound then shows that this one-dimensional Gaussian likelihood ratio asymptotically exhausts all remaining information, giving the exact total-variation profile.

papers.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
papers.abstract: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair; second, because physical theories must interact with the real world, it uses computational physics as an executable testbed while separating the qualification of numerical instruments from scientific claim review so solvers and diagnostics can be adapted within a recorded investigation.
