A corrected comparison normalizes and enlarges candidate policy banks using validation-only price sweeps and retains all ten applicable sources. The source-level results do not establish a statistically significant average advantage over group-blind pricing at the fixed minimum retained loss capture. We also compare with blocked-count, blocked-value, and protected-loss parity postprocessors, which do not directly constrain realized objections, and measure objections in candidate-count and loss units.

papers.title: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache
papers.abstract: A causal video generator produces two key--value (KV) states for every segment: the KV it uses while denoising that segment, and the KV it writes into the cache for later segments to read. In a pretrained generator the two already differ substantially, later segments attend to them differently, and replacing the written KV with the generation KV degrades the continuation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV) to learn a dedicated memory representation from its future use: a writer-specific low-rank residual on the shared backbone separates memory writing from generation and is trained through the future reads of what it writes. Learning a write from its future use needs gradients through the cache, which the mutable cache in common use cannot provide. dKV Forcing replaces the training-time cache by persistent differentiable pages with local rematerialization and, in one temporal traversal, computes exactly the gradient that a two-pass reconstruction of the same objective computes. One traversal computes the full memory gradient at $7\%$ generator-update overhead over detached-write training, with $28\%$ less resident memory and $20.8\%$ shorter training cycles than the two-pass reconstruction. Over Self Gradient Forcing (SGF), the same objective trained with the same traversal, writer adaptation raises VBench-Long aesthetic quality by $6.6$ points at 60\,s and $8.5$ points at 240\,s with the highest subject and background consistency, and rollout dropout of the residual keeps most of this gain while restoring the motion of training without write gradients.

papers.title: Near-Optimal $\sqrt{K}$-Regret for Online Learning in Uninformed Markov Games
papers.abstract: We study online learning in two-player uninformed Markov games, where the opponent may follow an arbitrary, unknown policy in each episode and the learner does not observe the opponent's actions. [TWYS21] showed that achieving sublinear external regret requires an exponential dependence on the episode length $H$. Motivated by this limitation, they studied the weaker notion of Nash-value regret and obtained an $\widetilde{O}(K^{2/3})$ regret bound, where $K$ is the number of episodes. More recently, [LLZR26] introduced a stronger notion called empirical Nash-value regret and achieved an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{K})$ bound when the opponent's non-stationarity is moderate, including the case where the opponent follows a fixed policy. However, whether the $\sqrt{K}$ rate is achievable in the worst case remained open. In this paper, we resolve this open question by developing an algorithm that achieves $\widetilde{O}(H^{3/2}S\sqrt{AK})$ empirical Nash-value regret against arbitrary opponent policies, where $S$ is the number of states and $A$ is the number of learner's actions. Specifically, our algorithm combines global and local planning by maintaining a collection of candidate predictions of future losses, each associated with a policy. Global planning learns which candidates to favor across episodes, while local planning combines their policies differently at each state to make decisions. A key ingredient is to coordinate these two components to control the discrepancy between local loss estimates and the total loss of the executed policy, using only the learner's observed trajectories.

papers.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.

papers.title: Physics-Informed One-Step Generation on Long-short flow maps
papers.abstract: Physics-informed generative models should produce samples that are both data-aligned and physically valid, yet existing methods are often iterative and too slow for practical use. Achieving this with a one-step flow-map model is difficult because both data-distribution and physics-constraint learning are enforced only indirectly through surrogate objectives, making their joint learning fragile for long-range flow maps. We propose \textbf{Physics-Informed Long-Short Flow Maps with Direct Guidance (LSFM-DG)}, which makes direct target computation feasible by decomposing one-step generation into a long flow map for global evolution and a near-terminal short flow map with computable closed-form solutions and physics potentials. As the short flow map shrinks to zero, it provides both direct distributional and physical targets for learning the long flow map. This yields a unified one-step flow-map model that removes Jensen's gap, improves training stability, and achieves stronger data fidelity and physical consistency without distillation.

papers.title: EEG-HealthLLM: Hierarchical Adaptation of Large Language Models for Unified Heterogeneous EEG Health Assessment
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive means for neurological and mental health assessment, yet existing EEG models are typically developed for individual tasks and are difficult to unify across heterogeneous signal configurations and assessment objectives. Large language models (LLMs) offer a common interface for multiple tasks, but adapting heterogeneous EEG signals to a shared LLM raises a key challenge: how to preserve task-specific signal characteristics while enabling effective language-side parameter sharing. To address this problem, we propose EEG-HealthLLM, a unified and parameter-efficient framework for heterogeneous EEG health assessment. We introduce an Asymmetric Hierarchical Adaptation Strategy: task-specific EEG adapters preserve heterogeneous spatio-temporal dynamics, while a unified shared LoRA is injected into the LLM backbone (e.g., Phi-3) to capture shared high-level assessment semantics across tasks. We further establish EEG-HealthBench by reorganizing five existing EEG resources into paradigms covering epileptic seizure detection, major depressive disorder assessment, anxiety risk assessment, depressive symptom risk assessment, and emotional state assessment under a unified subject-independent protocol. Extensive experiments show that EEG-HealthLLM achieves an average balanced accuracy (BAC) of 69.58%, ranking first among the evaluated methods in both average BAC and macro-F1. Compared with independent single-task LoRA adaptation, it improves average BAC from 67.70% to 69.58% while reducing the aggregate language-side adapter footprint by 80.0%. Further analyses reveal task-dependent cross-task interactions and trade-offs, supporting the proposed hierarchical adaptation strategy. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/Marui-88/EEG-HealthLLM.

papers.title: An Unusually Clumpy Ultra-Diffuse Galaxy in the Coma Cluster: A Missing Link for Globular Cluster Formation?
papers.abstract: We present a study of Coma-B122, an unusually clumpy star-forming ultra-diffuse galaxy (UDG) in the Coma cluster outskirts, using deep Keck Cosmic Web Imager integral-field spectroscopy and Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam imaging. B122 hosts $\sim10$ luminous star-forming clumps contributing $\sim25$% of its luminosity and $\sim7$% of its stellar mass, with typical clump masses of $\sim10^6\ M_\odot$ comparable to the most massive super star clusters known in nearby starbursting dwarfs. The clumps form a distinctive ring configuration $\sim2$ kpc from the center. Full-spectrum fitting shows that $\sim12.5$% of the diffuse body's stellar mass formed during an extended episode of enhanced star formation over the past $\sim300$ Myr, within which all the clumps assembled. B122 shows evidence of weak ram-pressure stripping (RPS), including a diffuse light distribution truncated on the side facing the Coma center and extended to the opposite side, along with an asymmetric H I velocity profile. Its ordered stellar and ionized-gas rotation, cold gas fraction, and phase-space position are consistent with an early stage of infall. Spatial variations in clump star formation histories and gas-phase abundances further indicate that RPS-driven metal-poor gas inflow may have triggered and sustained the recent star formation. B122 may offer a rare present-day view of how UDGs assemble their globular cluster (GC) systems during cluster infall, although it remains uncertain if the clumps could survive as GCs. Future observations with higher spatial resolution and of more analogs are important to provide a complete picture of the formation and evolution of clumpy low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxies.

papers.title: Absolute descent and the Bénabou--Roubaud theorem
papers.abstract: We continue the programme developed in Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory by studying descent for augmented pseudocosimplicial objects. Let $\mathcal H$ be a $2$-category, and let $\operatorname{suc}=\mathsf{1}+(-)$ be the successor monad on the augmented simplex category. Precomposition with $\operatorname{suc}$ induces the décalage pseudomonad $\mathbb S$ on the $2$-category of augmented pseudocosimplicial objects with values in $\mathcal H$. We prove that every successor contraction makes the corresponding augmented pseudocosimplicial object effective for descent. This structure is preserved by postcomposition with every pseudofunctor. Consequently, the resulting descent object is an absolute bilimit. A first application concerns split epimorphisms. We recover the Janelidze--Tholen characterization of absolute effective descent morphisms given in Facets of Descent II. Moreover, we prove that one direction holds for every pseudofunctor $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, where $\mathcal H$ is an arbitrary $2$-category. Consequently, every $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra is of absolute descent. In particular, this holds for every free $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra, and hence for every one-sided décalage. This makes the shift-effectiveness hypothesis in the Bénabou--Roubaud theorem of Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory automatic. Thus, under the adjointness and Beck--Chevalley hypotheses, the descent and Eilenberg--Moore factorizations are equivalent whenever they exist. We thus obtain a stronger version of the Bénabou--Roubaud theorem for arbitrary augmented pseudocosimplicial objects, which we call the formal Bénabou--Roubaud theorem. Applied to indexed Čech objects associated with pseudofunctors $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, this theorem extends the classical Bénabou--Roubaud theorem to an arbitrary $2$-category $\mathcal H$.

papers.title: A Hybrid Anomaly Detection Method for Electric Vehicle Identification from Smart Meter Recordings
papers.abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles (EVs) have attracted much attention due to their potential to decarbonize the transport system. EV charging imposes challenges on power grids, such as load imbalance and voltage instability. Therefore, electricity distributors need to identify which users have an EV. Smart meter recordings can be effectively used for this purpose. The major issue associated with such data is the imbalance problem, where the majority of the data belongs to users without EVs. The existing methods for EV identification from smart meter recordings have framed it as a classification task. In this paper, we frame the problem as an unsupervised problem and propose a hybrid anomaly detection method that combines the power of prediction-based and reconstruction-based anomaly detection methods. The proposed model considers temporal and stochastic representation information of smart meter time series via prediction-based and reconstruction-based components, respectively. The performance of the proposed model is compared with state-of-the-art supervised and unsupervised methods. Its superiority is verified on real-world data.

papers.title: AIDA: An AI Outage Registry with Evidence from On-Chain MEV
papers.abstract: Generative AI coding tools have lowered the cost of writing trading software, but no systematic dataset records when these services fail. We introduce the AI Incident and Disruption Archive (AIDA), a multi-vendor registry of 5,868 deduplicated outage incidents across 30 providers from 2025 to 2026, with foundation-model incidents verified against primary status-page or postmortem URLs. Pairing AIDA with 5,041,034 verified maximal extractable value (MEV) transactions by 8,516 Ethereum addresses, their contract creations, and a 22-month Base Layer-2 panel of 1,099,593,191 swaps and 29,120 private executors, we establish two findings. First, entry into MEV expanded where code and public state suffice, as active arbitrage addresses quadrupled from late 2024 to late 2026 and liquidators grew by a third, while sandwich attackers, who need private order flow and builder access, declined. Execution nonetheless remained concentrated, with the top fifty addresses executing two thirds of verified trades. Second, AI outages stall new trading code while deployed bots keep trading. On Ethereum, addresses releasing a private executor fall to 0.67 on the day of an eight-hour disruption (0.68 for executor creations during OpenAI outage hours) and to 0.66 at lag two before rebounding on day three; on Base, operator top-level creations fall to 0.76 during OpenAI hours and executor-deploying operators to 0.88 at lag two. Non-trading creations, automated factory clones, and live arbitrage and sandwich execution across both chains remain unchanged. Cheaper code thus lowers the barrier to building MEV contracts, while private order flow, latency and capital still determine who wins execution.

papers.title: FiDeR: Denoising Astronomical Images at the Observational Resolution
papers.abstract: We present Finite-iteration Deconvolution--Reconvolution Denoising (FiDeR), a method for reducing noise in astronomical images while retaining approximately the input point-spread function (PSF). We first apply a finite number of Richardson--Lucy (RL) iterations to the nonnegative source-plus-background image. We then measure the response of a calibration point source processed with the same settings and derive a reconvolution kernel matched to the observational PSF. The calibration includes the background-to-source flux ratio. We compare FiDeR with six denoisers using simulated point-source and mixed stellar--galaxy fields, and observations from the James Webb Space Telescope Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) and Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI). In the stellar tests, bright-source widths remain close to the input widths; faint sources show small residual offsets. For the mixed field, FiDeR reaches peak signal-to-noise ratios of 46.701 and 44.850 dB at backgrounds of 10 and 20 counts per pixel, with wing errors of 0.657 and 0.858 counts. It also gives small aperture-flux and shape errors, although block-matching and three-dimensional filtering (BM3D) gives higher structural similarity. The NIRCam data show lower core and combined-region errors, while the three-exposure MIRI test gives benefits mainly in the stellar aperture and photometry. These results support substantial noise reduction with little change in the measured PSF within the tested regimes. The denoised images can provide inputs for further reconstruction and measurement; their uncertainties must account for residual noise correlations.

papers.title: Long-Time Behavior of Zero-Noise Mean-Field Adam
papers.abstract: Adaptive methods such as Adam are the most commonly used methods for training neural networks, but their long-time behavior is not as well understood as that of non-adaptive methods. This is particularly true in the mean-field limit, where the dynamics of infinitely many neurons are described as a distribution over parameters which satisfies a self-consistency condition. In this paper, we study a deterministic continuous-time model of Adam in the mean-field setting. Under a condition relating the averaging rates of the momentum and second-moment variables, the size of the gradients, and a regularization parameter, we prove that the distribution of parameters converges to the set of equilibria. This condition extends the range known for finite-dimensional models, and we show that it is sharp. Under an additional Lojasiewicz-type inequality for distributions, we prove that individual parameter trajectories converge and obtain quantitative rates for this convergence. We verify the qualitative convergence assumptions for a regularized two-layer neural network. We also show that adding noise to the momentum prevents the system from approaching these equilibria and rules out many free-energy type Lyapunov functionals. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate the energy estimates, give evidence of persistent oscillations outside the sufficient parameter range, and compare the observed decay with the predicted rates.

papers.title: HuG: Learning Humanoid Whole-Body Affordance-Aware Grasping with Active Perception
papers.abstract: Acquiring objects in human environments is hard for humanoids: targets are partially occluded under egocentric viewpoints, and reaching them demands coordinated whole-body motion that keeps the target visible and reachable while the base stays stable. We present HuG, a framework for whole-body affordance-aware grasping with active perception that couples perception and action through a Perceive-Align-Grasp pipeline: belief-driven active perception resolves occlusion by treating viewpoint as an explicit decision variable; a point-cloud-conditioned affordance policy proposes whole-body grasps; and an affordance-aware alignment stage repositions the body to the most executable configuration. A key insight is that, on a floating base, kinematic validity is not enough: we curate training data with controller-in-the-loop dynamics simulation, rejecting 73% of kinematically valid grasps that would destabilize the deployment controller, so the policy learns kinodynamically feasible affordances. Trained entirely in simulation with zero real demonstrations, HuG attains 87.5% real-world success on a multi-level shelf task, generalizes to novel objects, and holds at least 73% success at every tested height. Beyond generalizing within its training distribution, the policy extrapolates spatially: at scale in simulation it succeeds at table heights well below any seen during training, indicating that kinodynamically filtered synthetic data grounds affordances in object geometry and whole-body feasibility rather than in memorized configurations.

papers.title: Structural and Optical Properties of PVP-Modified ZnS Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
papers.abstract: Pristine and PVP-modified ZnS nanoparticles were investigated to examine how PVP addition affects structural, surface, optical, and methylene blue (MB) decolorization properties. X-ray diffraction confirmed cubic zinc-blende ZnS in all samples, with apparent Scherrer coherent-domain sizes of 3.10-3.31 nm. Electron microscopy revealed agglomeration, while HRTEM and electron diffraction confirmed locally crystalline regions in S1 and S4. The estimated direct Tauc gap decreased from 3.69 eV for S1 to 3.58 eV for S4. Between 100 and 300 K, the principal TO-like Raman band softened on heating, while visible photoluminescence changed predominantly within the overlapping green-yellow region. After 210 min under 254 nm irradiation, MB-band losses near 664 nm reached 19.33%, 58.18%, 70.00%, and 94.42% for S1-S4, compared with 6.58% for the catalyst-free control. PVP modification therefore alters optical and dye-decolorization responses while preserving the principal ZnS phase; however, dye-band attenuation alone does not establish complete mineralization.

papers.title: A Hybrid Anomaly Detection Method for Multivariate Time Series
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series are ubiquitous in monitoring smart systems such as power plants, smart houses, and servers. These systems use multiple sensors to collect the system's status over time. Those sensors represent the status of the whole system as one entity. Anomaly detection in such smart systems is of critical importance to prevent system failure and maintain functionality. But anomaly detection in such multivariate time series data is very challenging since this type of data includes both temporal and spatial information. Capturing both of these pieces of information is important to detect anomalies. In this paper, we propose a hybrid deep learning-based anomaly detection method, which captures both temporal and spatial information. We propose to take advantage of the feature extraction capabilities of 2d convolutional network in a variational autoencoder, alongside a prediction-based deep neural network of 2d convolutional networks and a gated recurrent unit network to capture both spatial and temporal information. Experiments on public data against state-of-the-art show the potential of our method.

papers.title: Holographic study of the scalar meson $K_0^*(1430)$ with dynamical longitudinal confinement
papers.abstract: Within the framework of light-front holographic QCD, where transverse confinement is inherently realized through holography, the structure and mass spectrum of the light scalar meson $K_0^{*}(1430)$ are investigated by employing the invariant mass ansatz and enhancing the model with a longitudinal confinement potential (specifically, the 't Hooft equation and the analytically solvable LMZV potential). The combined transverse and longitudinal confinement dynamics lead to more reliable calculations of key observables, including decay constants, parton distribution function, $ξ$-moments, and twist-$2$ and twist-$3$ distribution amplitudes. Transition form factors for the semileptonic decay $B \rightarrow K_0^{*} \ell^+ \ell^-$ are computed from these amplitudes, yielding predictions for differential branching ratios and longitudinal lepton polarization asymmetries as functions of $q^2$. The results are compared with other theoretical models, offering valuable insights into the non-perturbative dynamics of QCD. The predicted observables provide theoretically motivated benchmarks for future experimental investigations of $B\rightarrow K_0^*(1430)\ell^+\ell^-$ decays at LHCb and Belle II.

papers.title: GatedVLA with Camera-Based Emergency Braking: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
papers.abstract: This report presents GatedVLA, our entry for the Physical AI AV (PAI-AV) track. Our learned vision-language-action (VLA) policy pairs the driving-pretrained Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B vision-language model with a layer-wise flow-matching action expert that outputs a 2.5 s horizon of acceleration and curvature controls, augmented with a soft visual mask applied to the expert's cross-attention. Compared to an identically trained baseline, the masked policy achieves comparable overall open-loop error while reducing error on left turns. In local closed-loop evaluation across the same 150 scenes (two rollouts per scene), the visual mask increases the mean scene score from 0.479 to 0.517 (paired difference +0.038, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.018, +0.093], wins/losses 37/26, sign test p = 0.21). Incorporating a rule-based automatic emergency braking (AEB) module at deployment further increases the mean score to 0.599 (+0.082, CI [+0.023, +0.143]) and reduces the mean number of scenes with at-fault collisions from 34.0 to 11.0.

papers.title: Spectral Exactness and Quantitative Instability Approximation in the Euler-Zeitlin Model for Zonal Equilibria
papers.abstract: Building on finite-time convergence results for geometric matrix hydrodynamics, we establish global spectral exactness for Zeitlin's approximation of the two-dimensional Euler equation on the sphere linearized about polynomial zonal vorticities. By separating each azimuthal block into a skew-adjoint transport operator and a compact perturbation, we obtain a dimension-uniform estimate $\|K_N-K\|=O(N^{-1})$ and the sharper fixed-block estimate $\|K_{N,m}-K_m\|=O(N^{-2})$. These bounds, together with strong-resolvent convergence of transport, yield exact approximation of the isolated spectrum off the imaginary axis: algebraic multiplicities are preserved, Riesz projections converge in norm, and spurious off-axis spectral limits are excluded. Every algebraically simple off-axis eigenvalue has an $O(N^{-2})$ approximation error. For eigenvalues of higher multiplicity we establish second-order convergence of arithmetic means of eigenvalue clusters and $O(N^{-2/α})$ individual eigenvalue bounds, where $α$ is the maximal Jordan-block size. For any prescribed positive growth margin, the numbers of unstable and stable eigenvalues beyond that margin are eventually correct. The argument combines an exact matrix-harmonic coordinate recurrence, uniform bounds for high azimuthal modes, and resolvent factorizations involving compact operators. An explicit degree-three zonal equilibrium has a rigorously enclosed simple unstable eigenvalue, providing a concrete instance of the quantitative theory.

papers.title: Multirate Data-Driven Predictive Control: Rank Obstructions, Identifiability, and Noise Conditioning
papers.abstract: We develop rank, identifiability, and noise-conditioning results for compact input--output predictors in multirate data-driven predictive control. The inverse of a square zero-input response matrix used in an existing compact-lifting construction is shown to be undefined under its observability and minimal-polynomial assumptions. We derive exact replacements using rank-complete data, characterize all predictor extensions, and establish the minimum-norm and minimax Euclidean noise properties of the canonical Moore--Penrose extension. A joint predictor is identified directly from mixed experiments with arbitrary initial states. Deterministic perturbation bounds quantify reconstruction errors through informative singular-value margins, while a positive-definite reduced weighting preserves the nominal quadratic cost. Sampling-rate observability and event-triggering analyses identify additional conditions needed for reconstruction and stability guarantees.

papers.title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Design-Based Tests of Whether Biological World Models Use Actions
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly trained on data from randomized experiments, and whether their predictions respond to actions is usually checked by replacing or removing the actions and measuring the loss in accuracy. We show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see, and a better model learns the stand-in better. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model, provided the resampler conditions on the full state the design used; resampling from a simpler law reproduces the false effect. We identify a second failure, specific to world models: when many sites share one action sequence (cells in a microscope field, pixels in a frame), the natural pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into overwhelming evidence against a true effect. In a pixel world, its median log e-value fell from $-17.3$ to $-6832$ as frames grew from 64 to 4096 pixels, while the oracle's rose. Tempering the score by a design effect estimated on training data changes the bet, not the validity. Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed in exactly this way; a tempered statistic, selected on synthetic data and registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field ($E\approx 1.1\times10^{10}$). Every analysis is preregistered, fixed in a dated protocol before it was run, or labelled exploratory, and every reported result is generated from hashed result files.

papers.title: Generalized Principal Eigenvalues of Spatially Periodic Nonlocal Operators with Applications to Noncooperative KPP Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study generalized principal eigenvalues of the spatially periodic cooperative nonlocal operator $\mathcal{L}\boldsymbol{\varphi}=\mathcal{J}*\boldsymbol{\varphi} -\boldsymbol{\varphi}+A(x)\boldsymbol{\varphi}$ and their applications to noncooperative KPP systems. In the periodic setting, we characterize the existence of a classical principal eigenvalue and explicitly construct and classify Radon measure solutions to the associated eigenproblem when a positive continuous principal eigenfunction does not exist. On the whole space, we consider two notions of generalized principal eigenvalues defined through positive test functions and characterize them through a family of weighted periodic spectral values and Dirichlet approximations. For large spatial periods, we identify the spectral limits through a scalar Hamilton--Jacobi cell problem and, under additional assumptions, derive leading-order corrections and eigenfunction concentration results. For small spatial periods, we characterize the limits by an averaged operator and obtain refined expansions for specific classes of kernels, including formulas for the difference between the two whole-space generalized principal eigenvalues. Finally, we apply the spectral theory to establish extinction and persistence criteria for the associated noncooperative KPP systems, characterize spreading speeds along rays by a Freidlin--Gärtner-type formula, and study their asymptotic behavior as the spatial period tends to infinity or zero.

papers.title: Muography Simulations for Carbon Capture and Storage Monitoring
papers.abstract: Muography can monitor CO2 storage through reservoir density changes, but site-scale simulations are costly: reservoirs can be deep and borehole detectors are small. We address both with two approaches. First, a two-stage workflow splits the kilometer-scale simulation: a fast code transports muons through the overburden, and a general-purpose Monte Carlo code through the reservoir and detectors. Second, a geometric filter at the source keeps only muons whose direction and position let them reach the detectors, within a margin for multiple scattering, and a range cut removes those with too little energy. Both are available in the UCMuon simulation suite for muon generation, filtering and transport. At a deep (800-1000 m) and a shallow (65 m) CO2 storage site, each approach reduces the computing time about 700-fold, and the filtered simulation gives the same hit rate as a full one, as long as the margin exceeds the muons' sideways scattering drift.

papers.title: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
papers.abstract: GPTQ is Babai's nearest-plane algorithm on the lattice of the Cholesky factor of the layer's input second moment $Σ$. In the high-rate, entropy-coded regime it needs $\tfrac12\log_2(\AM/\GM)$ of its Cholesky pivots more bits than WaterSIC, which is within $0.255$ bit of the rate-distortion limit for every $Σ$; random rotations close most of this gap in practice, and Ordentlich and Polyanskiy asked for the worst-case gap between rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC. We show that after a Haar rotation the $k$-th pivot converges almost surely, uniformly in $k\geδn$ and over spectra $ν$ of bounded condition number, to $1/S_ν(-k/n)$, a classical formula from the theory of Lyapunov exponents, and use it to answer the question. Over spectra with condition number $κ$ the worst rotated gap is $\tfrac12\log_2κ-\log_2\lnκ+\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\ln2}+o(1)$ bits, attained only by two-point spectra, just $\tfrac12\log_2\lnκ+O(1)$ bits below the worst case without rotation, so rotation cannot replace waterfilling in general. It nearly can on real layers: rotation cuts the cost of an $η$-fraction of outlier eigenvalues of size $μ$ from about $ημ$ to $η^2μ/2$ to leading order, but cannot remove spectral spread on a logarithmic scale; for non-Gaussian weights it also adds a weight-side rate cost, which we characterize exactly under a standard high-rate assumption. On $96$ Hessians of Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 the rotated gap has median $0.04$ bit and maximum $0.36$ bit, against $2$--$5$ bits in the worst case for the same condition numbers, and the limit matches it to within $0.009$ bit.

papers.title: Aperture Photometric Accuracy of Point-spread-function-deconvolved Astronomical Images
papers.abstract: This paper introduces an improved Richardson--Lucy (RL) framework utilizing negative backfilling (NB) and the novel filtered image deconvolution and noise backfilling (FiDNoBa) algorithm. By integrating a low-pass prefiltering stage---specifically employing a Kalman filter---with the reintegration of filtered-out noise components after RL iterations, we effectively suppress noise artifacts while maintaining rigorous flux integrity. We extensively evaluate our Kalman + RL + NB approach using both numerical simulations and real observational data. Simulations across three regimes demonstrate superior photometric accuracy, reducing the relative mean deviation (RMD) to below 1\% for isolated sources, maintaining high fidelity (RMD $\sim$0.37\%) for blended Sérsic galaxies, and achieving $\sim$5\% RMD in crowded stellar fields while significantly increasing source recovery rates compared to traditional point-spread function photometry. Crucially, we validate the practical efficacy of FiDNoBa on real space-based (JWST/NIRCam) and ground-based (Very Large Telescope Survey Telescope OmegaCAM) images. The results confirm that our method reliably handles complex instrumental signatures, such as the extended wings of the STPSF, mitigating the severe ringing artifacts typical of traditional RL deconvolution while ensuring highly stable aperture photometry in practical survey processing.

papers.title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
papers.abstract: We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

papers.title: From Rock Tumbling to Telescope Mirror Grinding: How Optical Perfection Emerges from Random Motion
papers.abstract: When two glass disks are rubbed together by hand with an abrasive between them, their surfaces spontaneously converge to perfectly matching spherical curves, accurate to tens of nanometers. How does such optical precision emerge from an essentially random manual process? Starting from Preston's law of material removal, we derive a first-principles explanation. Symmetries of the grinding stroke imply that planes and spheres are the generic equilibria of the process. Their stability is governed by a hierarchy of timescales: small-scale irregularities decay exponentially on the grinding timescale $T_\text{grind}$, while large-scale deviations from a sphere diffuse away on the longer spherizing timescale $T_\text{sphere} \propto (R_\text{mirror}/R_\text{stroke})^2\, T_\text{grind}$. Gravity and finite disk size destabilize planar surfaces, but for sufficiently short strokes spheres remain stable ($T_\text{deform} \gg T_\text{sphere}$), with only their radius of curvature varying adiabatically. The same framework unifies telescope mirror grinding with everyday phenomena: rock tumbling (explaining why rotary tumbling rounds edges more than vibratory, and why neither produce spheres) and sanding (explaining why small flat surfaces inevitably round). These examples offer an accessible classroom context for stable and unstable equilibria, exponential relaxation, diffusion, multi-timescale analysis, and the emergence of the Laplacian operator from averaging over a local area.

papers.title: Boolean Rank Nine for Polygons with 35 to 40 Vertices
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the rectangle covering number, or Boolean rank, of every polygon slack matrix of order 35 through 40 is nine. The upper bound is due to Goucha, Gouveia, and Silva; the new contribution is the matching lower bound. A hypothetical covering by eight rectangles yields a saturated inclusion cycle between two antichains on eight coordinates. An exact maximal-chain identity bounds its length and assigns a nonnegative penalty to each inclusion edge. The equality case is excluded combinatorially, leaving at most 39 lower vertices. For orders 35 through 39, symmetry reductions and a shadow bound leave fifteen finite exclusions, each supported by a checked reverse-unit-propagation refutation. The main text presents the mathematical reductions and their dependencies; the accompanying supplement gives the complete cycle parameters, encodings, and certificate record. The previously known equality for orders 41 through 55 is cited directly.

papers.title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
papers.abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. Benchmarking under the same measurement budget demonstrates substantially higher reconstruction fidelity than other encoding strategies, highlighting the advantages of learned optical compression. With the optical encoder fixed, decoder-only neural adaptation enables experimental transfer to previously unseen data distributions, extending the utility of the learned measurement representation. These results establish learned optical compression as a measurement-efficient and reusable framework for QPI, integrating phase-information compression into single-pixel intensity measurements while retaining adaptability to new data. This approach paves the way for low-data-rate phase imaging and sensing, with the potential to extend QPI to spectral regions where high-quality detector arrays are costly or unavailable.

papers.title: MMCoT$^3$: Empowering 3D Scene Understanding with 3D-Text Interleaved Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract: Understanding and reasoning over 3D scenes from point clouds is essential for a broad range of AI applications. Recent 3D large language models have shown promising results, yet they still face two fundamental limitations: (i) insufficient capability for grounded multi-step reasoning in complex 3D scenes, and (ii) a text-centric inference paradigm that lacks effective interaction between textual reasoning and visual evidence. As a result, these models often fail to verify intermediate inferences, disambiguate similar object instances, and avoid hallucinations. To address these limitations, we propose MMCoT$^3$, the first 3D-Text Interleaved Chain-of-Thought (CoT) framework for 3D scene understanding. The core idea is to explicitly interleave textual reasoning with task-relevant 3D evidence, enabling the model to consult scene observations throughout the reasoning process. In addition, since a textual mention in 3D scenes may correspond to multiple candidate objects, naive object-mention alignment can inject incorrect evidence and mislead subsequent reasoning. To mitigate this multi-instance ambiguity, we design an ambiguity-aware evidence aggregation mechanism that uses query-guided cross-attention to fuse candidate object tokens and inject both evidence and ambiguity cues into the reasoning process. To better equip the model with multi-step reasoning capability, we further develop PointCoT, a large-scale 3D-specific CoT instruction tuning dataset with approximately 176.2K instances spanning captioning, question answering, dialogue, and planning tasks. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks show that our method consistently improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art results, validating the effectiveness of our proposed ambiguity-aware 3D-text interleaved reasoning for 3D scene understanding.

papers.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In receiver-directed federated learning, each site draws a trust boundary. For every source and model component it judges, on its own data, whether the transfer helps (admit), harms (reject) or cannot yet be told (abstain). We ask whether this boundary holds over hundreds of rounds. Our benchmark has a federation of thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle for every evaluated transfer, paired seeds, an attack protocol, fourteen methods over 600 rounds and Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500. The answer depends on which boundary is measured. Across 20 paired CPU seeds, a gate judging against a fixed reference better identified transfers useful relative to the site's starting model. Yet it admitted 29% of transfers harmful to the model the site now has. A gate judging against the current model admitted 2% of harmful transfers on that target in the CPU tier, but missed many transfers useful to the starting model. Two short propositions explain these distinct failures. We also evaluate a held out audit that leaves gate verdicts intact. After training, it decides whether each final model is deployed or the site falls back to local training, and reports admissions that have gone stale. With independent audit data its guarantees hold after any training history. At 600 rounds the audit deployed 65 to 72% of models, none with negative benefit on its target, and kept 98% of the gain. No stale report had the wrong sign in our runs. With 20,000 audit observations, a variance-adaptive bound found 99% of stale transfers that cost at least 0.01 in log loss. A common-target Qwen3 comparison on 60 selected transfers shows the same tension over 100 rounds. With 38% adversarial sites, FedFomo and CS-Gate were the only evaluated methods with positive mean gain in every honest group.

papers.title: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0: Causal World Models for Real-World Driving and Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: We present Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0, a unified streaming causal world model for Physical AI. It models and generates causal physical evolution in the real world, and unifies heterogeneous conditioning inputs for view-consistent generation. The architecture integrates View-Temporal Attention (VTA) to capture cross-view spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics, together with Multi-view Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) to encode positional relationships across views and time. WorldRec 2.0 reconstructs static and dynamic 3D Gaussians from multi-view, multi-temporal observations in a single forward pass and uses their renderings as explicit scene context to preserve geometry and appearance during long-horizon generation. Conditioning inputs are fused through VAE latent concatenation in a shared representation space. We incorporate Gated Linear Attention (GLA) into the temporal layers of VTA for efficient streaming inference, reducing computation and KV-cache memory during multi-view rollouts. A physical-interaction data pipeline covers diverse interactions and long-tailed events. From Pre-train onward, these data are combined with large-scale videos and heterogeneous visual modalities to learn visual, geometric, and dynamic priors. During Mid-train, training across diverse view configurations further improves the model's ability to capture how actions and object states shape subsequent scene evolution. After distillation-based Post-train, we apply the model to closed-loop simulation, closed-loop training, and World Action Model (WAM) applications. These applications generate physically consistent future states and support world-state prediction, policy learning, and action generation for Physical AI.

papers.title: Communication with Adversarial Users: Byzantine Models in Multi-User Information Theory
papers.abstract: We consider communication systems operating in environments where some participating users cannot be trusted. This motivates the study of Byzantine communication models, in which users may behave adversarially. In this survey, we provide a unified information-theoretic perspective on communication with adversarial users in multi-user settings. We review recent advances in Byzantine multiple access channels, including reliable communication, adversary identification, and distributed function computation. Furthermore, we discuss extensions to classical-quantum channels and highlight fundamental differences between classical and quantum models. Finally, we outline key open problems and future research directions at the intersection of communication, computation, and security.

papers.title: Bounds and sufficient conditions in quantum Zeno effect
papers.abstract: When a quantum system undergoes a series of repeated measurements during its time evolution to check whether it remains in the initial state, the resulting state lifetime can decrease (the quantum Zeno effect) or increase (the quantum inverse Zeno effect) as the inter-measurement period increases. Several transitions between these two regimes may occur within the same system. A carefully chosen measurement period $τ_\ast$ (or rate $r_\ast$ in the case of a stochastic measurement protocol) brings the state lifetime to its global minimum. Here, we describe the upper and lower bounds on the optimized state lifetime, which are expressed in terms of characteristic time scales encoded in the state survival probability $P(T)$, which is assumed to decrease monotonically to zero at large $T$. In addition, we analyze the bounds on the optimal measurement periods/rates and formulate sufficient conditions for observing the inverse Zeno effect. The analysis is also extended to states with non-monotonic survival functions. The results are illustrated numerically with an example of a system of optically trapped ultra-cold atoms.

papers.title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
papers.abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. Second, physics-informed methods impose a specified physical equation as a reconstruction constraint, but often require environment-dependent parameters that are difficult to acquire. As a result, practical 3D acoustic field reconstruction that is both physically grounded and robust to uncertain environmental information remains largely unexplored. This work takes an alternative route: instead of solving a fully specified wave equation, it extracts a structured representation from wave physics and learns its components from data. From the Helmholtz equation and normal mode propagation, we derive a structured spatial-angular tensor representation, termed the S/c representation. Under a low-rank specialization, it takes the form of a rank-(L,L,1) block-term tensor decomposition, which connects structured sampling patterns/routes used in ocean sensing to sufficient conditions for field recovery. Building on this tensor representation, we propose TIDAL, a neural reconstructor that uses the S/c representation as an inductive bias for structured decoding and aligns information aggregation with the sampling geometry. The neural learner removes the need for known model parameters required by conventional physics-based recovery methods. Experiments across three structured sampling geometries show that TIDAL achieves the best reconstruction performance and fastest inference among baselines, with benefits from the physics-derived representation under limited data and model capacity.

papers.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
papers.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. Energetic electrons deposit energy in silicon, producing nonequilibrium carriers that perturb the semiconductor surface potential and electric displacement across the adjacent aqueous interface. The resulting redistribution of interfacial water polarization drives a transient compensation current, whereas carrier relaxation restores the initial polarization state and generates an opposite-polarity recovery signal. The complete irradiation-detector-electrometer system exhibits exponential rise and recovery time constants of approximately 1.0 and 3.6 ms, respectively. The response is strongly regulated by water-layer thickness and ionic composition, and the 17 beam pulses of a programmed 1 s sequence at 17 Hz are resolved individually. Integration with Ce:YAG further introduces a scintillation-mediated excitation pathway. These findings establish interfacial water polarization as a tunable, zero-bias electrical transduction mechanism for time-resolved beta-radiation monitoring and motivate future investigations of higher-energy charged particles and secondary particles relevant to neutrino detection.

papers.title: Leveraging 2D Foundation Priors for Generalized Category Discovery under Test-Time Adaptation in 3D LiDAR Segmentation
papers.abstract: In autonomous driving, 3D LiDAR semantic segmentation is expected to adapt to evolving environments and recognize previously unseen categories, making generalized category discovery under test-time adaptation (GCD-TTA) an important problem. However, existing works treat GCD and TTA separately, while the limited semantic information in 3D point clouds makes GCD-TTA under domain shift more prone to feature collapse when combining GCD with TTA. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage framework for GCD-TTA in 3D LiDAR semantic segmentation. Specifically, in the first stage, we adaptively aggregate local 3D features according to geometric density variations and obtain reliable pseudo labels under a global class-wise prototype consistency constraint. In the second stage, we cast category discovery as an optimal transport assignment process for globally consistent grouping of novel categories. Meanwhile, semantic features from 2D vision foundation models are fused with 3D point cloud features to enrich 3D semantic information and promote a more separable feature space. Extensive experiments on Synth4D to SemanticKITTI, SynLiDAR to SemanticKITTI, and Synth4D to nuScenes demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our method achieves the best overall mIoU on 9 out of 10 benchmark splits and improves the overall mIoU by up to 12.21 points over the strongest re-implemented baseline.

papers.title: Accounting for correlations in the $ωπ$ spectral function and its implication on the leading model dependent contribution to the $τ^- \to π^-π^0 ν_τγ$ decay
papers.abstract: The $ωπ$ spectral function, measured in the decay $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ by the CLEO Collaboration, is described in the vector meson dominance approach. We sample the parameter space using a Metropolis Monte-Carlo algorithm and generate a set of parameters of the corresponding form factor, explicitly accounting for the correlation among them. We show the improvement in the uncertainty region of the spectral function with respect to neglecting correlations. We test the conserved vector current hypothesis by showing the agreement of the spectral function with the expected from the measurement of the cross section of $e^+e^- \to ωπ$ by the SND experiment, and the consistency of the branching ratio of the $τ^- \to π^-ων_τ$ decay with the value reported by the Particle Data Group. As an application, we consider the $ω$-channel of the $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τγ$ process, the leading model dependent contribution in the vector meson dominance approach. We compute the contribution to the long distance electromagnetic correction function $G_\text{EM}(t)$, of the pure $ω$-channel and its interference with the structure independent part. We show that the uncertainties, using the set of correlated parameters, are largely reduced with respect to neglecting correlations. The implication on the isospin symmetry breaking correction to the muon magnetic dipole moment estimation from tau data is found to be consistent with previous results but with improved precision.

papers.title: GaitFM: A Cross-Modal Foundation Model for Wearable Gait Assessment
papers.abstract: Gait assessment supports the diagnosis, monitoring, and prognosis of diverse movement-related conditions, such as neurological and musculoskeletal disorders. Recent advances in deep learning using everyday wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) offer an accessible and low-cost approach to automated gait assessment. However, IMU measurements vary substantially across individuals, body locations, and device configurations, while existing deep learning models are typically developed using small, homogeneous datasets for specific clinical tasks, limiting their robustness and generalizability in diverse real-world contexts. Here we present GaitFM, a cross-modal foundation model for gait assessment using IMU sensors. GaitFM improves the generalizability of gait assessment by transferring knowledge from large vision models and pretraining on unlabeled IMU sensor data. We pretrain GaitFM on a large curated dataset comprising about 4,000 participants and 1.23 million gait windows across diverse clinical and daily conditions, sensor modalities, and body locations. GaitFM demonstrates strong performance across 18 gait-related tasks, including 3 gait parameter estimation tasks, 14 disease and gait abnormality detection tasks, and 1 clinical outcome prediction task. Furthermore, GaitFM generalizes across different sensor configurations and body locations, including those commonly used in clinical settings and everyday wearable devices. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of transferring visual knowledge in improving sensor-based gait assessment performance, offering a new promising pathway for addressing data scarcity in the sensor and medical domains.

papers.title: Assessing Temporal Dispersion of Time-Varying Channel at 38 GHz for Different Reference Signals
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of reference waveform selection on temporal dispersion estimation in a time-varying radio channel at 38 GHz. Three reference waveforms-numerically generated in MATLAB, measured through a conducted connection, and recorded in an anechoic chamber -are compared using the same wideband channel measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Their effects on the estimated power delay profiles (PDPs), mean delay, and root mean square (RMS) delay spread are evaluated. Despite noticeable differences in the time-domain and spectral characteristics of the reference waveforms, the resulting PDPs exhibit similar multipath structures, while the estimated temporal dispersion parameters show relatively small differences. The results indicate limited sensitivity to reference waveform selection under the investigated measurement conditions.

papers.title: An Electrolyte Equation of State Based on openCOSMO-RS: From Aqueous Solutions to Non-Aqueous Systems
papers.abstract: Predictive COSMO-RS-based electrolyte models such as COSMO-RS-ES describe electrolyte solutions from quantum-chemical information, but treat the liquid as incompressible and give no access to densities or pressure effects. This work presents openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi, to our knowledge the first open-source implementation of a predictive electrolyte equation of state based on openCOSMO-RS. It combines the COSMO-RS-based equation of state openCOSMO-RS-Phi with the ion interaction energies and the long-range term of COSMO-RS-ES, which is first refitted on the same simplified short range. With this refit, a dielectric decrement improves the mean ionic activity coefficients (MIAC), whereas a Born term counts the solvation of the ions a second time and is therefore left out. The equation of state then adds only volume, dispersion and temperature parameters of the ions, fitted to aqueous MIAC and densities. openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi reproduces COSMO-RS-ES in dilute aqueous solutions, improves on it in concentrated ones and also yields solution densities. Extrapolating from aqueous systems, it predicts the MIAC in water + cosolvent mixtures as accurately as the fitted COSMO-RS-ES, as well as the MIAC and bubble points of a benchmark database of water-alcohol-salt systems. Salting-out of organic components is not described as accurately, and salts come out too soluble in organic solvents. Overall, the interaction model developed for COSMO-RS-ES carries over to a large extent to an equation of state, which makes openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi a sound base model for further development, with ion transfer between solvents as a clear target for fitting to non-aqueous data.

papers.title: Percentile oscillations and the intrinsic square function
papers.abstract: Wilson's intrinsic square function tests the input against all the cancellative functions of a given smoothness, at every location and scale. We show that it is dominated pointwise by a sparse square function, whose coefficients are the percentile oscillations of the input modulo polynomials, at every polynomial order below the smoothness plus one. These coefficients are local sizes, which nevertheless retain essentially all the cancellation: the weighted norms of the sparse square function are equivalent to smooth grand maximal norms, for all $0<p<\infty$ and $A_\infty$ weights, with explicit dependence on the weight. These are weighted Hardy norms in the range allowed by the smoothness. Consequences include potential bounds, and weighted Hardy space estimates with the sharp factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$. For the derivatives of Calderón--Zygmund operators, we characterize the corresponding square function estimates by testing conditions on the polynomial symbols of their wavelet resolution. In the quadratic setting, the factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$ detects a transition from $\mathrm{BMO}$ testing conditions to vanishing symbols.

papers.title: SEALECT: Scene-Conditioned Pose Priors for Plausible Maritime Vessel Retrieval
papers.abstract: We address scene-conditioned object retrieval for compositional augmentation in maritime imagery, where strong geometric constraints make appearance-only retrieval produce physically implausible vessel insertions. We propose SEALECT, a retrieval framework that jointly models visual compatibility, vessel pose, scale, and scene geometry through a unified score combining neural similarity, scene-conditioned pose priors, and observed-pose consistency. We construct a maritime scene-pose library and model the pose and scale priors nonparametrically, as a kernel that conditions each prior continuously on the scene with no learned parameters. Across seven maritime benchmarks, our trained scene-conditioned retriever exceeds the strongest appearance encoder (SigLIP 2) in recall (+0.14), and the training-free prior raises geometric plausibility further at negligible recall cost, more than halving the constraint violations of appearance retrieval and outperforming learned foreground-search baselines (GALA-style, DiscoFOS). In a blind study of end-to-end composites (BootPlace placement, DiffHarmony harmonization), SEALECT ranks first among six methods, ahead of random and GALA-style selection and statistically tied with CLIP, DiscoFOS, and DINO.

papers.title: Partially wrapped contact Fukaya categories of 1-jet spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category of a 1-jet space equipped with a stop, which is an \(A_\infty\)-category of Legendrians equipped with representations of their Chekanov-Eliashberg algebras. This category is invariant under contact isotopies of the stop. We prove a wrapping exact triangle and a generation theorem. When the stop is bounded subanalytic singular isotropic, we prove a Morita equivalence between the partially wrapped contact Fukaya category and a microlocal sheaf category.

papers.title: Sharp upper and lower bounds on the variance of U-statistics
papers.abstract: For a U-statistic with a symmetric kernel of any rank, we offer new upper and lower bounds on its variance, which are uniformly sharper than those established in the classical paper by Hoeffding (1948, Theorem 5.2). Our new bounds have strong optimality properties and can tightly describe how the variance scales with the degree of the kernel. As an application, we leverage our new upper bound to improve an existing Berry-Esseen theorem for the normal approximation of incomplete U-statistics based on Bernoulli sampling, in a computationally frugal regime where the computational budget is much smaller than the available sample size.

papers.title: Spherically-symmetric solutions with internal Ricci-flat spaces in Brans-Dicke theory
papers.abstract: We construct a new family of exact spherically symmetric solutions in $D$-dimensional Brans-Dicke theory with $n$ internal Ricci-flat spaces. The spacetime is assumed to be a product of a four-dimensional spherical sector and $n$ Ricci-flat internal manifolds. By performing a conformal transformation to the Einstein frame, the problem is reduced to Einstein gravity with a minimally coupled scalar field, for which the exact solution is already known. Applying the inverse transformation to the Jordan frame yields explicit expressions for the metric and the Brans-Dicke scalar field, together with a generalized algebraic constraint on the exponents. The obtained solutions generalize the four-dimensional Brans solutions and the multidimensional solutions with Ricci-flat internal spaces. We analyze the causal structure of the four-dimensional section and derive the necessary condition for the surface $R=L$ to be an event horizon, $ν\equiv \left|a+b+\frac12\sum_i a_iN_i\right| \ge 1$. A Kretschmann-scalar analysis shows that, apart from the Schwarzschild limit and the case of frozen internal spaces, a regular horizon is generically absent when the extra dimensions are dynamical. For the four-dimensional section we also obtain the photon-sphere and ISCO radii and discuss their Schwarzschild limits. The results clarify the role of nonminimal Brans-Dicke coupling in multidimensional black-hole geometries with Ricci-flat internal factors.

papers.title: Phase-wise MLLM Tuning for Multi-framework WebUI Code Generation
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance in translating WebUI screenshots into HTML/CSS. However, when they faced multiple frameworks (React/Vue/Angular), they often suffer from negative transfer that leads to compilation failures. These failures commonly stem from mixing framework specific syntax and violating framework constraints. This paper studies supervised fine-tuning for multi-framework WebUI code generation and proposes a phase-wise MLLM tuning method driven by compatibility and heterogeneity signals across frameworks. We first apply a normalization mapping that preserves each framework's native syntax while suppressing noise from variable naming and literal content. We then estimate cross framework heterogeneity and compatibility offline, and automatically derive training groups and their ordering by maximizing a phased objective. Finally, we perform phase-wise adapter tuning to reduce cross framework interference. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our proposed method improves both generation quality and compilation success rate compared with baselines.

papers.title: Stein Criteria for Holomorphic Fibre Bundles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Steinness of holomorphic fibre bundles. Over a compact Riemann surface, we prove that every holomorphic ball bundle is weakly $1$-complete and that its total space is Stein if and only if it admits no holomorphic section. We also obtain higher-dimensional Stein criteria for reductive ball bundles and affine bundles in terms of positivity of the canonical class. A topological obstruction to the $1$-convexity of holomorphic fibre bundles is also established.

papers.title: Direct Covariance-to-Beamformer Mapping for Low-Latency Hybrid ISAC Beamforming with Subsequent DoA Estimation
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems typically employ a two-stage beamforming pipeline, in which target directions are first estimated from the received covariance matrix and then used to compute the beamforming weights by solving non-convex optimization problems. Although effective, this approach introduces processing latency that can limit beam adaptation in dynamic environments. This letter proposes a beamforming deep neural network (BFDNN) for direct covariance-to-beamformer learning in ISAC systems. BFDNN is a compact regression network that maps covariance-matrix features directly to the hybrid beamforming weights produced by a hybrid ISAC beamformer, eliminating the direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation stage during inference. Compared with MUSIC, classification-DNN, and regression-DNN based beamforming pipelines, BFDNN generates comparable beam patterns and higher effective spectral efficiencies while reducing the beamforming prediction latency by 25-30 times on the evaluated platform, demonstrating the potential of direct covariance-to-beamformer learning for low-latency ISAC beam updates. Moreover, the target directions can be inferred indirectly from the generated radiation pattern, yielding DoA accuracy competitive with that of dedicated learning-based methods in the evaluated scenario.

papers.title: SPAR: Experience-Driven Strategy Evolution in Multi-Session B2B Sales
papers.abstract: B2B outbound sales involves high transaction values and relationship-based trust, so closing a deal typically requires multiple rounds of outreach building on prior context. Existing LLM-based sales agents operate within single sessions and cannot carry forward context or refine strategies from experience. Methods that do learn from experience store lessons as unstructured text and treat all outcomes as equally informative, with no mechanism to distinguish a flawed strategy from an external factor. We propose SPAR, a self-evolving framework that models selling strategies as testable hypotheses and refines them without parameter updates. A double-loop architecture lets an inner loop adapt to individual merchants through episodic memory while an outer loop evolves a shared strategy playbook through causal attribution and hypothesis-driven evolution. In a live A/B test on the 1688 platform with over 200,000 merchants, SPAR achieves +15.8% conversion lift and +35.8% high-intent merchant growth. Human evaluation by domain experts rates SPAR at 4.62 out of 5 on overall sales quality, the highest among all methods.

papers.title: Restoring Semantic Fidelity for Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation in Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based text-to-image models have recently achieved remarkable success in image synthesis. However, when directly applied beyond their training resolution, these models often suffer from severe semantic degradation, where meaningful semantic content disappears. Although existing training-free high-resolution generation methods can mitigate this issue, the inherent semantic degradation at high resolutions remains largely unresolved, leading to degraded fine-grained details. Furthermore, widely used structural guidance methods lack modeling of the structure and details in the intermediate trajectory, which degrades the quality of the generated results. In this paper, we propose a training-free framework for high-resolution image generation to address these challenges. First, we propose a text-visual scale-decoupled attention (TVSDA) module, which restores the model's ability to generate semantically meaningful content at high resolutions by preserving the global receptive field of text tokens while aligning the receptive field of image tokens with the training resolution. Second, we propose a structure-detail guidance (SDG) strategy that explicitly models structural information and fine details through scale-wise and temporal-wise guidance, overcoming the limitations of conventional low-resolution guidance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves both structural coherence and detail fidelity over existing training-free DiT-based high-resolution generation approaches. The code is available at https://github.com/ljjcoder/Restoring-Semantic-Fidelity.

papers.title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
papers.abstract: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $μ$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

papers.title: Subset-system derived topologies and coreflective categories of $T_0$-spaces
papers.abstract: Given a subset system $H$ on $T_0$-spaces, we associate with each topology a closure-testing derived topology and study the fixed points of this operator. The $H$-determined topologies above a given topology are closed under intersections and hence determine a least fixed-point hull. We prove that this hull is obtained by transfinite iteration, is functorial, and defines a right adjoint to the inclusion of $H$-determined spaces into $\mathbf{Top}_0$. Consequently, the corresponding full subcategory is coreflective and complete. We isolate restriction-stability and open-locality hypotheses under which determinedness is inherited by closed and open subspaces, and we establish a general non-reflectivity criterion. If $H$ is contained in the directed-subset system, the category of $H$-determined spaces is Cartesian closed; its exponentials are obtained by coreflecting the pointwise convergence topology on continuous maps. The construction subsumes familiar monotone- and irreducible-determined cases while separating the formal consequences of the subset-system axioms from the additional hypotheses needed for heredity and exponentials. It therefore provides a uniform categorical mechanism for producing complete Cartesian closed categories of $T_0$-spaces with explicit higher-order function spaces, as required in denotational semantics.

papers.title: Chaotic Dynamics of Charged Particles in Magnetic Fields with Singular Forces
papers.abstract: We study charged-particle dynamics under a non-Lipschitz velocity-dependent force with magnetic and damping effects, focusing on continuation through zero velocity and chaos in the velocity direction. For a time-independent directional force and fixed parameters, we introduce a $C^1$ regularization. When an unregularized trajectory reaches zero velocity in finite time, inner rescaling yields convergence to a reference orbit within the regularization ball, while the regularized trajectories converge locally uniformly outside it to a unique continuation. For the directional dynamics, stereographic projection yields a parameterized Euclidean system. By choosing the skew-symmetric magnetic part, we obtain a nonautonomous parameterized center manifold reduction with a prescribed finite Taylor jet. Under an additional factorization assumption, the reduced dynamics admits Shilnikov homoclinic orbits and associated chaos.

papers.title: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents often rely on persistent memory to retain user preferences and operational rules across sessions. However, this capability introduces a new safety risk: malicious instructions from messages, documents, or Web content can be retained in memory and influence future tasks even after the original attack content is removed. Existing attack success metrics, however, fail to capture who is affected and how attacks translate into downstream harm during otherwise normal task execution. We introduce MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark for evaluating cross-session prompt injection in memory-persistent AI agents. MemHarmBench considers three categories of potential victims: users, workspace/project owners, and external stakeholders. Our evaluation first exposes an agent to malicious instructions and tests whether they are retained in memory. We then remove the attack content and initiate a new session with a legitimate task while preserving the agent's memory. We jointly evaluate whether the agent follows the attacker's intent, completes the legitimate task, and exhibits observable execution anomalies. Across multiple agent systems, we find that cross-session attacks can remain behaviorally stealthy: agents often complete tasks normally and exhibit no detectable anomalies while still making critical decisions aligned with the attacker's intent. By connecting malicious memory retention to downstream decisions and affected parties, MemHarmBench provides a systematic framework for exposing safety risks that conventional attack- and task-success metrics may overlook. We publicly release MemHarmBench at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/MemHarmBench.

papers.title: Just-in-Time Skill Retrieval via Long-Horizon State Tracking
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external skill libraries to support complex task execution. However, determining which skills are needed remains challenging in long-horizon tasks. Existing methods typically select a fixed skill set before execution, implicitly assuming that a task's procedural requirements can be determined from its initial description. This assumption is restrictive for long-horizon interaction, where new requirements emerge from intermediate observations, execution outcomes, and newly revealed constraints. This motivates just-in-time skill retrieval, which dynamically selects skills as execution unfolds.
