Just-in-time skill retrieval is promising but challenging: the utility of a skill depends not only on the current context, but also on the evolving task state shaped by prior steps. To this end, we propose JitSkill, a state-grounded framework that addresses this challenge through continuous task-state tracking. By connecting emerging requirements with accumulated task progress, JitSkill provides procedural support throughout execution without treating each retrieval decision independently. Experiments across three agent benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness in improving long-horizon task completion. Our code is available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/JitSkill.git/.

papers.title: SparseLift: Automatically Optimizing Opaque Sparse Paths in Industrial-Scale Recommendation Model Training
papers.abstract: The sparse path, comprising sparse operations and collective communication, is a critical component of large-scale recommendation models. However, these operations are often represented as opaque nodes in the training computation graph, hindering whole-graph optimization. We present SparseLift, a low-overhead compiler for the sparse path of large-scale recommendation training. It exposes sparse computation and communication to whole-graph analysis to expand the optimization space and improve training efficiency. By analyzing model structure and runtime information, SparseLift reconstructs opaque nodes as analyzable subgraphs, recovering the resource semantics of sparse computation and communication within the graph. Building on the recovered semantics, we design incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to automatically select and organize subgraph optimizations into an execution plan that is reused during subsequent steady-state training. We evaluate SparseLift on an industrial video-platform recommendation task with 100B sparse parameters and the public DLRM benchmark. SparseLift improves steady-state throughput for ordinary industrial training steps by 16.5\% over the native baseline. On DLRM, it achieves $1.60\times$ and $1.26\times$ model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline and TorchRec, respectively.

papers.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.

papers.title: MatMoE: Matryoshka Mixture-of-Experts with Dynamic Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient Inference
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture has been widely adopted in large language models (LLMs) since it reduces the computational cost through sparse expert activation. However, the massive parameter scale of MoE models hinders their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Although existing mixed-precision quantization reduces the model size, they are inherently static, fixing the bit-width of each expert across decoding steps. Such static schemes yield suboptimal performance as they overlook the dynamic variation in expert importance during decoding. Furthermore, they fail to adapt to the dynamic latency constraint driven by the fluctuating system utilization. To address these challenges, we propose MatMoE, a dynamic mixed-precision quantization framework for efficient MoE inference. MatMoE features: (1) a Matryoshka MoE PTQ algorithm that enables experts to operate flexibly at multiple precisions within a stringent memory budget; (2) a floor-and-compensation quantization method that eliminates redundant memory accesses in the Matryoshka representation; and (3) a dynamic bit-width allocation strategy that determines the precision for each expert based on their routing scores to satisfy the dynamic latency requirement. We implement our MatMoE system atop llama.cpp for both CPU and GPU platforms. Extensive evaluations across three modern MoE models and challenging benchmarks demonstrate that MatMoE achieves $4.0\% \sim 18.3\%$ higher accuracy than state-of-the-art static mixed-precision method. Compared to llama.cpp, MatMoE delivers $1.3\times \sim 3.7\times$ speedup on Raspberry Pi 5, and $1.2\times \sim 1.3\times$ speedup on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Orin.

papers.title: Fréchet Oral Distance: A Coordinate-Free Metric and Benchmark for Speech-Driven Oral Animation
papers.abstract: Recently, speech-driven facial and oral animation technologies have been used in various fields such as education, speech therapy, and healthcare. But methods to objectively evaluate the quality of generated results are still limited. Accordingly, we propose the Fréchet Oral Distance (FOD), which uses embeddings from an Oral Motion Encoder (OME) and a TIMIT-Vis reference distribution. In experiments, FOD reproduced model rankings similar to the coordinate-based metric, Lip Vertex Error (LVE), and showed trends consistent with user preference. Our framework provides objective and reproducible benchmarking without relying on expensive equipment or subjective evaluation, and it can be extended to compare a variety of 2D/3D models.

papers.title: Agent-Based Disruption Simulation on an Edge-Level Product-Annotated Supply Network of the Automotive Industry
papers.abstract: Disruptions spread through supply networks when customers cannot replace the products they lose. We ask how portfolio-overlap and product-specific rules for selecting candidate suppliers change cascades when customers search for new suppliers and form new supply edges. From the MarkLines database, we construct a product-annotated network of about 77,000 firms and 197,000 supplier-customer edges in the global automotive industry. We extend an agent-based disruption model with edge-level products, a product-specific substitution rule based on the semantic similarity of product names, and calibrated capacities and inventories. Only 6% of the edges carry observed products. We impute the others and test the imputation against the annotated edges. We run 119,000 simulations. With all other mechanics fixed, the product-specific rule makes the cascades after a hub failure four to five times larger than the portfolio-overlap rule of the original model. Under alternative imputations and similarity thresholds, the factor ranges from 1.2 to 18. Within the simulations, substitutability also shapes which suppliers are critical. Network topology largely determines which firms a shock reaches, and substitutability determines how many of them fail. Of the 50 most damaging suppliers under random disruptions, topology alone identifies 20 and an index that adds product substitutability identifies 32. The index carries over without refitting to a regional scenario modelled on the 2011 Tohoku Earthquake. Supply network risk assessment should account for product-level substitutability and therefore needs product data on supply relationships.

papers.title: SMART-AIMC: Sensitivity-Aware Mixed ADC Resolution with Fine-Grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing
papers.abstract: Analog In-Memory Computing (IMC) is a promising paradigm for accelerating GEMM-based AI workloads by executing computations directly within the memory array in the analog domain. While IMC delivers substantial energy and throughput improvements, it can suffer from significant task accuracy degradation due to analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization noise, which occurs at the GEMM output and is thus different from weight/activation quantization, which occurs at the GEMM input. Mixed ADC resolution allows IMC modules to choose between high- and low-resolution ADC modes with different energy costs, offering a compelling accuracy-energy trade-off. However, selecting ADC resolutions across IMC units while respecting hardware granularity constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose SMART-AIMC, a Sensitivity-aware Mixed ADC Resolution framework with fine-grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing. SMART-AIMC correlates the algorithmic task loss to hardware ADC quantization noise in the form of an ADC Channel Sensitivity (ACS) metric. Using this metric, SMART-AIMC systematically, and in a disciplined manner, allocates ADC resources to critical computations. Furthermore, we introduce a sensitivity-based channel reordering scheme that overcomes the hardware granularity constraints with no runtime overhead and approaches the optimal ADC quantization possible for the model. Evaluated across diverse workloads, SMART-AIMC unlocks a superior accuracy-energy Pareto frontier, providing (1) higher task accuracy at matched energy budgets and (2) fine-grained tuning across efficiency targets, from aggressive energy savings to near-digital inference accuracy. At the latter operating point, SMART-AIMC achieves $6.99\times$ higher modeled system-level energy efficiency for linear projections than the INT8 digital baseline with negligible accuracy degradation.

papers.title: A new upper bound for the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$
papers.abstract: Fauzan's determinantal proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational also yields $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-260}$ for all large $b$. The exponent is the product $\varrhoλ/\varepsilon$ of three constants attached to the construction, of which $\varrho$ governs the growth of a relative matrix norm. We show that $\varrho$ may be taken to be $9.09$ instead of $6933/500=13.866$, and deduce $|ζ(5)-a/b|>b^{-171}$ for all integers $a$ and all sufficiently large integers $b$, so that the irrationality exponent of $ζ(5)$ is at most $171$. Two closed-form functions replace two worst-case estimates: a node function, which bounds the residue weights individually instead of uniformly, and the external field of the energy estimate, which replaces a factor-by-factor bound on the weight. The result is conditional on Fauzan's preprint. An exact arithmetic verifier is attached.

papers.title: Comparative Strategies for Handling Imbalanced QSAR Regression: A Case Study on hERG Activity Prediction
papers.abstract: Data imbalance frequently occurs in QSAR modeling, yet most studies focus on classification tasks, and few address regression tasks, as it is challenging to determine which regions of the data are sparse or dense. Data-level and algorithm-level imbalance-handling strategies can have different effects on model performance. In this study, we systematically compare various strategies across GCN and fingerprint-based machine learning models. To evaluate model performance more meaningfully, we partitioned the target region into several subregions based on both domain knowledge and data distribution. We focused on the region of greatest practical interest. Our results demonstrate that selecting models based on this interest-region metric leads to more reliable performance than using the total region metric. We also observed that different imbalance-handling strategies can have divergent effects depending on the model type. These findings highlight the importance of region-aware evaluation in regression QSAR modeling and provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate strategies for imbalanced datasets.

papers.title: CST: Lightweight Risk Triage with Source-Grounded Evidence for Web Discussions
papers.abstract: Web communities rely on moderators to catch harmful messages such as insults, hate speech, and scams, but no one can read every message. Existing tools give each message a risk score, which tells moderators where to look but not what to read or how to check it. Yet meaning depends on context: the same reply, "I agree.", can support or oppose removing someone from a group. Moderators therefore need source-grounded evidence, not just scores: a few key messages kept with their original wording and replies. We present CST, a lightweight triage pipeline that first decides where to look, then what to show. It scores risk by pairing character patterns, which capture exact wording, with sentence meaning from a fixed multilingual model, so it handles several languages and runs on an ordinary CPU. It then groups related messages and picks from each group in turn, so a small reading budget covers different parts of a discussion, and links every pick back to the original thread. Across six tasks from five datasets in several languages, CST ranks harmful messages more accurately than a fully fine-tuned multilingual model and, under the same budget, finds more of them than reading by score alone. In a user study, reviewers needed at least 27% less time with CST's grouped evidence while keeping decision accuracy above 94%. CST turns risk scores into evidence that moderators can read quickly and check in context. Code and dataset reconstruction resources will be released at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/CST-MIL.

papers.title: Irrationality measures for $Γ(1/4)$ and $Γ(1/3)$
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ denote the irrationality exponent. Bruiltet proved in 2002 that $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 10^{143}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 10^{151}$. We prove $μ(Γ(1/4))\le 3.24\cdot 10^{26}$ and $μ(Γ(1/3))\le 1.74\cdot 10^{26}$, with explicit thresholds $h(p/q)\ge 5.4\cdot 10^{7}$ and $h(p/q)\ge 4.7\cdot 10^{7}$ respectively, against $10^{75}$ and $10^{79}$ in the published statements. The proof keeps the architecture of Bruiltet's argument -- Philippon's transcendence criterion together with a zero estimate in commutative algebraic groups -- and replaces three of its ingredients. First, an approximate Schwarz principle based on Hermite interpolation replaces the gravitation estimate of Reyssat; on a lattice point set its cost per node is governed by a lattice energy and drops from about 3.7 to about 1.0. Second, a summation lemma for the failure of Diaz's approximation lemma sharpens the passage from an approximation measure to an irrationality measure. Third, the auxiliary point is taken at a torsion point of order 4, respectively 3, which lowers the degree of the base field from 8d to 2d. All numerical constants are produced by a verifier run in interval arithmetic, supplied as ancillary files.

papers.title: When Disagreement Labels Do Not Identify F1 Rankings
papers.abstract: Agreement labels cancel from an accuracy comparison but can change an F1 ranking. We specialize partial identification to an explicit audit after labeling disagreements: two agreement counts give exact bounds, certifying a ranking or a choice within a specified F1 tolerance under every completion. Across 3,200 frozen model pairs, shared completions tighten bounds and a 0.01 tolerance reduces labeling costs. A zero-loss (weak-winner) control attributes most savings to positive tolerance, not ties. Guarantees concern the evaluated batch, not future data.

papers.title: Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair for Safe Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models can generate task-oriented robot actions, but they do not guarantee safe execution in obstacle-rich manipulation scenes. Although CBF-QP safety filters can locally project unsafe actions into a safe set, such correction may push the robot away from the learned task trajectory and leave the VLA policy without a reliable recovery direction. We propose Route-Guided CBF-QP Repair, a post-hoc repair module that uses the short-horizon action chunk predicted by the VLA to detect blocked nominal trajectories and generate entry-exit-rejoin guidance around obstacles. The selected route is added to the CBF-QP objective as a soft guidance term, while the CBF safety constraint remains hard. On SafeLIBERO, our method improves collision avoidance, task success, and SafeSuccess compared with AEGIS. Our project page is available at GitHub.

papers.title: The Three-Color Generalized Schur Number of \(x+(k-1)y=z\): A Proof for All \(k\) from a Critical Set of 33 Polynomials
papers.abstract: For an integer \(k\ge 3\), let \(T_k(3)\) be the least positive integer \(N\) such that, for any \(3\)-coloring of \([1,N]\), there exists a monochromatic solution to \(x+(k-1)y=z\). In this paper, we prove that \(T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2\) for all \(k\ge 3\). In the notation \(s_a(3)\) of the first author, with \(a=k-1\), this says that \(s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1\) for all \(a\ge 2\), which confirms the conjecture proposed in 2020. Note that every solution to \(x+(k-1)y=z\) is also a solution to \(x_1+\dots+x_k=x_{k+1}\). So the theorem also gives a new proof of the upper bound in the three-color theorem of Boza, Marín, Revuelta and Sanz, using only this restricted equation. The lower bound is an explicit recursive coloring. For the upper bound, we fix one set \(\Xmin\) of \(33\) polynomials in \(k\), together with the \(144\) polynomial identities \(z=x+(k-1)y\) that hold among them, and we show that no \(3\)-coloring of \(\Xmin\) avoids a monochromatic identity. Since every relation is an identity in \(k\), a single argument covers all \(k\). The argument is a case analysis with \(62\) cases and depth \(8\), and it uses only two elementary rules. It is written out in full in an appendix and has been checked by an independent program. The set \(\Xmin\) is critical, that is, removing any one of its elements makes it \(3\)-colorable. It is also a critical subset of minimum size of the \(51\)-element set from which it was extracted. Finally, we describe the rigid structure shared by all extremal colorings of \([1,k^3+2k^2-3]\).

papers.title: EarlySelectKV: Anticipatory KV Selection via Cross-Layer Query Proxies
papers.abstract: Query-conditioned sparse KV selection reduces long-context inference cost by attending to a subset of historical KV entries at each decoding step. Existing selectors must wait for the target-layer query before scoring candidates and generating indices, placing routing on the immediate pre-attention path. We introduce EarlySelectKV, a training-free transformation that uses proxy queries from earlier hidden states to precompute selected KV indices while retaining the real target-layer query for final attention. Tests with RocketKV, Quest, and Loki show no consistent pattern of quality degradation across the evaluated settings. In the primary RocketKV evaluation, ES-RocketKV differs by +0.018 points on LongBench, approximately -0.01 points on RULER, and +0.25 percentage points on representative NIAH/Passkey settings. In a TensorRT-LLM deployment with CPU-offloaded routing, ES-RocketKV improves end-to-end output throughput by up to 12.4% and reduces GPU-resident memory by 11.1% of the combined KV/K-summary pool. This makes routing timing an explicit optimization target alongside KV subset selection in sparse long-context decoding. Code is available at https://github.com/sea-with-sakura/EarlySelectKV.

papers.title: Derived Torelli for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between the integral Mukai lattices of the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds is induced by an exact equivalence. The proof uses Markman--Mehrotra's comonad reconstruction method to recover both Kuznetsov components from a common Fourier--Mukai comonad on a moduli space of stable objects. As an application, we prove that the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds are equivalent whenever their Fano varieties of lines are derived equivalent.

papers.title: Algebraic properties of Toeplitz operators on annulus and multiply connected domains
papers.abstract: We study the Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over the annulus and provide a complete characterization of them. Based on that, we single out a certain class of Toeplitz operators that satisfy the multiplicativity property and lead to a zero product theorem. We further extend the results for the general multiply-connected domain and prove the zero product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over such a domain.

papers.title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
papers.abstract: Task success, retrieval quality, and cost do not show whether an LLM agent used a delivered memory or what followed from that use. We introduce MemUse, which evaluates memory at its point of use in recorded trajectories: each memory delivery is compared with what the agent could already see and followed through the agent's later actions and their consequences. An agentic judge rates each delivered entry's relevance, accuracy, novelty, influence, and observed effect; programmatic checks enforce complete reading of cited evidence, and fixed rules aggregate the ratings into verdicts linked to memory histories and delivery cost. On 8,000 SWE-bench Verified episodes from three memory systems, resolve rates stay within 0.4 percentage points of a no-memory baseline, yet MemUse shows that most delivered entries were irrelevant, most relevant entries went unused, and in two systems most deliveries restated content the agent could still see. It also surfaces effects that outcomes hide: 23.2\% of episodes with beneficial memory use still failed, and 5 of 16 with harmful use still succeeded.

papers.title: Strict Separation of Antiperiodic Degeneracy Curves for Elliptic Euler and Lagrangian Solutions
papers.abstract: We prove strict separation of antiperiodic degeneracy curves associated with elliptic Euler and Lagrangian solutions of the planar three-body problem. For every eccentricity $0<e<1$, each Euler pair issuing from a common circular parameter is strictly ordered in the extended family $β>0$, and the two Lagrangian curves remain disjoint. Every antiperiodic degeneracy point in these families with $0<e<1$ has a one-dimensional full kernel. Rotation and reflection decomposition yield, for each model, two half-integer Fourier block operators with identical tails and different first blocks. In the Euler case, a positive definite first-block perturbation gives a definite connecting crossing form; a spectral-flow rectangle and sectorwise index counts then force strict separation. In the Lagrangian case, exact tail elimination and an explicit estimate for a two-dimensional Schur complement exclude simultaneous degeneracy in the two reflection sectors.

papers.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
papers.abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. To produce the radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed to be most likely an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of $-(6.8-9.6)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$ when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD ($1.4~M_\odot$). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than $1.4~M_\odot$ if the measured period derivative exceeds $-9.6\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra-contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a $1.0-1.6~M_\odot$ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of $-(4.9-13.5)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of $1.35-1.5~M_\odot$. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be $0.006$ when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

papers.title: GDBack: A Group-Delay Backdoor Attack on Speaker Identification via Analytic All-Pass Filtering
papers.abstract: Existing phase-based backdoor attacks on speaker identification rely on shared absolute phase patterns for cross-sample trigger consistency, while other audio backdoor attacks have explored shared transformations that produce input-dependent triggers. Whether phase-based triggers can achieve similar consistency without imposing identical output phase patterns remains unclear. We propose GDBack, a poison-only group-delay backdoor attack using cascaded second-order analytic all-pass filters. Applying a shared transformation across utterances ideally preserves spectral magnitude while introducing a consistent frequency-dependent phase response and group-delay contribution, without forcing identical output phases. Experiments on LibriSpeech and VoxCeleb1 with ECAPA-TDNN, x-vector, and RawNet3 achieve attack success rates above 94% across all six settings (97.00% on average), while maintaining benign accuracy close to clean models. Phase and magnitude interventions, inverse compensation, and parameter-sensitivity analyses support the role of the induced phase transformation in backdoor activation. Speech quality and content evaluations indicate limited perceptual and linguistic distortion, while robustness experiments, including real over-the-air tests, reveal varying effectiveness across conditions and architectures. These findings demonstrate that cross-sample trigger consistency can arise from a shared phase transformation without requiring a common absolute phase pattern.

papers.title: Higher-Order Symmetry Energy Effects on the Properties of Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: We study the effects of the symmetry-energy curvature $K_{\rm sym}$ on the equation of state (EoS) and neutron-star properties within the relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework. We construct controlled families of RMF parametrizations based on the TM1 and IUFSU models by varying $K_{\rm sym}$ while keeping the symmetry energy $J$ and its slope $L$ fixed at saturation density. We find that, although a larger $K_{\rm sym}$ leads to a lower symmetry energy at suprasaturation densities and a reduced proton fraction in $β$-equilibrated matter, it results in a stiffer EoS and a higher sound speed. The maximum neutron-star mass is weakly affected, whereas the canonical radius $R_{1.4}$ exhibits a nearly linear dependence on $K_{\rm sym}$.

papers.title: A sensor-driven physics-informed neural network for real-time occupant-centric space heating control
papers.abstract: Conventional space heating systems typically rely on single or sparse fixed-point temperature measurements, overlooking non-uniform indoor temperature distributions, transient thermal dynamics, and occupant-specific comfort requirements. This study explores an occupant-centric control strategy that aims to maintain the desired temperature around the occupant location. Spatially and temporally varying temperature fields, together with occupant mobility, make real-time local temperature estimation challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a control-oriented Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model for indoor temperature-field prediction. Conventional PINNs rely on explicit time inputs and assume consistent temporal patterns across samples, which limits adaptability under variable initial conditions and heating sequences. The proposed model infers temporal dynamics implicitly from spatial coordinates and limited sensor measurements, improving robustness to changes in initial conditions and external disturbances. The method was validated across nine horizontal sensing planes in three controlled room-scale configurations. Against a validated COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, the PINN predicted the evaluated temperature fields with a maximum relative error below 1.85% across validation cases. These predictions supported an occupant-centric space heating control scheme. Compared with COMSOL-based offline control, the PINN-based system achieved an average prediction error of around 0.67%, and its rapid inference supports real-time occupant-centric control implementation. This work represents a move away from reliance on fixed-point temperature measurements in space heating control to an occupant-centric control strategy informed by real-time environmental feedback.

papers.title: Beyond Imputation: Mask-Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Tree Embeddings on General Missing Data Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free framework for uncertainty quantification with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. Yet, missing values introduce distributional heterogeneity, where marginal coverage can hide systematic undercoverage for certain missingness patterns. At the same time, existing methods based on distances or smoothness require a continuous representation of partially observed covariates. Although imputation restores continuity, it obscures the missingness patterns and introduces task-dependent overhead. We develop a new CP framework that is \emph{adaptive to missingness patterns}, without imputing covariates. We rely on data augmentation by feature embedding that accounts for missingness. Our framework represents each input with missing values by a tree embedding together with its raw missingness mask, and then learns a regularized quantile score function. Varying the choices for the penalty function and the augmentation enables us to characterize three practically relevant validity levels: exact coordinate-wise validity, exact validity on observed masks, and approximate missingness-conditional guarantees for general mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support these guarantees and show that the proposed method reduces miscoverage risk while maintaining informative intervals, especially in non-MCAR settings. These results highlight the practical value of uncertainty quantification that adapts to missingness.

papers.title: Uniqueness of SRB measures for stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: For a dissipation stochastic differential equation (abbreviated as SDE), exponential ergodicity has been investigated a lot in a wide range of settings. In this paper, we prove that the Markovian measure $μ$ determined by the unique stationary measure is also the unique invariant measure which satisfies the entropy formula. Consequently, the existence of an SRB measure is completely determined by the sign of the sample top Lyapunov exponent of $μ$: if $χ_μ^1>0$, then $μ$ is the unique SRB measure, whereas if $χ_μ^1\leq0$, then the SDE admits no SRB measure. As an application, we establish a dichotomy of SRB measures for the 2D additive-noise stochastic Hopf normal form within a shear parameter domain.

papers.title: Symmetry energy effect on hot nuclear matter and proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: We examine the effects of symmetry energy on proto-neutron stars (PNSs) by employing equation of state (EOS) described by the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model. The thermal properties of dense matter and the bulk properties of PNSs are investigated under the assumptions of isothermy, isentropy, and fixed lepton fractions. The polytropic index is calculated at finite temperature, revealing a negative correlation with the PNS maximum mass that the EOS can support. The properties of PNSs during the heating and cooling stages along their evolution line are explored under different combinations of lepton fraction and entropy. We investigate the correlation between the symmetry energy slope $L$ and the properties of PNSs. As $L$ increases, the PNS radius also increases; however, this effect diminishes with a growing lepton fraction for the isentropic case. These results indicate that the nuclear symmetry energy and its density dependence play crucial roles in determining the properties of PNSs and their evolution stages.

papers.title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
papers.abstract: We study adapted finite-variation tracking of fractional Brownian motion under quadratic loss and proportional adjustment costs. For $H\in(0,1)$, \[ V_λ(T;a,b,σ)\underset{λ\downarrow0}{\sim}κ_HT a^{(1-H)/(1+H)}(λb)^{2H/(1+H)}σ^{2/(1+H)}. \] The positive long-run cell value $κ_H$ is unchanged by full past information. A bounded full-past reset correction yields finite-horizon bounds and continuity in $H$. The Brownian value is $κ_{1/2}=\frac12(\frac32)^{2/3}$. Coupling local paths with their filtrations gives a local limit, which we verify for Gaussian Volterra targets. Every asymptotically optimal control has the same leading tracking--variation cost split. Primal and dual bounds quantify the cell value. For $H<1/2$, we construct a positive-factor approximation and relate factor resolution to horizon length.

papers.title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. Specifically, we mine reusable collaboration structures from selected benchmark tasks at two levels. Local collaboration patterns capture recurring interactions among subtasks, while global task structures characterize how these interactions contribute to complete workflows. Through coarse-to-fine composition, these structures are recombined into task graphs combining different collaboration requirements. Tasks are instantiated in executable environments with automated verification of partial progress and complete task resolution.

papers.title: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
papers.abstract: Most robot policies, whether trained by imitation learning (IL) or reinforcement learning (RL), map observations to action values at discrete control steps and leave the continuity of physical motion to be learned implicitly. We propose ODE policy, which learns the dynamics of the action rather than the action itself. A neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) learns the vector field of the action by matching the integrated actions to the targets over short action chunks in IL and single control steps in RL. A lightweight diversity head captures multi-modal behavior by randomizing the direction of the field. At deployment, each action is integrated from the previous one, so the executed trajectory is continuous by construction. We evaluate it as a visuomotor policy, as the action head of vision-language-action (VLA) and world action models (WAMs), and as the actor of model-based RL against 14 baselines on unimanual, bimanual, dexterous, locomotion, and loco-manipulation tasks. In IL, against flow matching, it reaches 5.9$\times$ the success, 5.4$\times$ the generalization, and 3.9$\times$ the mode balance after one epoch, and generates actions 10.8$\times$ faster. It mostly moves more smoothly than human demonstrations. On 14 real-world tasks across single-arm, dual-arm, dexterous, and humanoid robots, it achieves the highest success rate. In RL, it further speeds up SuperMimic for humanoid motion tracking and smooths its actions. Efficient in learning, data, parameters, and execution, ODE policy offers a promising path to scaling robot learning.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Cervical Cytology Screening: Methods, Algorithms, Challenges and Prospects
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer death among women, with more than 90\% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries, where cytology screening is constrained by a shortage of trained cytopathologists. Deep learning has made automated cytology screening increasingly feasible, but the literature is fragmented across cell, patch and whole-slide-image scales, task formulations and supervision regimes, hindering comparison and clinical translation. This Review synthesizes the deep learning literature for cervical cytology screening, organizing the field along three axes---data scale, functional task and supervision---and distinguishing two clinical roadmaps: whole-slide-image confidence aggregation and cell-level detection with Bethesda classification. We examine 16 publicly available or publicly documented cytology datasets alongside the CAISHI histopathology dataset, compare quantitative performance while exposing incomparable metrics and data leakage, and assess commercial systems, regulatory status, HPV-era screening pathways and low-resource deployment. Single-cell accuracy on Herlev and SIPaKMeD has plateaued, but this reflects benchmark saturation rather than clinical readiness; prospective and randomized evidence is emerging but remains limited. We consolidate the evidence into five challenge areas---data and benchmarks, architecture and label-efficient learning, trustworthy AI, clinical translation and health economics, and evaluation and reproducibility---and provide an evidence-to-agenda map and a deployment decision matrix. Progress now depends on multi-center benchmarks, externally validated label-efficient methods, calibrated and fair predictions, and pragmatic clinical trials rather than further gains on saturated single-cell benchmarks.

papers.title: Robust EEG-based Emotion Recognition from Coarse Trial-level Labels under Intra-trial Affective Variability
papers.abstract: EEG-based emotion recognition has become an active research area in brain-computer interfaces. However, fine-grained affective annotation is costly, so most datasets provide only a global label for each long EEG trial. For practical emotion recognition, trials are commonly divided into short temporal windows, with the global label propagated to all windows for training. This practice treats trial-level emotion as temporally uniform, although affective responses may fluctuate within a trial. Consequently, windows that weakly reflect or deviate from the global emotional state may receive unreliable labels, posing a key challenge to robust EEG-based emotion recognition. To address this challenge, we propose VARY, a variability-aware robust learning framework for EEG-based emotion recognition from coarse trial-level labels. VARY incorporates a Two-stage Sample Selection (TSS) strategy to identify EEG windows with reliable emotional labels, and introduces MixAug, a data augmentation method tailored for EEG to improve model robustness under limited and unreliable supervision. We comprehensively evaluate VARY under the setting of label-noise learning on two public datasets, using three network architectures and multiple label-noise settings. Our method demonstrates superior performance, achieving a maximum accuracy gain of 11.54% on the DREAMER dataset and 5.39% on the SEED dataset compared with the best-performing baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of VARY in learning from unreliable trial-level labels under intra-trial affective variability.

papers.title: Decoherence suppression in quantum dense coding
papers.abstract: By harnessing entanglement to transmit information beyond the limits of classical communication, quantum dense coding serves as a key component in various quantum technologies. However, in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, noise-induced decoherence poses inevitable challenges to its practical implementation. By investigating the non-Markovian decoherence dynamics of the two categories of quantum dense coding protocols realized in discrete- and continuous-variable systems, we demonstrate a physical mechanism to suppress the decoherence in quantum dense coding. It is found that the formation of a bound state in the energy spectrum of the entire system consisting of each subsystem and its local environment of the quantum channel restores the quantum advantage of dense coding in the presence of decoherence. Refreshing our understanding on the noisy effect on quantum dense coding, our finding offers a guide toward the practical realization of noise-tolerant quantum dense coding.

papers.title: Less but Sufficient: Relation Knowledge Selects Compact Knowledge-Graph Contexts, and What External Checks Can and Cannot Catch
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) read knowledge-graph facts ranked by relevance, leaving open whether they suffice or conflict. Our checks use relation knowledge, written by hand or learned from training questions labelled with their relation paths. It selects a compact context of facts yielding an answer, and derives it; a derivability check tests whether an answer follows, a consistency check whether facts conflict, and a validation-chosen routing gate decides where the derived answer replaces the LLM's. Seven open LLMs read the compact context better in exact match than relevance-ranked facts; on ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ) they match SubgraphRAG's facts at a quarter of the prompt tokens, and stronger LLMs read SubgraphRAG's better. Where the routing gate passes, ours leads SubgraphRAG's in exact match in all 53 LLM, benchmark and prompt settings. A precision gate, returning the derived answer only when the check passes with exactly one derived entity, answered 18 and 5 percent of held-out WebQSP and CWQ questions in a pre-specified test, right for 90 and 96 percent. The consistency check judges facts by path evidence only where another path joins their entities, true of 2.5 percent of named-entity facts in our compact WebQSP and CWQ contexts.

papers.title: Optimal Control of Chemical Reaction Networks with Thermodynamic Cost
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic control seeks to realize desired functions at minimal thermodynamic cost, yet existing frameworks remain largely confined to slow driving regimes or state-to-state transport. Here we establish a thermodynamic optimal-control theory for Markov jump processes (MJPs) and chemical reaction networks (CRNs) that accommodates objectives over both states and reaction fluxes beyond slow-driving limit. By deriving the thermodynamic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we demonstrate that the optimal dynamics take the form of a perturbed generalized-gradient flow driven by the value function. A convex representation of the entropy-production rate via generalized means identifies its Legendre--Fenchel dual as the dissipation function. The resulting dynamics shares the thermodynamic structure of CRNs and admits an information-geometric characterization. We further derive a thermodynamic Pontryagin equation by recasting the control problem in terms of thermodynamic forces, providing a complementary description of optimal trajectories and clarifying connections to thermodynamic optimal transport. Our results establish a thermodynamic and geometric foundation for controlling MJPs and CRNs beyond mere transport, opening avenues for optimizing biological processes and finite-time thermodynamic operations in far-from-equilibrium regimes.

papers.title: CacheWeave: Learning to Recompute for Efficient Position-Independent KV Caching
papers.abstract: Position-independent caching reuses chunk KV caches across positions and requests. Independent encoding, however, omits cross-chunk interactions and can degrade accuracy. In our study, neither PIC training nor rule-based recomputation, alone or combined, consistently recovers full-prefill accuracy. Oracle-guided recomputation on PIC-trained models improves accuracy at the same budget, motivating better selection. We present CacheWeave, which adapts the full backbone to PIC, then freezes it and trains a model-native block selector on the adapted model's oracles. The selector uses compact cached chunk features and question hidden states without extracting backbone attention scores. It selects contiguous token blocks aligned with KV blocks to support efficient recomputation and limit copy-on-write amplification. Its runtime, CacheWeave-Serve, supports private and shared KV caches, keeps selection and recomputation on the GPU, and stages sliding-window KV for hybrid attention models. Across three models and four tasks, CacheWeave outperforms CacheBlend and ProphetKV by 7.2 and 3.5 percentage points on average at a 5% recomputation budget, with a mean relative accuracy loss of 1.6% to full prefill. With 32-token blocks, CacheWeave-Serve cuts single-request TTFT by up to 16.1x over full prefill and 1.7x over ProphetKV, and raises SLO goodput under load by up to 7.8x.

papers.title: RSI-Env: An Open-Ended Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agents
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) envisions agent systems that autonomously improve their own models and harnesses, with each updated system continuing to improve itself. Existing approaches typically restrict optimization objectives, editable components, or evaluation procedures, limiting open-ended exploration and continuity across generations. We introduce RSI-Env, a persistent environment for coordinated model-harness improvement, supporting autonomous training, harness modification, and retention of research state. An independent Host Controller manages services, evaluation, and versioning. Under Self, each accepted model-harness version takes over the next improvement round. We define three settings that vary goal specificity and access to benchmark feedback: Open-General, Capability-Directed, and Benchmark-Guided. Across these three settings, we compare Self with two fixed external Teachers on seven tasks, starting from Qwen3.8-27B with a minimal harness. Without benchmark feedback, Open-General Self raises GPQA Diamond accuracy from 65.2% to 73.2% and AIME 2026 accuracy from 53.3% to 56.7%. All three Capability-Directed Self runs achieve target-aligned gains. Knowledge Self demonstrates continued improvement across system updates, with SimpleQA accuracy rising from 82.0% to 85.0% and then 88.0%. Benchmark guidance and Teacher benefits vary by task. These results demonstrate RSI-Env's support for open-ended exploration and sustained recursive improvement within the studied runs, while highlighting challenges in preserving gains across capabilities.

papers.title: Mitigating sloppiness with intermediate controls in sequential multiparameter spin interferometry
papers.abstract: Multiparameter quantum sensing requires different parameters to produce distinguishable probe responses while allowing their information to be extracted simultaneously. In sequential sensing without intermediate control, two phases encoded through the same generator are locally indistinguishable. Here we show that parameter-independent intermediate controls overcome this limitation in a collective-spin interferometer by separating the corresponding effective generators in the probe covariance geometry. Specifically, a transverse collective rotation provides an analytically tractable realization, and intermediate one-axis twisting (OAT) generates additional nonlinear operator directions and a broad regime of enhanced joint estimation. For fixed total particle number $N$ and matched twisting resource, both marginal precision bounds lie below those of a separated-OAT strategy while measurement incompatibility remains weak. For intermediate OAT, conditional optimization of an upper bound on the Holevo cost yields asymptotic $N^{-2}$ scaling. For this protocol, a fixed rotated-Dicke measurement retains simultaneous two-parameter enhancement over a broad phase region. These results show that nonlinear intermediate control can mitigate sloppiness while preserving quantum-enhanced precision with a common readout.

papers.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. In particular we develop an observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. In particular, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. We provide an explicit easy-to-implement observer design guaranteeing convergence. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of same dispersive water-wave models.

papers.title: Expected Minimax Regret Rates for Adaptive LQG Control on Fixed Parameter Sets
papers.abstract: We study how a fixed model family determines expected minimax regret in adaptive LQG control. The family is compact and affine, with partial observation and unknown noise covariances. We quantify how information from residual covariances and input responses can vanish relative to differences between optimal control laws. This relation yields matching bounds that classify regret as bounded, logarithmic, sublinear polynomial or linear. Polynomial exponents are rational. For real algebraic model and cost data, a terminating procedure determines the regret class and the exact exponent of polynomial growth before data collection. A causal policy attains these rates using model estimation and bounded probes, reselecting model sets from observations without a supplied common stabilizer. For costs with fixed positive definite output and input weights, polynomial exponents are at most one half.

papers.title: How Does Chain-of-Thought Supervision Teach Models to Reason? A Theoretical Analysis
papers.abstract: Training with chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision is an effective approach for teaching models multi-step reasoning procedures. At inference time, however, models may need to continue reasoning beyond the finite teacher CoT sequences observed during training, and longer reasoning can instead degrade performance, a phenomenon known as overthinking. How the amount and structure of training-time CoT give rise to such failures remains theoretically poorly understood. To study this problem, we introduce an in-context weight prediction model trained on finite gradient descent trajectories for linear regression. Using high-dimensional asymptotic analysis, we show that the success and failure modes of long-horizon reasoning undergo phase transitions depending on the context length and the total amount of training CoT. We further distinguish two mechanisms of overthinking, error accumulation and error amplification, and show that with short training contexts, increasing the training CoT budget can worsen long-horizon error before eventually stabilizing reasoning. Experiments with fully trained linear and multi-head softmax attention further show that these qualitative behaviors persist. Our results provide a theoretical account linking properties of training-time CoT to inference-time failures and offer guidance for designing teacher CoT that supports stable reasoning.

papers.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.title: From Single-Agent Self-Discovery to Multi-Agent Adaptation: Scaling Laws of Partner Feedback and Convention Rigidity in Meta Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
papers.abstract: A key milestone toward Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) is replacing hand-crafted optimizers with meta-learned update rules (such as Disco103 and OPEN) that discover how agents learn. Yet when a self-discovered RL model trains with adapting teammates, does co-evolution sustain capability gains or trap agents in brittle conventions? Across 1,800+ runs in continuous collective robotics (VMAS) and discrete coordination (Overcooked), we establish five laws of multi-agent adaptation. First, four-cell counterfactual partner swaps expose an evaluation illusion: apparent team progress often masks focal regression (+1.066 team gain concealing -0.119 focal loss) and inflates transfer by +0.649 to +1.210. Second, a 288-run physical-coupling sweep ($α\in [0, 1.5]$) reveals a linear scaling law ($β= +0.255$, $p = 0.000488$, Spearman $ρ= 1.0$): live reciprocal feedback keeps Disco103 invariant (AUC 0.297--0.322), whereas severing feedback triggers a monotonic collapse (-0.172 to -0.490), with OPEN establishing a sensitivity spectrum (Disco103 > OPEN > MAPPO). Third, extending navigation training eightfold (1.05M steps) enables Disco103 to overtake MAPPO (+0.087 team return, +0.133 bank gain), while decoupled training boosts cross-partner completion by +10.16% (56.25% vs. 46.09%). Fourth, in Overcooked, MAPPO's self-play conventions induce a 28.13% cross-partner collision rate, whereas Disco103 cuts collisions to 12.77% and achieves 3.33x higher bank return (9.96 vs. 2.99; net gain +6.43), further improved by decoupled meta-adaptation (+1.39 with scripted partners). Finally, perturbation pulses ($p=0.00098$), auxiliary entropy diagnostics (8.485 nats), and 48 multi-lifetime meta-evolved rules ($L_2 \in [2.11, 4.91]$) trace these dynamics to partner-gradient blindness and auxiliary drift, informing multi-agent self-discoverd algorithms.

papers.title: VeriBase: Automated Construction of Theorem Libraries for Software Verification
papers.abstract: Software verification is typically more challenging than coding. Software developers routinely build on mature libraries and APIs, but turning successful verification solutions into reusable libraries still requires substantial expert effort. In this paper, we propose VeriBase, a framework for automatically constructing software-verification libraries by jointly generalizing code and its associated theorems from successful verification solutions. The key challenge is to generalize implementations together with the theorem statements and proofs that depend on these implementations, and reconcile overlapping components across verification tasks. To this end, VeriBase treats code and its associated theorems as declaration families, and designs a three-phase pipeline, which proves seed tasks, generalizes code and associated theorems, and harvests the resulting families into shared interfaces. VeriBase updates dependent declarations as interface change and uses Lean to check the resulting code and proofs. We evaluate VeriBase across four benchmarks with three backend LLMs. The results show that the general-purpose library built from independent 4,191 programs increases the average task success rate by up to 17.0% and meanwhile reduces the proof completion time by up to 21.4%. When VeriBase constructs a benchmark-specific library, further improvement can be observed.

papers.title: Convex Regression at Scale: Geometry-Preserving Constraint Sparsification
papers.abstract: Convex regression provides a flexible nonparametric estimation framework while incorporating appropriate shape information. However, its standard least-squares formulation has $O(n^2)$ supporting-hyperplane constraints creating a computational bottleneck as the sample size $n$ increases. We study a $K$-nearest-neighbor (KNN) localized relaxation for convex regression where we for each sample, we only maintain the $K$ nearest hyperplane constraints. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish statistical guarantees for our modified estimator in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. In particular, for $d>4$, the population risk of our modified problem can be shown to have equivalent convergence rates as the original least square convex regression estimator of $\widetilde O(n^{-2/d})$ using neighborhoods sizes (i.e. $K=K_n$) of order $\widetilde O(n^{2(d-1)/(2d-1)})$ for general convex functions and $\widetilde O(n^{(d+1)/(d+2)})$ for strongly convex functions. To corroborate our theory, we implement iterative optimization methods to compare the prediction accuracy of the KNN relaxation with those of the full estimator across synthetic convex benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that KNN prediction risk approaches the full-estimator prediction risk at neighborhood sizes matching the theoretical scale.

papers.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-$1$ Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions generate a spin-nematic squeezed state in the $m_F=\pm1$ modes. The resulting pair-correlated state has a rank-one quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for the two mode phases relative to the $m_F=0$ mode and therefore cannot resolve them independently. Nevertheless, we find that a parameter-independent passive three-mode transformation lifts this rank deficiency and enables joint estimation of both phases. In the undepleted-pump regime, we derive expressions for the QFIM, optimize the equal-weight multiparameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound, and obtain a full-rank probe with squeezing-enhanced sensitivity below the matched fixed-total-number standard quantum limit (SQL). These analytical predictions are confirmed by exact-diagonalization calculations. We further construct a parameter-independent readout that maps the phase combinations onto displacement channels accessible through atomic homodyne or parity measurements. Our results provide a route from spin-mixing-generated quantum correlations to two-phase estimation in spinor condensates.

papers.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Self-evolving agents accumulate experience from task streams, but existing frameworks typically rely on fixed pipelines to retrieve and utilize this experience, neglecting when and how to deploy it. We introduce Online Meta-Control of Experience (OMCE), a framework that updates experience memory and learns a meta-control policy from task feedback during test-time adaptation. OMCE employs a lightweight contextual-bandit meta-controller that uses compact retrieval signals to select among four cognitive actions: DIRECT, EPISODE, GUIDE, and DISTILL. This routing mechanism operationalizes three coupled decisions: whether to invoke experience, which memory format to utilize, and when to consolidate new guidance. OMCE evolves online, leveraging task feedback to update the memory bank and refine the routing policy via contextual bandit updates. Experiments on four online adaptation benchmarks across four backbones show that OMCE improves first-attempt success by up to 20.5 percentage points over the strongest compared baseline, while reducing per-task token use by a factor of 5.7 to 62.5 relative to ACE with GPT-5.2. Controlled ablations further support the benefits of learned routing and continued routing policy adaptation.

papers.title: CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control
papers.abstract: Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

papers.title: An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems
papers.abstract: Physical restrictions on operations can make quantum coherence inaccessible. Quantifying off-diagonal density matrix elements in a chosen basis alone does not reveal which information is hidden by each restriction. To distinguish their effects, we describe physical restrictions through subalgebras of accessible observables. The associated trace-preserving conditional expectations unify two reconstruction principles: each gives both the maximum-entropy state compatible with the accessible data and the closest state in the corresponding subalgebra in relative entropy. We apply this framework to anyonic systems to separate the contributions from local-charge superselection and non-Abelian fusion rules. We prove that the charge-line severing map is the conditional expectation onto the local-product subalgebra. It is completely positive and quantum-trace-preserving, and uniquely reconstructs a state in this space from all local-product expectation values. The hierarchy of measurement restrictions then separates total bipartite coherence into three nonnegative contributions: coherence between local charges, inaccessible fusion information, and conventional coherence. The first two decompose the anyonic charge entanglement and distinguish the effects of local-charge superselection from the remaining fusion information. Finally, we relate basis-independent measures of anyonic coherence to entanglement. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.

papers.title: The maximum concentration of results in incomplete round-robin tournaments
papers.abstract: The Herfindahl--Hirschman Index (HHI), a standard measure of market concentration, is widely used to quantify competitive balance in sports tournaments. To enable comparisons over time or across leagues, both its minimum and maximum should be known. The minimum is usually trivial. Our paper provides results on the maximum HHI in incomplete round-robin tournaments, where the set of matches is represented by a regular but not complete undirected graph. We prove that the lower bound of maximum HHI is reached when the tournament consists of independent round-robin groups, while the upper bound of maximum HHI is reached when the set of matches is represented by a bipartite graph. Maximising HHI is computationally difficult even for highly structured graph types corresponding to real-world tournaments, where the teams are partitioned into pots and play the same number of matches against opponents from every pot. The complexity of the problem does not depend on the scoring system or the number of opponents from a pot.

papers.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Real-Time Electric Vehicle Charging Management in IoEV-Enabled Smart Cities
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) in urban environments demands intelligent, decentralised charging management strategies that operate under strict real-time constraints. This paper proposes an Edge-Intelligent architecture in which each EV selects a charging station (CS) by querying a shared, centrally trained Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy over a lightweight MQTT publish-subscribe backbone; independent per-EV edge inference is the deployment target, not the configuration evaluated here. The reported simulation evaluates that shared DQN policy applied sequentially to each vehicle's observations within a single SUMO run, using MQTT for KPI telemetry while observations are obtained through TraCI. The system is evaluated on two real-world road networks from OpenStreetMap (Rabat Agdal-Hay Riad and Tangier, Morocco); the primary network carries four geolocated public charging stations with heterogeneous power levels (50 kW and 150 kW). Three traffic demand profiles (morning, midday, evening peak) are simulated, and four decision policies are compared: an Adaptive Heuristic, a Tabular Q-Learning agent, the proposed DQN agent, and a Double DQN variant. A multi-seed statistical protocol (7 seeds, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Cohen's d) evaluates the results. The DQN agent achieves a 6.8% relative improvement in charge rate and a 5.4% increase in delivered energy over the Adaptive Heuristic under Evening Peak demand ($p = 0.016$, Cohen's $d = 0.99$ and $1.51$), while showing no advantage in waiting time; on the second network the heuristic leads on waiting time, so the ranking is not stable across geographies. A scalability analysis shows linear state-space growth with station count and sub-millisecond inference; all runs include intermittent station outages under a Markov failure process.

papers.title: From Logs to Faults: Reference-Free Fault Localization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Pipelines
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines are widely used for domain-specific question answering, yet locating faults remains manual and time-consuming. Fault localization is challenging because RAG pipelines consist of interdependent stages, where faults can propagate downstream, masking their origin, or remain undetected even when the final answer is correct. Existing evaluation approaches often focus on individual stages and rely on reference answers or code instrumentation. We present RAGLog, which detects and localizes faults across RAG stages using execution logs, without requiring reference answers or code instrumentation. RAGLog transforms heterogeneous API logs into a common RAG schema and combines rule-based, embedding-based, and LLM-based checks to identify faulty stages. We introduce a live fault injector and RAGLog Faults, a dataset of 3,134 runs from five RAG pipelines with stage-level fault labels. With Claude Haiku 5.5, RAGLog achieves a pooled F1 score of 0.73 on runs with naturally occurring faults, outperforming Claude Code (0.58) and Codex (0.52), and comparable effectiveness on runs with injected faults (0.84 versus 0.80 and 0.82, respectively). It analyzes runs in approximately five seconds at US\$0.005 each, with overall lower cost and latency than agent baselines. RAGLog is available as an open-source tool for debugging, evaluating, and monitoring RAG pipelines.

papers.title: On Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport Filter and its Multilevel Variants
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of filtering partially observed diffusions associated to discrete time observations. This problem requires the development of advanced numerical methods such as particle filters. In this article we develop a new sequential entropic optimal transport filter (EOTF). The main idea is to sample from successive couplings of the filters. To achieve this, we adopt the approach of an entropic optimal transport (EOT) update implemented through a learned Schrödinger potential, in the spirit of the light Schrödinger bridge methodology \cite{korotin2024light}. Based on this, we develop a multilevel version of this filter (ML-EOTF) in which consecutive discretization levels are coupled at the terminal time by a scaled EOT plan with level-dependent regularization $\eps_l=\eps_0 h_l^κ$ with discretization stepsize $h_l$. Under mild conditions, we show that the level-difference estimator with exact Schrödinger potentials has variance of order $N_l^{-1}\{h_l^β+\eps_l\}$, where $β$ is the strong-error for the discretized SDE. The analysis is then extended to learned potentials, with all approximation and optimization errors summarized by a joint Kullback--Leibler discrepancy whose contribution to the mean squared error is explicitly quantified. Combined with a fixed-time weak-error estimate, this yields the canonical multilevel complexity $\cO(δ^{-2}|\logδ|^2)$ to achieve an MSE of $δ^2$ for Euler--Maruyama discretizations. Numerical experiments validate the results.

papers.title: ReCoG: Relative Node Contexts for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training
papers.abstract: The success of foundation models in language and vision has motivated Graph Foundation Models (GFMs), which learn transferable knowledge through multi-domain graph pre-training. Existing methods advance GFMs through feature unification and structural learning, and in doing so they rely on the raw graph structure to organize node contexts. However, we observe that removing a large proportion of edges from source graphs during pre-training improves cross-domain transfer accuracy across four representative methods. Our theoretical analysis identifies the raw graph structure as a source of conflict in cross-graph model sharing. We therefore advocate defining node contexts using criteria consistent across graphs. Achieving this requires (1) constructing node contexts consistently across graphs without a shared positional structure, such as the token order of text or the pixel grid of images, and (2) retaining the structural and neighborhood information of the original graphs. To this end, we introduce Relative Contexts for Graphs (ReCoG) for multi-domain graph pre-training. Specifically, we first construct attribute contexts to provide a comparison rule independent of the raw graph structure. Furthermore, we construct structural contexts based on common neighbors and semantic contexts based on neighborhood attribute summaries to retain the topological and neighborhood information of the original graphs. Since all graphs share these construction rules, we pre-train a single graph encoder by reconstructing node attributes over these contexts, without domain-specific modules. We conduct extensive experiments on 18 target datasets, which demonstrate the effectiveness of ReCoG. In particular, ReCoG exceeds the strongest baseline by 7.61 percentage points in mean 1-shot cross-domain node classification accuracy and by 4.47 points in cross-type transfer to heterophilous graphs.

papers.title: Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.

papers.title: A Bounded Evaluation Protocol for Representational Systematicity
papers.abstract: Multiple studies have shown that neural networks can be behaviorally systematic, producing correct outputs for novel combinations of familiar parts. Whether they are also representationally systematic, that is, whether they represent these parts and their roles and use them to produce the outputs, remains hard to test, because each kind of evidence can mislead on its own: correct outputs can come from shortcuts, a decodable signal need not be used, an intervention can act through unintended pathways, and a failed search does not show absence. We propose a bounded evaluation protocol for representational systematicity (Bounded-RS): for an explanation that attributes a systematic behavior to a declared representation, it tests on a matched behavioral contrast whether that representation is recoverable and whether it is causally used, checks the validity of this evidence, and assigns the explanation one of four bounded states, Unsupported, Present-only, Causal-use, or Undetermined, through control-calibrated scores, gates, and stop rules. On a semantic-parsing testbed of 96 matched sets that we release, the tested role-filler Binding explanation of fine-tuned T5 models is Causal-use and the distributed Geometry explanation is Unsupported within its declared search space, verdicts that hold across calibration-compatible parameter configurations, training seeds, and T5-base. On 41 cases with known causal status, full adjudication licenses a false Causal-use in 1 of 34 noncausal cases, against 13 when recoverability is taken as use, without missing any causal case. Bounded-RS thus turns the question of representational systematicity, debated since Fodor and Pylyshyn, into comparable and falsifiable verdicts on declared explanations, each reported with the evidence pattern that licenses it and, for a negative, the search space that bounds it.

papers.title: Stochastic Orders of the Exit Pair and the Monotone Response to Resetting
papers.abstract: Resetting a process, that is, restarting it from its initial position at random times, changes the probability that it leaves an interval through one end rather than the other. We show that the direction of this change is governed by how the exit time depends on the exit side, and we express this through classical stochastic orders. For random walks and birth-death chains we determine when resetting more intensively always moves the exit probability in the same direction, and we show that this can fail: we give an explicit chain in which the direction reverses twice over time, and bound the number of such reversals spectrally. We also show how the direction depends on the starting point. In the continuum limit we obtain the corresponding results for diffusions with drift.

papers.title: Spatially-Guided Speaker Extraction Based on Relative Position Cues
papers.abstract: We present a multi-channel target speaker extraction (TSE) framework that is guided by relative spatial cues rather than explicit speaker-dependent references, such as clean enrollment utterances or precise directions of arrival (DOA). The proposed approach encodes the target speaker through discrete, interpretable relations between concurrent speakers, such as left and right or near and far, referred to as the Relative Position Cue (RPC). This relational conditioning effectively leverages spatial information while avoiding explicit DOA estimation, thereby enabling more robust operation under realistic conditions.
