papers.abstract: We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$ The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks. A positional encoding of the finite-field moment curve has $q$ elements in an interval of length $O_h(q^h)$, while, for each $1\leq r<h$, sums arising from distinct $r$-element multisets are separated by more than $q$. This separation allows whole blocks to be appended to a prescribed finite set without a further dilation. In particular, our result gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Szemerédi \cite{szemeredi}.

papers.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Linear Programming
papers.abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman-Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale linear programming problems. We first introduce the semi-proximal HPR framework and summarize its convergence guarantees, together with its connections to Halpern PDHG and ergodic Peaceman-Rachford iterations. To improve practical performance, we develop adaptive restart and penalty parameter update strategies. We then describe several computational enhancements, including GPU-based preprocessing, diagonal scaling, reusable execution plans for sparse matrix-vector multiplication, and sieving techniques. We further discuss multi-GPU parallelization and lossless model storage and loading for handling large-scale instances. These developments form the foundation of HPR-LP, a GPU-accelerated solver for large-scale linear programming.

papers.title: Interaction-Enabled Bulk-Boundary Correspondence without a Global Band Gap
papers.abstract: A challenge of growing interest is how to make topology observable when conventional gap-based frameworks no longer suffice. In bulk-edge correspondence, this challenge arises when the global band gap closes and localized boundary modes disappear, even though the bulk topology remains intact. Here we show that interactions unlock a novel emergent boundary response from this spectrally hidden topology without reopening the global band gap. These interaction-induced excitations originate from a bulk-band minimum, yet reconstruct the characteristic boundary channels of a gapped topological parent sharing the same Bloch eigenspaces. We establish this interaction-enabled bulk-boundary correspondence for first- and higher-order topology in one- and two-dimensional bosonic lattices, respectively, and identify a general compatibility principle governing its emergence. Our results extend bulk-boundary correspondence beyond its conventional spectral manifestation, with experimental prospects in cold-atom and photonic platforms.

papers.title: Efficient Lempel-Ziv Prediction with the Run-Length BWT
papers.abstract: Lempel-Ziv Plurality (LZP) is an algorithm of Kosoy that predicts the next symbol of a string by using its Lempel-Ziv factorization, and makes at most $O(z\log n)$ mistakes on every string of length $n$ with $z$ LZ77 phrases. We give efficient online implementations of LZP and of a new variant of it. Our first implementation maintains a run-length encoded Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) of the reversed history. It implements LZP, uses $O(z\log z\log^2 n)$ bits, and has worst-case update and prediction times $O(\log z+\log\log n)$ and $O(σ(\log z+\log\log n))$, respectively, where $σ$ is the size of the alphabet. This is an exponential improvement over Kosoy's implementation, whose update time is $O(z\log^7 n)$. We then introduce the Lempel-Ziv Majority (LZM) predictor, which has the same mistake bound and update time, and predicts in $O(1)$ time independently of $σ$. These two predictors accept new symbols at any time, without knowing the alphabet in advance. For an alphabet known in advance, a different data structure gives $O(σ(1+\log z/\log\log n))$ time per symbol, which is constant when $σ=O(1)$ and $z=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$.

papers.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum-Weight Degree-Bounded Forests
papers.abstract: In the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem, we are given a graph with nonnegative edge weights and a degree upper bound on each vertex. The objective is to find a maximum-weight forest satisfying the degree bounds. We show that this problem admits a simple $2$-approximation via the greedy algorithm. This already improves over the best-known guarantees obtained via a reduction to weighted $3$-matroid parity, and sets a baseline to improve upon. Our main result is an $\frac{8}{5}$-approximation algorithm for the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem. For the special case of uniform degree bounds, our algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of $\frac{3}{2}$. It computes two sets of edges, each of which we then restrict to a feasible solution in an optimal way, and finally returns the better of the two resulting solutions. To obtain the initial two edge sets, we first relax the degree bounds and leverage an algorithm by Lau and Singh [JACM'15] for degree-bounded spanning trees, and second we relax the forest constraints and employ an algorithm for maximum-weight $b$-matchings.

papers.title: Acoustic and Attentional Challenges Shape the Balance Between Attended and Competing Speech Tracking Differently
papers.abstract: Selective attention enhances cortical tracking of attended speech, but the role of ignored speech remains less clear. In particular, it is unknown whether attended and ignored speech contribute to cortical tracking in a fixed balance or whether this balance changes with listening conditions. We addressed this question across six electroencephalography (EEG) datasets spanning acoustic and attentional challenges, hearing impairment, and hearing-aid processing. We systematically varied the relative weighting of attended and competing speech and studied how their combined contribution affected cortical speech tracking. Across most listening conditions, cortical tracking was improved when we included competing speech, compared with attended speech alone. Importantly, the balance between attended and competing speech changed across conditions. Increasing acoustic difficulty increased both the benefit and the optimal contribution of competing speech, with the same general pattern observed in normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners. In the hearing-aid datasets examining noise-reduction conditions, the contribution of competing speech was more limited. Attentional challenges also changed the contribution of competing speech, but differently from acoustic challenges. These findings show that attended and competing speech do not contribute to cortical tracking in a fixed balance. Rather, their balance depends on the listening challenge. Although these results do not define a single optimal ratio, they provide a step toward hearing devices that adapt not only to the attended talker, but also to how competing speech is balanced in complex listening environments.

papers.title: On $W^{2,1}$-Regularity for Rivière's System with a Local Hardy Drift
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the endpoint regularity of weak solutions to the inhomogeneous Rivière system $$ -Δu=Ω\cdot\nabla u+f \qquad\text{in }B_1\subset\mathbb R^2, $$ with an antisymmetric potential $Ω\in L^2$ and a local Hardy drift term $f\in h^1$. We construct a continuous solution in $W_0^{1,2}$, which fails to belong to $W^{2,1}$ in every neighborhood of the origin, even when $\|Ω\|_{L^2}$ is arbitrarily small. Smooth truncations further show that the corresponding uniform interior $W^{2,1}$ estimate fails even for smooth solutions and coefficients. Thus, the $L\log L$ assumption ensuring local $W^{2,1}$ regularity cannot in general be replaced by componentwise local Hardy data.

papers.title: Don't Guess, Ask Wisely: Benchmarking and Training Proactive Elicitation in Open-Domain LLM Conversations
papers.abstract: When user queries are incomplete, large language models should ask targeted questions before committing to an answer, a capability we call proactive elicitation, yet evaluation on real user-assistant queries across seven LLMs (8B to frontier) shows that fewer than 11% of underspecified queries trigger a follow-up question. To benchmark and train this capability, we introduce VagueBench, where each seed query is annotated with structured intent and detail units then degraded into intent-vague and fully-vague variants via controlled removal of linguistic cues, yielding known hidden information sets for evaluating both when and what to ask. We propose DialogGRPO, an offline reinforcement learning method that organizes multi-turn elicitation as a dialogue-state directed acyclic graph, where candidate questions at each node receive dense turn-level rewards combining immediate information gain with lookahead value through group-relative comparison, enabling fine-grained credit assignment without runtime simulation. DialogGRPO elicits missing information on over 88% of vague queries with substantial gains in both recovery efficiency and answer coverage, without over-asking on complete queries, outperforms prompting and test-time-scaling baselines, and generalizes zero-shot to MultiWOZ 2.4 and AmbigQA.

papers.title: Graphs Have Structure: Declarative Manifolds, 3D Z-Order Monoid Roll-ups, and Zero-Simulation Visual Analytics in a Graph DBMS
papers.abstract: Every real-world graph is embedded in an ambient structural manifold: proteins fold in Euclidean space ($R^3$), telecom networks sit on a planetary surface ($S^2 \times R$), and ontologies and calendars form discrete subsumption posets ($(V, \sqsubseteq)$). Yet property graph databases treat node coordinates as opaque payload scalars, leave spatial proximity edges unindexed, and force visualizers into $O(V^2)$ client-side force-directed simulations that destroy true geometry and truncate hierarchy roll-ups. We elevate ambient manifold structure to a first-class primitive in Samyama Graph. First, we introduce a declarative and auto-detected structural convention contract (samyama.structure/1) persisted in .sgsnap headers that binds node labels to Euclidean 3D, Geo-Spherical, Causal Spacetime, or Poset Hierarchy manifolds. Second, we show that both discrete posets (via Order-Embedded Hierarchy $[tin, tout]$ DFS intervals) and continuous 3D manifolds (via a 63-bit 3D Morton Z-order Structural-Geometric Index, SGI) reduce regional aggregation to 1D rank-interval monoid folds answered directly from index-resident Fenwick trees (SUM, COUNT) and Segment Trees (MIN, MAX). At $100,000$ 3D nodes, SGI builds in $28.14$ ms and answers Morton-interval SUM and MAX roll-ups in $0.048\,μ$s and $0.104\,μ$s---$8,345.1\times$ and $3,824.4\times$ faster than property scans. Third, we introduce 3D voxel-hashed virtual contact edges weighted by Topological--Geometric Stress $σ(u,v) = d_{graph}(u,v) / d_{manifold}(u,v)$ to isolate long-range tertiary folds, plus manifold-guided $A^*$ shortest-path search that cuts explored states by up to $3.80\times$ over Dijkstra. Fourth, we replace client layout simulation with server-computed 3D Cone-Tree/Ribbon coordinates and a non-WebGL 2.5D Isometric projection with painter's-order depth sorting and sub-millisecond Level-of-Detail (LoD) macro-cuts.

papers.title: Ray-Tracing-Parameter-Based Lightweight Hybrid Precoding via Cascade XGBoost for Wideband Massive MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.abstract: Hybrid precoding reduces the radio-frequency (RF) hardware burden in wideband massive MIMO-OFDM systems, but conventional optimization and deep neural network (DNN)-based approaches can incur high online complexity. This paper proposes XGB-SVD, a lightweight hybrid precoding framework that maps compact ray-tracing path parameters directly to analog beamforming codeword indices using cascade eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The cascade captures sequential beam-selection dependencies and transmit--receive propagation correlation, while the digital precoder and combiner are obtained from the reduced-dimensional equivalent channel using singular value decomposition (SVD). Evaluations over five DeepMIMO scenarios spanning sub-6-GHz and millimeter-wave bands show that XGB-SVD consistently outperforms the considered DNN baselines and approaches simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) in several environments. Cross-scenario results further indicate improved transfer from propagation-diverse training environments, while XGB-SVD provides lower online computational and training costs than the DNN baselines.

papers.title: Green Learning-Based Signal-Level Detection of RIS Spoofing Attacks in Vehicular ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless infrastructure to jointly support communication and environmental sensing, but also introduces new physical-layer security threats. A malicious reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can manipulate its time-varying reflection phases to generate spoofing echoes and distort the sensing results of a roadside unit (RSU). Existing trajectory-level detectors rely on reconstructed sensing parameters and vehicle trajectories, making their performance dependent on upstream estimation accuracy. In this paper, we propose a signal-level Green Learning (GL) framework that directly detects RIS spoofing from matched-filtered RSU echoes. The proposed method combines two-stage Subspace Approximation with Adjusted Bias (SAAB), Discriminant Feature Test (DFT), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for spatial-temporal representation learning, feature selection, and classification, respectively. Simulation results show 99.335\% detection accuracy for a 32-element malicious RIS at $-80$ dBm receiver noise power. GL remains competitive with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) baselines while requiring only 0.1119 million floating-point operations (FLOPs), and also generalizes to previously unseen RIS sizes.

papers.title: Convergence of the Calabi flow on Kähler surfaces with bounded Sobolev constants
papers.abstract: We study global Calabi flows $g(t)$ on compact Kähler surfaces with a uniform Sobolev constant. For any sequence $t_j\to\infty$, set $g_j(t):=g(t_j+t)$. After passing to a subsequence, these flows converge to an eternal Calabi flow on a compact extremal Kähler orbifold surface. The convergence holds in the spacetime $\hat C^\infty$-Cheeger--Gromov topology: it is uniform in the Gromov--Hausdorff sense on compact time intervals and smooth away from the orbifold singularities, using comparisons fixed in time.

papers.title: Propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam with conserved topology
papers.abstract: We report the generation and control of a propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam through the digitally controlled superposition of a first-order petal- and Gaussian- mode each marked with orthogonal polarizations. We present a detailed analysis of the spatial and polarization profiles and unveil their intricate topological features, showing that they have properties that are invariant to the propagation dynamics, in addition to their preserved intensity. The differential Gouy phase between the spatial components is shown to rotate the great circle traced by the polarisation distribution on the Poincaré sphere. Finally, we assess the beams for laser cutting and optical trapping, highlighting the relevance of topological structured light to these applications.

papers.title: The Runtime-Moment Frontier for Universal Sampling
papers.abstract: Can one sampler give every string at least a polynomial fraction of the probability that any source in a class gives it, while keeping a bounded moment of its own runtime? We answer this in terms of runtime moments. For every oracle and every rational $a>0$, one sampler with polynomial $a$th runtime moment dominates every source with polynomial $r$th moment with power $B(a,r)=1+(a-\min\{r,1\})_+/r$, and the Rényi divergence of order $B/(B-1)$ of the source from it is $O(\log n)$, a sharp quantitative form of Gurevich's domination on average. Relative to an oracle, $B(a,r)$ is optimal in both senses, with failures at every large input length. So the first moment is a threshold: one sampler of order one is universal for expected polynomial time, but none of higher order is universal even for polynomial-space sources with all polynomial moments. For expected-polynomial-time sources the threshold also holds relative to a random oracle and, without an oracle, under a sequential-hardness hypothesis on iterated functions or a parallel-sequentiality hypothesis on verifiable delay functions with short seeds. The frontier governs algorithms as well. For rational orders we determine the exact exponent by which polynomial runtime moments of deterministic deciders transfer from one fixed sampler to every source, and show, relative to oracles, that all correct solvers of a sparse language in $\mathsf{UP}\cap\mathsf{coUP}$ meet it. Where $B(a,r)=1$, actual running times transfer better than arbitrary costs, but only above a critical moment.

papers.title: Fractional quantum Hall effect at ν=1/2 in wide GaAs quantum wells: Subband structure, exact diagonalization, and the magnitude of the gap
papers.abstract: Recent experiments on a wide GaAs quantum well report a fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor ν=1/2 with an unusually large activation gap, a sharp maximum of the gap as a function of density, and a possible transition from the non-Abelian Moore-Read Pfaffian to the Abelian Halperin 331 state. We analyze this system theoretically, with self-consistent subband calculations, exact diagonalization, and a reanalysis of the published transport data. We find that the well has two relevant subbands, that with the second subband frozen out the well most likely has no incompressible state at ν=1/2, that a strict bilayer at the maxima of the charge density does not produce 331, and that an active second subband is essential: the ground state is a paired state of electrons in both subbands, on a continuous path between the Pfaffian and 331, with a neutral gap much larger than that of a one-subband Pfaffian. The position of the state on this path is controlled by electrostatic energies that the accessible system sizes contain only in part, and the standard overlaps do not identify the state at these sizes. Our results are more consistent with a Pfaffian-like state than with 331, but they are not definitive. The transport data do not support the reported magnitude of the gap; the gap we extract is smaller and comparable to the calculated two-subband neutral gap. A benchmark calculation for the Laughlin state at ν=1/3 in the same well provides an experimental test of the electrostatic treatment.

papers.title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(μ)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
papers.abstract: We study the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cramér--Lundberg model with claims having an Erlang distribution of shape parameter 2. We derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. Boundedness excludes the growing exponential term and yields a representation of the transform as a sum of two decaying exponentials. We construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain. For a model parameter set, we obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, the mean time of ruin, and higher moments, including the third moment at zero initial surplus. We prove analyticity in the discount rate and justify the resulting moment series. We consider the analytic continuation of the representation to negative discount rates separately. For Erlang claims with an arbitrary positive integer shape parameter, we establish a closed linear system and the asymptotics of the root continuing the zero root at zero discount.

papers.title: Recent Developments in HPR Methods for Large-Scale Convex Composite Quadratic Programming
papers.abstract: We present recent developments in Halpern Peaceman--Rachford (HPR) methods for solving large-scale convex composite quadratic programming problems. Within a unified HPR framework applied to the restricted Wolfe dual, we develop several algorithmic variants based on different choices of the semi-proximal operator $\mathcal{T}_1$ for the joint dual subproblem. Specifically, an sGS-based construction leads to a sequential $w$--$y$--$w$ update scheme, while a block-linearized construction eliminates cross-block coupling and enables parallel dual updates. To improve the latter, we further introduce a coupling-aware construction that exploits a second spectral moment to obtain a tighter row majorizer. We extend the framework to convex quadratically constrained quadratic programming through factor-based second-order cone reformulations. Additional computational enhancements include equality Gram scaling and asynchronous CPU polishing. We establish convergence results under fixed metrics and discuss practical adaptive strategies.

papers.title: Prior-Guided Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Fast 4D MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Background and purpose: We propose PGPI4MR (prior-guided, physics-informed 4D MRI reconstruction), a deep learning method that leverages information from other respiratory phases or a setup scan, the first 30 s of the same scan, to improve 4D MRI reconstruction without extra scan time. Materials and methods: PGPI4MR is an unrolled network that reconstructs 16 respiratory phases from 60, 30, or 15 s of data, and single 3D volumes, each from 0.29-0.49 s of data, using a setup-scan image. The networks were trained once, on other volunteers, and were not retrained for new volunteers. We evaluated PGPI4MR on measured k-space from three datasets: free-breathing MR-linac (1.5T) and abdominal (3T) scans, and thigh scans with cuff compression (1.5T). All methods, including comparative models, received identical samples and were scored similarly. Results: In vivo, PGPI4MR had the lowest held-out error for 4D MRI at every scan time, and its 16 phases were ready a median of 7.5-13 s after the scan on the 2 GPUs tested. Coupling the 16 respiratory phases reduced the error at 60 s by 9.1% compared with reconstructing each phase alone. For sub-second MRI, the error at 0.49 s was 15.5% lower than that of the best comparison method, classical reconstruction toward the same prior, and on the faster GPU, every 0.29 s window was acquired and reconstructed within 0.5 s. Without retraining, PGPI4MR matched the best methods on the 3T abdominal scans but not on the thigh scans; after retraining on thigh data, it reduced the held-out error by 6.6% relative to the best comparison method. Conclusion: Prior information allowed PGPI4MR to reconstruct 4D and sub-second MRI more accurately than compressed sensing and a published 4D network, within seconds and without extra scan time. This could support 4D MRI for treatment planning and 3D motion monitoring during MR-guided radiotherapy.

papers.title: Numerical Verification Limits of Asymmetric Intrastromal Hydrogel Reinforcement for Decentered Keratoconus
papers.abstract: Spatially tailored intrastromal hydrogel scaffolds have been proposed for decentered keratoconus, but their mechanical and optical benefits require stringent numerical validation. We reanalyze conforming two-material finite-element benchmarks and earlier optomechanical screening calculations, distinguishing solver verification from constitutive adequacy and treatment efficacy. In a curved corneal-patch benchmark with a fixed-volume rectangular inclusion, the apparent peak-displacement benefit of an offset over a centered inclusion changes from -5.66% to +1.73% across four tetrahedral meshes, while absolute displacements remain strongly mesh dependent. On the finest mesh, the quadratic term in the Green-Lagrange strain tensor contributes about 18% of the root-mean-square magnitude of the linearized strain; the underlying finite-element solutions themselves remain linear elastic. Earlier optical screening was sensitive to corneal orientation, mesh refinement and wavefront-reference conventions and is not retained as validated evidence. These observations do not establish superiority of asymmetric reinforcement. Instead, they motivate prespecified criteria for geometry-invariant finite-strain simulations, two-material interface verification, optical wavefront convergence, and independent experimental validation. No clinical recommendation is implied.

papers.title: Tensor Contraction with ZX Calculus, a Graph-Theoretic Approach
papers.abstract: Tensors are higher dimensional generalisations of vectors and matrices. Tensor networks are a diagrammatic representation of complicated relations between tensors, and tensor contraction is the evaluation of a tensor network analogous to matrix multiplication. Tensor networks and tensor contraction are ubiquitous in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics. Most existing tensor contraction algorithms are focused on finding an optimal contraction order of the tensors' bonds. However, finding the optimal order is an NP-hard problem. It is equivalent to another possibly more straightforward but still NP-hard problem of finding the treewidth of the line graph of the tensor network. While in general finding the optimal bond-by-bond contraction order is hard, in many practical cases there is no need to find an optimal order. This observation leads to the core innovation of this thesis, which is a new tensor contraction paradigm that uses graph theoretic operations to produce an equivalent tensor network whose line graph has lower treewidth than the original tensor network, before applying the bond-by-bond contraction algorithm. We call these graph theoretical operations \textit{rewrite preprocessing}, and we name the algorithms that apply rewrite preprocessing before regular bond-by-bond contraction \textit{Tensor Contraction with Graph Operation}. There are many possible ways to perform rewrite preprocessing; in this thesis, we focus on the graph operations of ZX calculus, a diagrammatic language for quantum circuits. Ample numerical simulations have been performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

papers.title: Interface Quilt: Modifying Applications with Computer Use Agents and Generative UI
papers.abstract: Modifying an existing application is difficult when it does not provide programmatic access for that change. Recent advances in computer-use agents (CUAs) enable richer understanding and operation of existing interfaces, while generative UI (GenUI) makes it practical to generate new ones. We examine how these advances expand software modification through a design space of what can be changed and a framework for how modifications can be implemented. We then introduce Interface Quilt, a system that combines CUAs and GenUI to generate interface patches, which are new interfaces displayed over an existing application to modify its presentation, interaction, and capabilities. Through demonstrations across a variety of applications, we show that interface patches support a range of modifications without source code, APIs, or accessibility data.

papers.title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
papers.abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.

papers.title: Rethinking Model Aggregation for Federated Learning with Domain Skew: A Knowledge-Preserving Perspective
papers.abstract: Domain skew challenges federated learning by requiring a shared model to accommodate distinct visual distributions. Domain-specific experts can capture these distributions separately, creating an opportunity to integrate their representations in a unified predictor. We propose Federated Knowledge-Preserving Learning (FKPL), a two-stage framework that combines domain-oriented expert training with prototype-based classifier calibration. First, a one-shot subspace-based clustering procedure groups clients for intra-cluster training. The resulting expert encoders are concatenated and frozen, preserving each learned feature mapping during global integration. Second, clients interpolate their concatenated features with class-matched domain prototypes and upload the resulting virtual features. The server trains a global linear classifier on these features, concentrating classifier optimization at the server after a single feature upload. FKPL achieves average accuracies of 73.01\%, 67.00\%, and 64.51\% on Office-Caltech-10, PACS, and a four-domain subset of DomainNet, respectively. On DomainNet, its cross-domain standard deviation is 7.50 percentage points, the lowest among the evaluated methods. With the same concatenated extractor, prototype-based calibration improves average accuracy over federated classifier training by 9.99 and 14.94 percentage points on Office-Caltech-10 and PACS. These results identify classifier calibration as an effective way to combine preserved domain representations into a global predictor.

papers.title: Well-posedness and Quantitative Stability for Degenerate Fokker--Planck Equations with Rough Coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative stability and well-posedness for degenerate Fokker--Planck equations with Sobolev-regular and possibly fully degenerate diffusion coefficient. For two classes of rough drifts, stability estimates imply uniqueness, and existence is proved under suitable conditions. First, for anisotropic drifts with partial fractional Sobolev regularity, we prove both existence (as probability densities, essential for the probabilistic interpretation via superposition) and quantitative stability without imposing any growth conditions, covering the full range of fractional exponents and extending previous Lagrangian-flow results. Second, for drifts whose distributional gradients are given by singular integrals (e.g., Biot--Savart velocity fields from $L^1$ vorticity), we obtain stability estimates that allow the diffusion matrix to be time-space dependent and possibly degenerate, removing the prior restrictions of identity diffusion or bounded coefficients. Our results also recover the pure transport regime as a limiting case.

papers.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
papers.abstract: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. We show that this asymptotic order is attained: for every $d\ge 2$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that, for every positive integer $t$ and every prescribed length $L\ge C_dt^{d-1}$, there is a simple spherical $t$-design curve of length $L$. This establishes the analogue for curves of the theorem of Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska, which resolved the Korevaar-Meyers conjecture for spherical design points. More generally, we prove the corresponding result on closed, connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d\ge 2$, where eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator substitute for polynomials. The proof combines a geometric construction of curves with continuously adjustable local lengths and an application of Brouwer's degree theorem.

papers.title: The Brin-Katok local entropy formula for non-compact random dynamical systems and an application
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for $C^1$ random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for $C^2$ random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. Furthermore, we also construct a counterexample showing that the integrability condition above cannot in general be omitted.

papers.title: Evolutionary characterization of whole-genome doubling across human cancers
papers.abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) is common across human cancers and is associated with tumour progression and adverse clinical outcomes. However, how genome-doubled tumours evolve across diverse cancer types remains poorly understood. Here we characterize WGD-associated tumour evolution by integrating genomic analyses of 41,332 tumours from 12 cancer types with evolutionary timing and multi-omic data. Several canonical driver mutations generally preceded WGD when both occurred, as did the onset of homologous recombination deficiency-associated mutagenesis. Notably, post-WGD chromosome-arm losses showed substantially weaker cancer-type dependence than pre-WGD losses, with 61-75% less variance explained by cancer type. Beyond chromosomal evolution, WGD+ tumours showed reduced interferon-response and HLA antigen-presentation programmes linked to epigenetic remodelling, without disproportionate enrichment of genetic immune-escape alterations. Our findings highlight WGD as a recurrent evolutionary transition associated with altered chromosomal evolution and epigenetically linked immune adaptation across cancers.

papers.title: Robust Remote ECG Monitoring under Energy Constraints: Anomaly Filtering versus Predictive Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Machine learning for remote electrocardiogram monitoring must handle noise and diseases absent from training under tight resource constraints. We investigate whether upstream unsupervised anomaly detection can improve monitoring decisions more efficiently than classifier-derived uncertainty. We evaluate five detectors on PTB-XL and BUT QDB and compare a two-stage filter-classifier system with Monte Carlo Dropout and deep ensembles under unseen-disease and noise conditions. Performance is averaged over five training seeds. We measure single-pass energy, latency, and graph memory on a microcontroller's central processing unit (CPU) and neural processing unit (NPU). Per-score neural network costs account for repeated evaluations but exclude scoring outside deployed graphs. Energy equations relate filtering and rejection to avoided classifier execution. Across four disease scenarios, Deep Support Vector Data Description (Deep SVDD) achieves the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve within all tested finite CPU energy budgets. On the NPU, it leads at 1 mJ, while Monte Carlo Dropout has slightly higher means at 10 and 100 mJ. With a narrow CPU classifier, the Deep SVDD two-stage system increases the fraction of correctly classified or correctly rejected inputs by 15.0-19.4 percentage points over classification without rejection. Estimated energy per input is 1.93-6.99 mJ, compared with 52.53 mJ for Monte Carlo Dropout and 8.76-17.51 mJ for deep ensembles, at each method's retrospectively selected test accuracy peak. These results support upstream filtering for efficient remote monitoring, while independent validation and complete-system measurements remain necessary.

papers.title: Disorder, Interactions, and the Fate of the Two-Dimensional Electron System: Wigner Crystal, Metal-Insulator Transition, and Amorphous Solid
papers.abstract: We present a unified theoretical study of the interplay between Coulomb disorder and Coulomb interactions in two-dimensional electron systems, covering the Wigner crystallization transition, the metal-insulator transition, and the crossover from a Wigner crystal to an amorphous localized solid in both zero magnetic field and the lowest Landau level. Using Hartree-Fock theory, variational Monte Carlo, and percolation and strong-localization arguments, we show that quenched charged disorder destroys true long-range Wigner crystalline order in the thermodynamic limit at any nonzero charged-impurity density, within the Imry-Ma-Larkin framework; the finite-system density image is that of an amorphous solid with crystalline coherence over at most a few lattice spacings. For the two-dimensional metal-insulator transition we show, in a controlled nonlinear-Thomas-Fermi model of long-range Coulomb disorder at setback d, that the half-depletion density of the semiclassical landscape and the Ioffe-Regel-Mott density of Born-RPA transport track each other to within a factor of order unity over the physically relevant range of impurity density and setback, with a slow n_i^(-1/10) d^(-1/5) spread; the agreement reflects the common energy scale E_dis ~ E_F at the transition rather than a theorem, and modest independent short-range transport channels can shift the ratio by factors of order two. The article is a theoretical study under well-defined approximations; it takes the recent scanning tunneling microscopy imaging experiments on two-dimensional electron systems and the longstanding disorder-versus-interaction debate on the two-dimensional metal-insulator transition as motivation, and leaves to the reader the comparison between its calculated signatures and the published experimental analyses.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Robustness in Fine-tuned Models
papers.abstract: Our study systematically evaluates the robustness of fine-tuned pre-trained models across different datasets and attack types, aiming to provide insights for researchers in selecting pre-trained models for image classification tasks while prioritizing robustness against potential attacks. Our work explores the influence of fine-tuning pre-trained models with different datasets and attack types on their robustness and overview of the appropriate pre-trained model for image classification based on factors such as computation resources, memory usage, and accuracy on clean data. We fine-tune the models with weights. Evaluate the models on data before any attack and after different attack cases. The study utilizes publicly available image datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and SVHN to assess the robustness of pre-trained models. The results indicate that the robustness of fine-tuned models varies across different data distributions and sample sizes, emphasizing the need for tailored selection based on specific task requirements. The findings also highlight the varying performance of ResNet50, DenseNet, and MobileNet in defending against attacks on different datasets. Overall, this research provides valuable insights into the robustness of fine-tuned pre-trained models and their suitability for real-world applications in image classification.

papers.title: Pore-scale mechanisms of capillary imbibition in cement-based materials revealed by direct numerical simulations in a realistic FIB-SEM microstructure
papers.abstract: Moisture transport in cement-based materials involves transient multiphase flow through highly irregular pore networks, where evolving air--water interfaces strongly influence liquid invasion and gas displacement. Here, pore-resolved, image-based direct numerical simulations (DNS) are used to investigate spontaneous imbibition in a FIB--SEM-reconstructed cementitious microstructure, resolving air--water interface dynamics at nanometre-to-micrometre spatial scales and nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. As these dynamics remain inaccessible to direct experimental observation at such scales, the simulations provide, to the best of our knowledge, the first direct view of transient imbibition within the capillary porosity of a realistic cementitious microstructure. The three-dimensional simulations reveal highly heterogeneous wetting-front propagation, continuous interface reconfiguration, and progressive air entrapment, showing that local dynamics depend on evolving interface curvature and capillary-pressure fields rather than on characteristic pore size alone. Significant air entrapment develops even within the capillary pores and under perfectly water-wetting conditions, progressively reducing the saturation rate, while the capillary pressure of trapped-air clusters depends strongly on local interface geometry rather than gas volume alone. Controlled two-dimensional analyses show that the balance between capillary, viscous, inertial, and gravitational effects is strongly scale-dependent. Comparison with the three-dimensional simulations highlights the importance of out-of-plane interface curvature and pore-network connectivity. The framework also resolves moisture conditions at the steel--concrete interface, illustrating its potential for corrosion-relevant pore-scale analysis.

papers.title: Training-Free Motion-Corrected 3D Brain MRI Reconstruction via Event-Guided References
papers.abstract: Head motion causes artefacts in 3D brain MRI and can bias structural measurements. Model-based correction alternates between image and motion estimation, but artefacts in the reconstructed reference can reinforce motion errors. Learned priors can reduce these artefacts but require pretraining and may add test-time computation. We propose EventMC (event-guided motion correction), a training-free method for interleaved Cartesian acquisitions. It iteratively detects motion events and estimates motion using reference images reconstructed from stable intervals. It then refines the image and motion from low to high spatial frequencies. In a fair comparison in simulation (same reconstruction), EventMC's motion estimates improve mean PSNR by up to 4.0 dB over those of the learning-based MotionTTT. A single run of EventMC is up to 7.5 times faster than MotionTTT with less than half the GPU memory. On in vivo motion-corrupted scans, EventMC achieves similar mean image quality to MotionTTT without any training. Code is available at https://github.com/bayesbreeze/EventMC.

papers.title: Federated Estimation of Loading Spaces in Tensor Factor Models under Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Tensor factor models provide low-dimensional representations of tensor-valued observations while preserving their multiway structure. When these observations are held by different clients, privacy constraints may prevent them from being pooled for centralized analysis. We study estimation of common loading spaces in Tucker tensor factor models under federated differential privacy, allowing heterogeneous sample sizes, privacy budgets, and factor strengths. The proposed method combines private stability testing, Huber aggregation, and Gaussian perturbation at each client with weighted aggregation at the server. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds governed by a scaled harmonic mean of the squared local error rates, and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors under strong factors, fixed factor ranks, and fixed noise variance. We further develop a private calibration procedure that selects the local tuning parameters and aggregation weights without knowledge of the noise level or client-specific factor strengths. The resulting adaptive estimator preserves the privacy guarantee and attains the error rate obtained with oracle tuning. We illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators through simulation experiments and an application to a Meditation Traits EEG dataset.

papers.title: Superscalar Loop Processors
papers.abstract: To sustain the computational demands of modern ML and HPC workloads, programmable accelerators integrate large arrays of processing elements (PEs), typically built around single-issue in-order cores to maximize integration density and energy efficiency. As a result, each PE's instruction throughput is upper-bounded at one instruction per cycle (IPC), often suffering from significant underutilization of its functional units (FUs). Conventional superscalar processors can improve FU utilization by increasing IPC, but they typically incur substantial area and energy overheads. This work proposes the Superscalar Loop Processor (SLP) architecture, a lightweight approach to superscalar execution that targets regular, compute-intensive loop kernels. We present the SLP execution model, which exploits the static structure of these workloads to enable efficient multiple-issue execution without the complexity of dynamic out-of-order scheduling. We demonstrate the SLP architecture through an open-source prototype implementation, Schnizo, developed as an enhancement of a tiny RV32I core with floating-point support. Across several ML and HPC microkernels, Schnizo achieves substantially higher IPC and FPU utilization than the scalar baseline while retaining the efficiency of lightweight in-order designs. These results demonstrate that SLPs can provide an efficient architectural solution for programmable accelerators targeting regular, compute-intensive workloads.

papers.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
papers.abstract: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs. Two ingredients are new. The published class of 7,077 lines is grown to 7,193 by local search in three stages, as a sequence of exchanges between candidate lines and class lines; and the point count, which equals 52,416,000 + 2S + 2t with t the number of antipodal pairs and S the size of the union of t isometric images of the class, is maximised as a maximum-coverage problem by greedy search with iterated local search over pools of 4,000 automorphic images, reaching 92-100% of the trivial bound 7,193t. All results are verified in exact integer arithmetic, and the certificates are distributed with the code. Code and data: https://github.com/dimkadimon/KissingNumbers

papers.title: Online Active Learning Architecture for Safety-Critical Control Systems
papers.abstract: The transition of information-centric artificial intelligence to safety-critical applications is impeded by the limitations of conventional offline-training paradigms in open-world environments. This paper presents Control AI, an architecture for Online Active Learning (OAL) inspired by the continuous Prediction-Evaluation-Correction process of biological intelligence. The framework combines the hierarchical representation capacity of deep neural networks with the real-time error-feedback adaptation of adaptive control. A prediction model maps sensory input into a latent manifold, an optional latent model represents transitions in that space, and a reconstruction model maps the latent state back to observable signals. Residuals between predictions and measurements provide the internal learning signal. Spatial and temporal cross-reconstruction architectures prevent OAL from collapsing to a trivial identity mapping, while coupled, dual, and localized variants shorten error-transmission paths. Localized predictive coding style OAL is implemented through guidance-backpropagation and target-backpropagation architectures, and hybrid and scaled variants support high-dimensional deployment. The paper focuses on the architectural rationale and the progression from a conceptual feedback loop to practical large-scale configurations.

papers.title: Does reflective LLM feedback survive a wet-lab-scale label budget?
papers.abstract: Can reflective language-model feedback improve a biological predictor when each cycle buys only one plate of labels? We separate three possible sources of benefit: proposing model edits, choosing measurements, and revising decisions through repeated feedback. We replay $36$ ProteinGym assays, starting with $96$ labels and acquiring $96$ per round for six rounds, with a sealed test set and a shared edit schema. The pre-specified comparison of full LLM control against random edits detects no advantage in test rank correlation ($Δz=-0.008$, $95\%$ CI $[-0.034,+0.018]$); equivalence is also unestablished. Exploratory ablations nevertheless identify useful model editing. With random acquisition fixed, LLM edits improve Fisher-transformed test Spearman by $0.043$ over no edits; with acquisition fixed to upper confidence bound, they improve normalized top-variant recovery by $0.023$. LLM acquisition alone does not detectably outperform fixed adaptive rules, and repeated feedback does not detectably outperform one initial recommendation under full control. Thus, the observed gains support constrained specialist editing, while the incremental value of recursive reflection remains unestablished at this label budget.

papers.title: Who Asks, Who Answers: Linear Attention Builds the Query in Hybrid Language Models
papers.abstract: Hybrid language models interleave linear-attention layers with a small number of softmax-attention layers. Prior work largely attributes in-context retrieval to softmax attention, treating linear attention primarily as a mechanism for compressing past context. We revisit this division of labor and show that linear attention plays a direct role in retrieval by constructing the query used by softmax attention. Studying Qwen3.5 (Gated DeltaNet) and Granite4.0 (Mamba-2), we identify an Encode--Address circuit. An early Encode block preserves token identity, while an Address block constructs the final-position representation from which a softmax \emph{reader} forms its attention query. Transplanting this representation between prompts with different queried keys redirects retrieval in 0.97--0.99 of cases. The Address block's recurrent state carries the retrieval target, and its computation transfers across architectures: replacing Granite's Address block with Qwen's restores retrieval accuracy to 0.92--0.94 without updating either model's weights. Across six Qwen3.5 models, Address computation becomes distributed at larger scales over a chain of blocks, each guiding a successive reader, as the query no longer passes from one reader to the next through attention. These findings reveal a division of labor in hybrid retrieval: linear attention constructs the query, while softmax attention performs the lookup. Code is available at https://github.com/yuang-chen/LinearQuery

papers.title: EAGR: Evidence-Guided Adaptive Graph Retrieval
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for multi-hop reasoning requires retrieval to adapt as intermediate evidence reveals new information needs. Existing approaches support such retrieval through explicit graph structures or iterative query reformulation, introducing graph-construction or query-time overhead. We present Evidence-Guided Adaptive Graph Retrieval (EAGR), a framework in which accumulated evidence dynamically determines which semantic directions to explore next, and which requires no dedicated graph database and no explicit graph materialization. EAGR operates over an implicit semantic graph induced by compact passage metadata pre-ingested into a standard VectorDB. Starting from dense-retrieval seed passages, an LLM iteratively assesses accumulated evidence, identifies promising semantic directions, expands the retrieval frontier through metadata-based neighborhood lookup, and terminates once sufficient evidence has been collected. By precomputing semantic metadata, EAGR enables evidence-conditioned graph exploration without materializing an explicit graph, maintaining a dedicated GraphDB, or iteratively rewriting the query. Across three widely used multi-hop QA benchmarks, EAGR achieves the highest LLM-based answer accuracy among evaluated methods, outperforming the vanilla RAG by 17\% and strongest graph-aware baseline by 4\% percentage points averaged across three popular benchmarks HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue.

papers.title: Generalized Hamiltonian gradient flow of contact type II: singularities, cut locus, and controllability
papers.abstract: We study singularities, cut loci and controllability for time-dependent contact Hamilton--Jacobi equations. A contact version of Arnaud's theorem identifies the superdifferential graph of an evolved profile with the contact Hamiltonian image of the differential graph of its positive Lax--Oleinik regularization. This representation defines intrinsic singular characteristics and determines their initial velocity through a minimum-energy selection on the space-time superdifferential. The curves are continuous and locally $1/2$-Hölder, but they need not be locally Lipschitz. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal even for a quadratic Hamiltonian. The intrinsic characteristic issued from a cut point is singular at every later time in the short-time interval. We also establish the contact Lax--Oleinik commutator identities, which identify the superlevel and sublevel sets of the cut time with the corresponding terminal momentum graphs through bi-Lipschitz maps. For reachable terminal data we characterize the associated calibrated sets, and we describe all continuous initial data that reach a prescribed semiconcave profile. The proofs use Herglotz' variational principle and short-time estimates for contact fundamental solutions.

papers.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
papers.abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

papers.title: SurgQ-VLM: Question-Conditioned Dual-Stream Compression and Answer-Type-Aware Reinforcement for Surgical Video Question Answering
papers.abstract: Reasoning about surgical video -- which phase is underway, which instruments act, and when events occur -- underpins operative documentation, workflow analysis, and skill assessment. Yet surgical visual question answering is still largely built on single frames and closed labels that cannot express a duration, an ordering, or a count, and the video models that lift the frame limit typically compress every clip the same way regardless of the question, discarding the temporal evidence the answer needs. Worse, the answers are structurally heterogeneous, spanning five incompatible structures -- binary, classification, multi-label, counting, and sentence-temporal -- that no single training signal scores uniformly well. We propose SurgQ-VLM, a two-stage model for surgical video question answering. Stage 1 trains a question-conditioned dual-stream (slow/fast) compressor for a LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-VL-7B: cross-attention conditions both streams on the question, and each clip's visual tokens shrink 49x from the raw ViT patches (11x vs. post-merge backbone tokens). Stage 2 post-trains with GRPO under an answer-type-aware reward that scores each question on the metric matching its answer structure (micro-F1 for label sets, normalised error for counts, a content-timing blend for temporal windows). On a sealed 21,840-question test split over Cholec80 and CholecT50, SurgQ-VLM reaches 0.779 keyword accuracy and a 10x BLEU-4 gain over zero-shot; GRPO adds 2.5 pp K-Acc (2.0 pp attributable to the answer-type-aware reward), concentrated in the structurally hard types, with answer format unchanged (ROUGE-L). Code is available at https://github.com/DhruvMakwana/SurgQ-VLM.

papers.title: Machine Learning Beyond Statistical Consistency for Hybrid AI
papers.abstract: We propose a new definition of machine learning, according to which a machine learns a function when it computes the function successfully, that is, when the value it returns for each input has a proper derivation in a formal system. We extend Gödel's Representability Theorem, which equates computation with derivation, to empirical targets in two ways: the theorem is extended to the computable reals, and the data are admitted into the system as empirical definitions that record what has been observed. We prove that a machine learns a true probability if and only if two conditions are met. The Truth Condition is that its estimate converges to the true probability, which is statistical consistency. The Assurance Condition is that the machine properly derives its own convergence inside the system. Learning thus lies beyond statistical consistency, for it requires a derivation of the convergence from the record. A global assumption about the data, such as the i.i.d. assumption, does not supply such a derivation, because it leads only to a circular one, as we show for PAC learning. On the other hand, the two conditions are met for the probability of a sentence over a finite ideal corpus. A real machine can approximate a true probability only if an ideal machine can learn it precisely, that is, only in a domain that meets the two conditions. Modern AI works in such a domain, and we offer this as a clue to its success. Modern AI is hybrid as well, in two senses: First, it performs two kinds of tasks, namely probabilistic ones such as predicting the next word and deductive ones such as proving and coding. Second, it combines two parts of different kinds, a statistical proposer and a deductive verifier, for proving and coding. Our framework explains both senses of hybridity in one formal system.

papers.title: Quadratic bounds for intersecting hypergraphs: An affirmative answer to a question of Duke and Erdős
papers.abstract: Let $m(k,b)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an intersecting $k$-uniform hypergraph in which every $(k-1)$-set of vertices is disjoint from at least $b$ edges, with $m(k,b)=+\infty$ if no such hypergraph exists. Duke and Erdős [Congressus Numerantium (1980)] asked whether $m(k,k)=o(k^4)$ is possible. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively and determine the order of growth of $m(k,k)$ by proving that $k^2+1\leq m(k,k)\leq Ck^2$ for all sufficiently large $k$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. More generally, we show that $m(k,b)=Θ(kb)$ for all sufficiently large odd $k$ and every integer $b$ with $k\leq b\leq (k-1)(k-3)/2$, where the implied constants are independent of $k$ and $b$.

papers.title: On closed symmetric monoidal enriched $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: We show that a closed symmetric monoidal V-enriched $\infty$-category can be described by a lax symmetric monoidal functor to V from its underlying $\infty$-category.

papers.title: Light Ring Stability Across Spacetime Dimensions and Theories of Gravity
papers.abstract: The light ring theorem states that four-dimensional stationary, axisymmetric, horizonless ultracompact objects (UCOs) possess light rings (LRs) in pairs, one of which is stable if the Null Energy Condition (NEC) holds in General Relativity (GR). The existence of a stable LR may trigger nonlinear spacetime instabilities, thereby raising questions about the viability of UCOs as long-lived black hole mimickers. We extend the LR existence and stability theorem beyond four-dimensional GR to modified gravity theories, in particular, $f(R)$ gravity, scalar-tensor theories, and restricted Horndeski gravity, in ($d \geq 4$) dimensional spacetimes. Our findings show that in four-dimensional modified gravities, the stability of LRs is governed by theory-specific coupling parameters in addition to the NEC. Consequently, a stable LR is not guaranteed to occur in certain parameter regimes. In higher dimensions ($d>4$), we confirm using topological arguments that LRs still emerge in pairs; however, the topological charges are now associated with four distinct types of LRs, including two types of saddle points. The stability analysis further constrains the allowed LR pairings, implying that, unlike in four-dimensional GR, the emergent pair does not necessarily include a stable LR. These findings directly impact tests of GR using UCOs, demonstrating that LR stability is highly sensitive to both the underlying gravitational theory and spacetime dimensionality.

papers.title: AgenticMobility: An Open-Source Platform for Multi-AI-Agent Mobility Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time. We present AgenticMobility, an open-source experimental platform for studying how mobility AI agents and other AI agents interact, adapt through repeated experience, and collectively shape mobility outcomes. Persistent agents retain identities and relevant states across rounds, with explicit interfaces defining information access, admissible actions, and decision schedules; linked records trace decisions, execution, and feedback. In the current implementation, large language model (LLM) agents act as travelers choosing routes and departure times and as a manager periodically adjusting link charges within MATSim. A preliminary demonstration spans 100 simulated days in each of five configurations, with one run per configuration and a shared simulation seed. In the joint traveler--manager run, all 1,179,300 finalized target decisions satisfied action constraints; execution checks verified implementation of accepted choices and preservation of personal memories across days. Trajectories show stable route choices alongside departure-time adjustments and differences between controlled-trip and population-wide outcomes. The platform supports experiments on individual adaptation, collective outcomes, and management interventions by varying information access, retained experience, and management feedback. Source code is available at https://github.com/Agentic-City-Research/Agentic-Mobility

papers.title: Alternating Sums in Compositions
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent asymptotic formula for the moment of the alternating sum of parts in partitions by Craig and Li, we study the moment of the alternating sum of parts in compositions. We establish closed formulas for this moment using techniques involving generating functions, matrix diagonalization, Krawtchouk polynomials, differential equations, and Faà di Bruno's formula. Our result is connected with some known integer sequences in the OEIS and admits a combinatorial interpretation by coin flipping.

papers.title: Multiplicative Weights for Mixed Block Constraints and Maximum Multicommodity Flow
papers.abstract: We study multiplicative-weights (MWU) algorithms for block-separable feasibility problems containing both packing and covering constraints. Each iteration optimizes a weighted linear objective over one block, either chosen uniformly at random or visited in a fixed cyclic order. We show that the cyclic algorithm returns an $O(\varepsilon)$-approximate solution after $O(kρ\varepsilon^{-2}\log m)$ oracle calls where $k$ is the number of blocks and $ρ$ is the width of the oracle. The same holds for the randomized version with high probability. Previously, such bounds were shown when the coupling constraints have the same sign [Radzik'95; Villavicencio-Grigoriadis'96]. These analyses critically depended on monotonicity arguments that are not available in the mixed case. As an application, we obtain a deterministic $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for maximum multicommodity flow (M-MCF) using $O(k\varepsilon^{-2}\log m\log(km/\varepsilon))$ approximate single-commodity min-cost-flow calls. For planar graphs, and more generally for graph families admitting a near-linear-time min-cost-flow algorithm, this gives total running time $\widetilde O(km\varepsilon^{-2})$. Compared with the $O(km^{1+o(1)}\varepsilon^{-1})$ algorithm of [Chen-Graur-Sidford'25], this improves the dependence on $m$ for these graph families at the cost of a worse dependence on $\varepsilon$. Finally, we give an exponentiation-free finite-precision implementation of the cyclic algorithm. It represents each internal weight by a logarithmic-bit mantissa and exponent, while every price supplied to the block oracle is rational and has a polynomially bounded common denominator.

papers.title: Vision-language classification of Torsades de Pointes risk from pseudo-coloured ECG images: do T-wave morphology and colour context help or hinder?
papers.abstract: Contextual prompting is widely presented as a cheap route to better performance from vision models, but the evidence comes largely from benchmarks in which an attribute named in a prompt is also present in the image, confounding the two channels. We investigate the significance of context for a semantically complex biomedical signal classification task using a domain-adapted vision-language model, BiomedCLIP. Building on our previous work that renders electrocardiogram (ECG) signals as colour-enhanced images to flag Torsades de Pointes risk using the QT-nomogram and pseudo-colouring technique, we cross four context strategies with four T-wave morphology label sets, evaluated zero-shot and with a class-balanced linear probe, under five-fold stratified cross-validation on 9,789 images. Zero-shot inference is unusable. Once trained, the colour-enhanced images outperform the colourless ones on every metric: balanced accuracy 0.903 versus 0.825, sensitivity 0.914 versus 0.827, specificity 0.892 versus 0.823, ROC-AUC 0.955 versus 0.888 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) 0.437 versus 0.311. Crossing colour-in-image with colour-in-prompt separates the confounded channels: the image contributes +0.126 MCC (+0.078 balanced accuracy, +0.067 ROC-AUC) whether or not the prompt names colour, whereas naming it changes nothing under any metric. Context is two-sided: the best prompt set gains 0.008 MCC where colour is present and 0.016 where it is not, while the worst loses 0.017 and 0.013. For a signal rendered as an image, the leverage lies in how the signal is drawn rather than in how it is described - and where the endpoint is an interval measurement, prompts naming T-wave morphology describe the wrong quantity.

papers.title: Parameter-robust preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of Biot's equations
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze parameter-robust block preconditioners for a stabilized control-volume discretization of the quasi-static Biot equations. Beginning with a five-field formulation, we eliminate the poroelastic stress and time-scaled Darcy velocity through independent vertex-local solves, obtaining a symmetric cell-centered displacement--rotation--pressure system. A macrocell rotation-jump term stabilizes the weak-symmetry constraint. We prove the well-posedness of the fully discrete scheme and show that the condensed, coupled displacement--rotation mechanics block is uniformly spectrally equivalent to its block-diagonal counterpart. For uncoupled preconditioners, we derive an exact discrete pressure-control criterion and a sufficient parameter condition that accommodates the scaling \(c_0\asymp K_{\rm dr}^{-1}\), thereby allowing the storage coefficient to vanish in the nearly incompressible limit. We then construct a Schur-consistent pressure block that approximates the mechanics-induced pressure correction and prove its uniform equivalence to the exact pressure Schur complement. These results yield parameter-independent spectral bounds for block-diagonal preconditioning and weighted field-of-values estimates for lower-triangular preconditioning. Practical realizations employ a macrocell mass-matrix approximation for the stabilized rotation block and tailored two-grid solvers for the displacement and pressure blocks. Numerical experiments verify the expected convergence behavior in two dimensions and demonstrate robust performance under mesh refinement and broad variations of the physical parameters in both two and three dimensions.

papers.title: Exact factorization of finite-range three-body matrix elements between Gaussian wave packets and its application to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$
papers.abstract: We introduce finite-range three-body interactions into the $β-γ$-constrained generator coordinate method of antisymmetrized molecular dynamics. These genuine operators give saturation without an additional prescription for the projection, but require $O(A^6)$ complex exponentials at every node of the projection grid. With the graph Laplacian of the ranges, as in spectral clustering widely used in machine learning, we factorize the exponential factor of a Gaussian three-body kernel exactly into pairwise tables of $O(A^2)$ exponentials. A cofactor expansion rewrites the remaining contraction as complex matrix-matrix products. For $^{12}C$, the factorization reduces the time of the kernels with the three-body term from $530$ to $24$ times that of the two-body kernels. We apply the method to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$ with the Volkov, Tohsaki F1, and Kanada-En'yo--Akaishi F3B interactions, restricting the intrinsic states to time-reversal-invariant ones. Without the three-body terms of F1 and F3B, $^{12}C$ collapses far below the three $α$ threshold, whereas with them the ground state lies close to its experimental position below the threshold. When we adjust the Majorana parameter to this position, the Hoyle state lies within 0.6 MeV of experiment for all three interactions.

papers.title: Experimental Realization of Higher-order Topological Water Wave Crystal
papers.abstract: Free-surface water waves provide a macroscopic platform in which topological localization can be measured through surface-elevation fields. Higher-order topological phases offer a route to localizing wave modes at structural corners, yet their experimental realization in water-wave systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a water-wave higher-order topological crystal, where surface waves are confined to structural corners and spectrally identified through measured free-surface responses. Bulk band analysis and finite-system simulations predict topological edge and corner states in the designed structure, while frequency-resolved surface-elevation measurements confirm the corresponding localized modes. The measured spectra and field distributions reveal pronounced in-gap corner localization consistent with the predicted higher-order topological modes. These results establish surface water waves as a directly measurable platform for higher-order topological physics, enabling spatial localization and spectral characterization of hydrodynamic wave modes.

papers.title: Global existence and decay estimates of solutions for the compressible Prandtl type equations in Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the global existence and large-time decay of solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces. We study small perturbations around a monotone shear flow and establish global weighted Sobolev estimates together with precise time-decay rates for the solutions. The main difficulties are that the normal velocity causes a loss of one tangential derivative, the variable density gives rise to nonstandard boundary and shear-flow coupling terms, and the global-in-time argument requires sufficiently strong decay to close the time-weighted energy estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we combine the cancellation method introduced by Masmoudi and Wong~\cite{MW2015} with the good-quantity approach developed by Paicu and Zhang~\cite{PZ2021}, together with weighted shear-flow estimates and a careful treatment of the natural boundary structure. Under suitable assumptions on the density perturbation, the shear flow, and the function $f(t)$ describing the outer tangential flow, we prove the global-in-time well-posedness of solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this sense, the present result may be viewed as a Sobolev-space counterpart of the recent analytic-framework result obtained by Chen, Huang and Li (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024), 110322)~\cite{CHL2024} for the two-dimensional compressible Prandtl-type equations, while requiring a weaker time-decay assumption on the density perturbation.

papers.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
papers.abstract: LLM-based agentic systems are increasingly combined with CoT reasoning to solve tasks that require accurate reasoning, external knowledge, and multi-step deliberation. Yet, explicit CoT incurs substantial generation overhead, while implicit CoT, which replaces textual rationales with compact continuous tokens, does not naturally support the explicit communication interface required for agentic tool-use. We propose TAC-CoT, a tool-empowered adaptive implicit CoT framework that replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent reasoning segments while retaining textual tokens only for tool calls, observations, and final answers. This interleaved design enables agentic tool-use without verbalizing every intermediate reasoning step. Experiments on agentic math and QA benchmarks show that TAC-CoT improves accuracy by up to 8.8 points while reducing model forward passes by up to 6.8x. Furthermore, analyses show that TAC-CoT improves tool-use quality in both single- and multi-tool settings.

papers.title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks
papers.abstract: Long-horizon terminal tasks are used to evaluate and train agents. Human-curated datasets are scarce, so many synthesis methods have emerged. They usually measure the length of a task by the turns a model needs to pass it, and its difficulty by labels the LLM sets during generation. We find, however, that the turn count largely reflects the habits of the model, not only the demands of the task, and that the labels barely track how often models pass. We describe a terminal task by its work, the number of operations it requires, and its depth, the number of turns that must happen in sequence because the commands of each turn can only be chosen after reading the output of the previous one. Estimating depth as the smallest turn cap, stated to the agent, under which the task passes, we audit 734 tasks from six existing datasets. Synthesis has mostly added work, not depth: 94% of the solved synthetic tasks pass within three turns, yet depth, unlike the turn count, predicts difficulty beyond work. We propose DEPTH, in which a generation agent writes each task one segment at a time in a real software environment, carrying out each segment before writing it and starting the next from the state it leaves. Our 105 tasks exceed every audited dataset in depth and work, and none of six current models passes half of them. Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on runs from these tasks improves it on two terminal benchmarks.

papers.title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
papers.abstract: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.

papers.title: Watch Your Step: Adam's Margin Maximization Bias Depends on the Learning Rate Schedule
papers.abstract: We study the implicit bias of Adam and its similarity to sign gradient descent on homogeneous models in binary classification tasks. Perhaps surprisingly, we uncover that these depend on the learning rate schedule.
